subject: Physics
question_english: How do we describe the position of an object? When is an object said to be in motion or at rest?
question_hinglish: Kisi object ki position kaise batate hain? Object kab motion mein aur kab rest mein kehlaata hai?
answer_english: We first fix a reference point. The distance and direction of the object from the reference point at an instant describe its position at that instant. If the position with respect to the reference point changes with time, the object is in motion; if it does not change with time, the object is at rest. For motion in a straight line, positions to the right of the reference point are usually taken as positive and to the left as negative.
answer_hinglish: Pehle ek reference point tay karte hain. Kisi instant pe reference point se object ki doori aur disha us instant pe uski position batati hai. Agar reference point ke hisaab se position samay ke saath badle, toh object motion mein hai; agar na badle, toh rest mein hai. Seedhi line mein motion ke liye reference point ke daayein ki positions aam taur pe positive aur baayein ki negative maani jaati hain.
ncert_context: To describe the position of an object, we first need to specify a fixed point as the reference point. The distance and direction of the object with respect to the reference point, at any instant of time, describes the position of the object at that instant of time. If the position of the object with respect to the reference point changes with time, the object is said to be in motion. On the other hand, the object is said to be at rest if its position with respect to the reference point does not change with time. For the object moving in a straight line, the object can move only in one of the two directions — forward and backward. The direction is represented by plus (+) and minus (–) signs. Positions to the right of the reference point O are generally taken as positive, and to the left of O as negative.

subject: Physics
question_english: A student says, 'The Earth moves around the Sun.' Can an object kept on the Earth be considered at rest?
question_hinglish: Ek student kehta hai, 'Dharti Sooraj ke chaaron or ghoomti hai.' Kya Dharti pe rakhi cheez ko rest mein maana ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Rest and motion depend on the reference point. An object kept on the Earth does not change its position with respect to a reference point on the Earth, so it is at rest relative to the Earth. But with the Sun as the reference point, its position keeps changing as the Earth moves, so it is in motion relative to the Sun.

Par Sooraj ko reference point maanne pe Dharti ke chalne se uski position badalti rehti hai, isliye woh Sooraj ke saapeksh motion mein hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is the difference between distance travelled and displacement? Explain with an example.
question_hinglish: Tay ki gayi doori (distance) aur displacement mein kya fark hai? Example se samjhao.
answer_english: Distance travelled is the total length of the path covered and needs only a numerical value. Displacement is the net change in position between two instants; it has a magnitude (the distance between the two positions) and a direction (from the first position towards the second). Both have the SI unit metre. For example, an athlete runs from O to A (100 m) and back 60 m to B: distance travelled = 160 m, but displacement = OB = 40 m in the positive direction.
answer_hinglish: Distance tay kiye gaye raaste ki kul lambaai hai aur isme sirf sankhya chahiye. Displacement do instants ke beech position ka kul badlav hai; iska magnitude (dono positions ke beech ki doori) aur disha (pehli position se doosri ki taraf) hoti hai. Dono ki SI unit metre hai. Jaise ek athlete O se A (100 m) tak daudkar 60 m waapas B pe aaye: distance = 160 m, par displacement = OB = 40 m positive disha mein.
ncert_context: Suppose an athlete starts running from point O at time t = 0 s, reaches point B at t = 4 s, then reaches point A at t = 10 s, then runs back along the same path till point B reaching there at t = 16 s. The total distance travelled is OA + AB = 100 m + 60 m = 160 m. The distance between the starting and the stopping positions is OB = 40 m. Displacement is the net change in the position of an object between the two given instants of time. A complete description of displacement requires specifying both a direction and its numerical value (with units), called its magnitude. The magnitude of displacement is the distance between the object's positions at the two instants. The direction of displacement is specified from the position at the first instant towards the position at the second instant. To describe the total distance travelled, only the numerical value is required. The SI unit for both is the metre (m).

question_english: When are distance travelled and the magnitude of displacement equal? Can displacement be greater than distance?
question_hinglish: Distance aur displacement ka magnitude kab barabar hote hain? Kya displacement distance se zyada ho sakta hai?
answer_english: For motion in a straight line, they are equal if the object moves in one direction without turning back. The magnitude of displacement can never be greater than the distance travelled; it is always less than or equal to it, and it can even be zero when the object returns to its starting point.

subject: Physics
question_english: A father walks 250 m to a shop on a straight road, returns home to fetch a bag, goes to the shop again and comes back home. Find the total distance travelled and his displacement from home.
question_hinglish: Ek pita seedhi sadak pe 250 m door dukaan tak jaate hain, thaila lene ghar laut-te hain, phir dukaan jaate hain aur ghar waapas aate hain. Kul distance aur ghar se unka displacement nikaalo.
answer_english:
Given: Home to shop = 250 m
The trip is home → shop → home → shop → home, which is 4 stretches of 250 m.
Total distance = 4 × 250 m = 1000 m
He ends where he started, so displacement = 0 m.

subject: Physics
question_english: A student runs from the ground floor to the fourth floor, then comes down to the second floor. If each floor is 3 m high, find the total vertical distance travelled and the displacement.
question_hinglish: Ek student ground floor se chauthi manzil tak daudta hai, phir doosri manzil pe neeche aata hai. Har manzil 3 m oonchi ho toh kul vertical distance aur displacement nikaalo.
answer_english:
Ground to fourth floor = 4 × 3 m = 12 m up
Fourth to second floor = 2 × 3 m = 6 m down
Total vertical distance = 12 m + 6 m = 18 m
Displacement = position of second floor from ground = 2 × 3 m = 6 m upward

subject: Physics
question_english: What is the difference between uniform and non-uniform motion in a straight line?
question_hinglish: Seedhi line mein uniform aur non-uniform motion mein kya fark hai?
answer_english: In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, for all choices of intervals, so it moves at constant speed. In non-uniform motion, it travels unequal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed increases, decreases, or both; if the distances in successive intervals increase, its speed is increasing.
answer_hinglish: Uniform motion mein object barabar samay antaraalon mein barabar doori tay karta hai, har antaraal ke liye, isliye uski speed sthir rehti hai. ncert_context: If an object moving in a straight line travels equal distances in equal intervals of time (for all possible choices of time intervals), it is said to be in uniform motion in a straight line. In this case, the object moves with increasing speed or decreasing speed, or a combination of both. If the distances travelled in the successive intervals of times are increasing, its speed is increasing.

subject: Physics
question_english: Two postmen start 210 yojanas apart and walk towards each other, one covering 9 yojanas per day and the other 5. In how many days will they meet? (Ganitakaumudi problem)
question_hinglish: Do daakiye 210 yojana ki doori se ek-doosre ki taraf chalte hain, ek roz 9 yojana aur doosra 5 yojana. Kitne din mein milenge? (Ganitakaumudi ka sawaal)
answer_english:
Together they cover 9 + 5 = 14 yojanas per day.
Time to cover 210 yojanas = 210 ÷ 14 = 15 days
In 15 days, the first covers 9 × 15 = 135 yojanas and the second 5 × 15 = 75 yojanas, which add up to 210.
Answer: they meet after 15 days.

question_english: An object dropped from a height has velocities 0, 9.8, 19.6, 29.4 and 39.2 m/s at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 s. Find the average acceleration in each one-second interval. What is this acceleration called?

answer_english:
0–1 s: (9.8 − 0) ÷ 1 = 9.8 m/s²
1–2 s: (19.6 − 9.8) ÷ 1 = 9.8 m/s²
2–3 s: (29.4 − 19.6) ÷ 1 = 9.8 m/s²

subject: Physics
question_english: What is the difference between an instant of time and a time interval? What is instantaneous velocity?
question_hinglish: Samay ke instant aur samay antaraal mein kya fark hai? Instantaneous velocity kya hai?
answer_english: An instant of time is a single clock reading at a given point of time, while a time interval is the duration between two instants, that is, between two clock readings. Instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a particular instant: as the time interval around an instant is made smaller and smaller, the average velocity approaches a fixed value, which is the instantaneous velocity. A speedometer reading is nearly the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.
answer_hinglish: Samay ka instant kisi pal pe ghadi ki ek reading hai, jabki samay antaraal do instants, yaani ghadi ki do readings, ke beech ki avadhi hai. Instantaneous velocity kisi khaas instant pe velocity hai: jab instant ke aas-paas ka antaraal chhota aur chhota kiya jaata hai, average velocity ek tay maan ke paas pahunchti hai, wahi instantaneous velocity hai. Speedometer ki reading lagbhag instantaneous velocity ka magnitude hoti hai.
ncert_context: An instant of time and a time interval are not the same thing. An instant of time is a single reading of clock at a given point of time. Whereas, a time interval is the time duration between two instants of time, i.e., between two readings of a clock. What we simply called 'velocity at an instant' is known as 'instantaneous velocity'. As the time interval around an instant is made progressively smaller, the change in average velocity gets smaller and smaller. When the time interval becomes infinitesimally small, the average value of velocity approaches a fixed value called the instantaneous velocity. The reading of the speedometer of a vehicle is nearly (but not exactly) the same as the magnitude of the velocity at an instant.

question_english: On a straight-line position-time graph, a vehicle is at 40 m at 2 s and at 80 m at 4 s. Find its velocity from the slope.

subject: Physics
question_english: What do the slope and the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
question_hinglish: Velocity-time graph ka slope aur uske neeche ka area kya dikhaate hain?
answer_english: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration, since it is change in velocity ÷ change in time. A line parallel to the time axis has zero slope, meaning constant velocity and zero acceleration; an upward line means increasing velocity, and a downward line means decreasing velocity. The area enclosed between the graph and the time axis over an interval gives the displacement in that interval.
answer_hinglish: Velocity-time graph ka slope acceleration deta hai, kyunki yeh velocity ka badlav ÷ samay ka badlav hai. Time axis ke parallel line ka slope zero hai, yaani sthir velocity aur zero acceleration; upar jaati line ka matlab badhti velocity, aur neeche aati line ka matlab ghatti velocity. Kisi antaraal mein graph aur time axis ke beech ka area us antaraal ka displacement deta hai.
ncert_context: The velocity-time graph of an object in motion represents the change in its velocity with time. When the velocity of the car is constant, the velocity-time graph is a straight line parallel to the X-axis and acceleration is zero. A straight line velocity-time graph rising upward indicates that the velocity is increasing with a constant acceleration, whereas a falling straight line indicates that the velocity is decreasing with a constant acceleration. The slope of the line on velocity-time graph gives how fast the velocity is changing with time, i.e., the acceleration. The area enclosed by the velocity-time graph and the time axis for a desired time interval is equal to the displacement in that time interval.

subject: Physics
question_english: A car starts from rest and its velocity rises uniformly: 5 m/s at 10 s and 10 m/s at 20 s. Using the velocity-time graph, find its acceleration and its displacement between 10 s and 20 s.
question_hinglish: Ek car rest se chalti hai aur uski velocity ek samaan dar se badhti hai: 10 s pe 5 m/s aur 20 s pe 10 m/s. Velocity-time graph se uska acceleration aur 10 s se 20 s ke beech displacement nikaalo.
answer_english:
Acceleration = slope = (10 − 5) m/s ÷ (20 − 10) s = 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5 m/s²
Displacement = area under the graph from 10 s to 20 s (a trapezium)
= rectangle + triangle = (5 m/s × 10 s) + ½ × 10 s × 5 m/s
= 50 m + 25 m = 75 m

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the first kinematic equation, v = u + at.
question_hinglish: Pehla kinematic equation, v = u + at, derive karo.
answer_english:
For constant acceleration, the acceleration equals the average acceleration over any interval. Let the initial velocity be u at t = 0 and the final velocity v at time t. Then:
a = (v − u) ÷ (t − 0)
at = v − u
v = u + at
This gives the velocity at any time if u and a are known. Its velocity-time graph is a straight line whose slope is the acceleration.

at = v − u
v = u + at
Isse u aur a pata hone pe kisi bhi samay ki velocity mil jaati hai. Iska velocity-time graph seedhi line hai jiska slope acceleration hai.

This equation allows us to calculate velocity (v) at all times if initial velocity (u) and acceleration (a) are known. subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the second kinematic equation, s = ut + ½at², using the velocity-time graph.
question_hinglish: Velocity-time graph se doosra kinematic equation, s = ut + ½at², derive karo.
answer_english:
On the velocity-time graph, velocity rises from u at t = 0 to v at time t. Displacement s equals the area under the graph, which is a rectangle plus a triangle:
s = (u × t) + ½ × t × (v − u)
From the first equation, v − u = at. Substituting:
s = ut + ½ × t × at
s = ut + ½at²
answer_hinglish:
Velocity-time graph pe velocity t = 0 pe u se samay t pe v tak badhti hai. Displacement s graph ke neeche ke area ke barabar hai, jo ek rectangle aur ek triangle hai:
s = (u × t) + ½ × t × (v − u)
Pehle equation se v − u = at. Rakhne pe:
s = ut + ½ × t × at
s = ut + ½at²
ncert_context: The displacement s of the object during the time interval t is given by the area enclosed within OABD. Thus, s = area of OABD = area of the rectangle OACD + area of the triangle ABC = AO × DO + ½ × CA × BC. Substituting AO = u, DO = CA = t and BC = BD – CD = EO – AO = (v – u), we obtain s = ut + ½ t (v − u). Substituting the value of (v – u) from Eq. (4.4a), s = ut + ½ t (at), so s = ut + ½ at². These two equations (v = u + at and s = ut + ½at²) are the primary equations.

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the third kinematic equation, v² = u² + 2as.
question_hinglish: Teesra kinematic equation, v² = u² + 2as, derive karo.
answer_english:
From v = u + at, the time is t = (v − u) ÷ a. Substitute this into s = ut + ½at²:
s = u(v − u)/a + ½a(v − u)²/a²
2as = 2u(v − u) + (v − u)²
2as = (v − u)(2u + v − u) = (v − u)(v + u) = v² − u²
So v² = u² + 2as. This relates velocity and displacement without time.

subject: Physics
question_english: When can the kinematic equations be used? What do the signs of u, v, a and s mean?
question_hinglish: Kinematic equations kab use ho sakte hain? u, v, a aur s ke chinhon ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: The kinematic equations (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) are valid only when acceleration is constant, for motion in a straight line. For motion in one direction, distance equals the magnitude of displacement and speed equals the magnitude of velocity. For motion in both directions, the sign of u, v, a and s shows the direction of that quantity. The origin and positive direction can be chosen freely, but must not change during a problem.
answer_hinglish: Kinematic equations (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) sirf tab sahi hain jab acceleration sthir ho, seedhi line mein motion ke liye. Ek disha mein motion mein distance displacement ke magnitude ke barabar aur speed velocity ke magnitude ke barabar hoti hai. Dono dishaon mein motion mein u, v, a aur s ka chinh us maatra ki disha batata hai. Origin aur positive disha apni marzi se chun sakte hain, par sawaal ke beech badalni nahi chahiye.
ncert_context: These kinematic equations are valid only when the acceleration is constant. subject: Physics
question_english: Brakes give a car an acceleration of −4 m/s². Find the stopping distance if the car was moving at (i) 54 km/h and (ii) 108 km/h. What do you notice?
question_hinglish: Brakes car ko −4 m/s² ka acceleration dete hain. Agar car (i) 54 km/h aur (ii) 108 km/h se chal rahi ho toh rukne ki doori nikaalo. Tumhe kya dikhta hai?
answer_english:
Given: a = −4 m/s², v = 0. Using v² = u² + 2as, s = u² ÷ 8.
(i) u = 54 km/h = 15 m/s: s = 15² ÷ 8 = 225 ÷ 8 ≈ 28.1 m
(ii) u = 108 km/h = 30 m/s: s = 30² ÷ 8 = 900 ÷ 8 = 112.5 m
Doubling the speed makes the stopping distance four times longer, which is why a safe distance from the vehicle ahead must grow with speed.

question_english: A bus at 36 km/h sees an obstacle 30 m ahead. The driver takes 0.5 s to react, then brakes with an acceleration of −2.5 m/s². Will the bus stop before the obstacle?
question_hinglish: 36 km/h se chalti bus 30 m aage rukaavat dekhti hai. Driver ko react karne mein 0.5 s lagta hai, phir woh −2.5 m/s² ke acceleration se brake lagata hai. Kya bus rukaavat se pehle ruk jaayegi?
answer_english:
u = 36 km/h = 10 m/s
Distance during reaction time (constant velocity) = 10 m/s × 0.5 s = 5 m
Braking distance: v² = u² + 2as gives 0 = 10² + 2 × (−2.5) × s, so s = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 m
Total stopping distance = 5 m + 20 m = 25 m
Since 25 m < 30 m, the bus stops 5 m before the obstacle.

question_english: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 5 s, moves at 20 m/s for 10 s, then brakes uniformly to stop in 6 s. Find the total distance travelled.

answer_english:
Stage 1 (0 → 20 m/s in 5 s): s₁ = average velocity × t = (0 + 20)/2 × 5 = 50 m
Stage 2 (constant 20 m/s for 10 s): s₂ = 20 × 10 = 200 m
Stage 3 (20 → 0 m/s in 6 s): s₃ = (20 + 0)/2 × 6 = 60 m
Total distance = 50 + 200 + 60 = 310 m

subject: Physics
question_english: What factors affect the stopping distance of a vehicle? Why must we keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead?
question_hinglish: Gaadi ki rukne ki doori kin baaton pe nirbhar karti hai? Aage wali gaadi se surakshit doori kyun rakhni chahiye?
answer_english: After brakes are applied, a vehicle moves some distance before stopping. This distance depends on the vehicle's velocity when braking starts, the road surface (wet or dry), the braking capacity of the vehicle, and the driver's reaction time. Since stopping distance grows with the square of speed, a faster vehicle needs a much larger gap to avoid a collision. Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication technology, being developed in countries including India, can warn drivers of possible collisions.
answer_hinglish: Brake lagne ke baad gaadi rukne se pehle kuch doori chalti hai. Yeh doori brake lagaate waqt gaadi ki velocity, sadak ki satah (geeli ya sukhi), gaadi ki brake kshamta aur driver ke reaction samay pe nirbhar karti hai. Rukne ki doori speed ke square ke saath badhti hai, isliye tez gaadi ko takkar se bachne ke liye kaafi zyada faasla chahiye. India sameth kai deshon mein ban rahi vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) technology driver ko sambhavit takkar ki chetaavni de sakti hai.
ncert_context: When brakes are applied to a moving vehicle, it moves some distance before coming to a stop. The distance travelled depends upon the velocity of the vehicle when the brakes are applied, the road surface (wet/dry, etc.), the braking capacity of the vehicle (the negative acceleration caused by the brakes) as well as the driver's reaction time. Can you now understand why it is important to maintain a safe distance from the vehicle moving ahead of your vehicle and how this distance needs to be adjusted given your initial velocity? With a braking acceleration of –4 m/s², the stopping distance is 28.1 m at 54 km/h and 112.5 m at 108 km/h. There is a vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication technology, now being developed in many countries including India, which allows vehicles to exchange signals and warns drivers of possible collisions.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is uniform circular motion? Why is it called accelerated motion even though the speed is constant?
question_hinglish: Uniform circular motion kya hai? Speed sthir hone pe bhi ise accelerated motion kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: Uniform circular motion is motion along a circular path at constant speed. The speed stays the same at every point, but the direction of velocity, which is along the tangent to the circle, changes continuously. Since acceleration is non-zero whenever velocity changes in magnitude or direction, uniform circular motion is accelerated motion.
answer_hinglish: Uniform circular motion gol raaste pe sthir speed se chalna hai. Har point pe speed same rehti hai, par velocity ki disha, jo gole ki tangent ke saath hoti hai, lagaataar badalti rehti hai. Kyunki velocity ke magnitude ya disha badalne pe acceleration hota hai, uniform circular motion accelerated motion hai.
ncert_context: When an object moves in a circular path with constant (uniform) speed, its motion is called uniform circular motion. In case of uniform circular motion, the speed is constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously. As the number of sides of a track increases, the athlete has to take turns more and more frequently. Finally, the track approaches a circle, and the direction of athlete's velocity changes continuously. Acceleration is non-zero if the velocity of an object changes. The velocity changes if either its magnitude or direction, or both changes. In uniform circular motion, the motion of the object is accelerated because the direction of its velocity continuously changes. The velocity at a point is along the tangent to the circle at that point, in the direction of motion.

subject: Physics
question_english: For an object in uniform circular motion of radius R, write the formula for its speed. Find the speed if R = 7 m and one revolution takes 22 s.
question_hinglish: R radius ki uniform circular motion mein object ki speed ka formula likho. Agar R = 7 m aur ek chakkar 22 s mein ho toh speed nikaalo.
answer_english:
In one revolution the object covers the circumference 2πR in time T, so speed v = 2πR ÷ T.
Given: R = 7 m, T = 22 s, π = 22/7
Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 m
v = 44 m ÷ 22 s = 2 m/s
In one full revolution, the displacement and average velocity are zero.
answer_hinglish:
Ek chakkar mein object samay T mein paridhi 2πR tay karta hai, isliye speed v = 2πR ÷ T.
Given: R = 7 m, T = 22 s, π = 22/7
Paridhi = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 m
v = 44 m ÷ 22 s = 2 m/s
Ek poore chakkar mein displacement aur average velocity zero hote hain.
ncert_context: What is the distance travelled by the child in making one revolution (going round the circle once)? It is equal to the circumference of the circle. So, if the radius of the circular path is R, the distance travelled by the child in making one revolution is 2πR. On the other hand, the displacement is zero, since the child comes back to its original position after making one revolution. If an object takes time T to make one revolution, its average speed v will be v = 2πR/T, while the average velocity during the time interval T will be 0, since the displacement is 0. For uniform circular motion, since the speed is constant, its value is the same at every point on the circle.

subject: Physics
question_english: A marble moving around the inside of a ring keeps going in a circle. What happens when the ring is lifted, and why?
question_hinglish: Ring ke andar ghoomti goli gol chakkar lagaati rehti hai. Ring uthaane pe kya hota hai, aur kyun?
answer_english: Once the ring is lifted, the marble moves off in a straight line. It continues to move in the direction it was moving at the instant the ring was removed, which is along the tangent to the circle at that point, because the ring is no longer turning it.
answer_hinglish: Ring uthaate hi goli seedhi line mein chal padti hai. Woh usi disha mein chalti rehti hai jisme ring hataane ke pal pe chal rahi thi, yaani us point pe gole ki tangent ke saath, kyunki ab ring use mod nahi raha.

This is because once the marble is released, it continues to move in the direction it has been moving at the instant the ring was removed. The velocity at a point is along the tangent to the circle at that point, in the direction of motion.

question_english: Which statement about displacement is true? (i) It is never zero (ii) Its magnitude can be greater than the distance travelled (iii) Its magnitude is less than or equal to the distance travelled (iv) Its magnitude is always less than the distance travelled

question_english: Fill in the blanks: The slope of a position-time graph gives ______, the slope of a velocity-time graph gives ______, and the area under a velocity-time graph gives ______.
question_hinglish: Blank bharo: Position-time graph ka slope ______ deta hai, velocity-time graph ka slope ______ deta hai, aur velocity-time graph ke neeche ka area ______ deta hai.

ncert_context: From a position-time graph, by finding the positions of the object at two instants of time, you can calculate the average velocity; BC/CA is called the slope of line AB. The area enclosed by the velocity-time graph and the time axis for a desired time interval is equal to the displacement in that time interval. By finding the slope and area from velocity-time graph for motion with constant acceleration, we can determine acceleration and displacement, respectively.

subject: Physics
question_english: What can a force do to an object? Why must the direction of a force be specified?
question_hinglish: Force kisi object pe kya kar sakta hai? Force ki disha batana kyun zaroori hai?
answer_english: A force can make an object move from rest, change the speed and direction of a moving object, and change the shape of an object; for example, a bat changes the direction of a ball and fingers squeeze a lemon. The effect of a force depends on both its magnitude and its direction, so like displacement, velocity and acceleration, force needs a direction along with its magnitude and unit. Its SI unit is the newton (N), and its magnitude expresses its strength.
answer_hinglish: Force object ko rest se chala sakta hai, chalte object ki speed aur disha badal sakta hai, aur object ka aakaar badal sakta hai; jaise bat gend ki disha badalta hai aur ungliyan nimbu nichodti hain. Force ka asar uske magnitude aur disha dono pe nirbhar hai, isliye displacement, velocity aur acceleration ki tarah force ke saath bhi magnitude aur unit ke alaava disha batani padti hai. Iski SI unit newton (N) hai, aur iska magnitude iski taakat batata hai.

question_english: How can the magnitude of a force be measured? What is weight?
question_hinglish: Force ka magnitude kaise naapa ja sakta hai? Weight kya hai?
answer_english: A spring balance can measure the magnitude of a force: pulling its free end shows the force with which the spring inside is pulled. subject: Physics
question_english: What are balanced and unbalanced forces? Explain with a tug of war.
question_hinglish: Balanced aur unbalanced forces kya hain? Rassa-kashi se samjhao.
answer_english: Balanced forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, so the net force is zero; in a tug of war, if both teams pull equally, the rope does not move. If one team pulls harder, the forces are unbalanced, a non-zero net force acts, and the rope moves towards the larger force. An object's motion depends only on the net force acting on it.
answer_hinglish: Balanced forces magnitude mein barabar par disha mein ulte hote hain, isliye net force zero hota hai; rassa-kashi mein dono teams barabar kheenchein toh rassa nahi hilta. Agar ek team zyada zor se kheenche, toh forces unbalanced hain, non-zero net force lagta hai, aur rassa bade force ki taraf jaata hai. Object ki motion sirf us pe lagne wale net force pe nirbhar karti hai.
ncert_context: Have you ever played a game of tug of war where two teams pull at a rope in opposite directions? If both the teams pull the rope with equal force, the rope does not move. Such two forces, which are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction are called balanced forces. However, if one team pulls harder, i.e., it applies a force of larger magnitude, the forces are no longer balanced and the rope moves in the direction of the larger force. If the forces applied on an object are not balanced, a non-zero net force acts on the object. Multiple forces may act on an object, but its motion depends only on the net force.

question_english: Forces of 10 N and 6 N act on a block. Find the net force when (a) both act to the right (b) 10 N acts right and 6 N left (c) 10 N acts left and 6 N right.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why does a box not move when a small force is applied, and why does a moving object stop when we stop pushing it?
question_hinglish: Thoda force lagaane pe box kyun nahi hilta, aur dhakelna band karne pe chalta object kyun ruk jaata hai?
answer_english: The force of friction between the box and the floor acts opposite to the applied force. The box moves only when the applied force is larger than friction, giving a net force in the direction of motion. Once moving, if we stop pushing, friction still acts against the motion, slows the object and brings it to rest, as when we stop pedalling a bicycle. So to keep an object moving on a real surface, we must keep applying a force to counter friction.
answer_hinglish: Box aur farsh ke beech friction ka bal lagaaye gaye force ke ulta lagta hai. Box tabhi chalta hai jab lagaaya force friction se zyada ho, jisse motion ki disha mein net force lage. Chalne ke baad dhakelna band karein toh friction motion ke khilaaf lagta rehta hai, object ko dheema karke rok deta hai, jaise cycle ka pedal band karne pe. Isliye asli satah pe object chalaate rehne ke liye friction ke khilaaf lagaataar force lagaana padta hai.
ncert_context: Many a times, you might have experienced that on applying a force on an object, it did not move and you had to apply a larger force to move it. It is due to the force of friction arising between the bottom surface of the box and the floor acting in a direction opposite to the direction of the force applied by you. The box will start moving when the force applied by you is of larger magnitude than the force of friction, so that a net force acts on the box in the direction of its motion. Once the box starts moving and you stop applying the force on it, the box slows down and comes to a stop. You stop pedalling a bicycle and after some time it comes to rest. On a moving object, we have to continuously apply a force to counter the force of friction. Otherwise, the force of friction acting against the direction of motion brings the object to rest.

subject: Physics
question_english: In the stack-of-coins activity, coins launched by the same stretched rubber band travel different distances on wood, laminate and marble. What does this show, and how is it confirmed with a spring balance?
question_hinglish: Sikkon ke dher wali activity mein ek hi kheenche rubber band se chhode sikke lakdi, laminate aur marble pe alag-alag doori tay karte hain. Isse kya pata chalta hai, aur spring balance se ise kaise confirm karte hain?
answer_english: The rubber band gives the same push each time, so the different distances show that friction differs between surfaces. On smoother surfaces like polished marble, the coins slow down more gradually and travel farther, meaning friction is smaller. Pulling a wooden block with a spring balance until it just moves on each surface confirms this: the reading, an approximate measure of friction, is smallest on the surface where the coins went farthest and largest where they went least.
answer_hinglish: Rubber band har baar barabar dhakka deta hai, isliye alag doori dikhati hai ki alag satahon pe friction alag hai. Chikne polished marble jaisi satahon pe sikke dheere-dheere dheeme hote hain aur zyada door jaate hain, yaani friction kam hai. Har satah pe lakdi ke block ko spring balance se tab tak kheenchna jab tak woh bas chalne lage, ise confirm karta hai: reading, jo friction ka andaaza hai, us satah pe sabse kam hai jahan sikke sabse door gaye aur jahan sabse kam gaye wahan sabse zyada.
ncert_context: Even though the rubber band is stretched by the same amount in each case, the distance travelled by the stack of coins on different surfaces changes. This indicates that the force of friction on these surfaces is different. Take a spring balance and a wooden block. Pull the spring balance with gradually increasing force and note down the reading on it when the block just starts moving. The reading of the spring balance gives an approximate measure of the force of friction acting between the surface of the block and the surface on which it moves. A smaller reading indicates a smaller force of friction, while a larger reading indicates a larger force of friction. When the force of friction is smaller, the velocity of the stack of coins decreases more slowly, and it travels a larger distance before coming to rest.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does friction help us walk? Why are soles and tyres grooved, and why is it hard to walk on wet polished floors or ice?
question_hinglish: Friction humein chalne mein kaise madad karta hai? Joote ke talve aur tyres pe groove kyun hote hain, aur geele chikne farsh ya barf pe chalna mushkil kyun hai?
answer_english: While walking, we push the ground backwards with our feet; as the foot tries to slide back, friction from the ground acts forward and moves us ahead, so here friction helps motion. Without friction, the foot would slip and we would fall. Grooves on soles and treads on tyres increase friction with the floor or road. Wet polished floors, ice and roads covered with water or snow have little friction, so walking or driving on them is difficult and risky.
answer_hinglish: Chalte waqt hum pairon se zameen ko peechhe dhakelte hain; jab pair peechhe phisalna chahta hai, zameen ka friction aage ki taraf lagkar humein aage badhaata hai, yaani yahan friction motion mein madad karta hai. Bina friction pair phisal jaata aur hum gir jaate. Talvon ke groove aur tyres ke treads farsh ya sadak se friction badhaate hain. Geele chikne farsh, barf aur paani ya barf se dhaki sadakon pe friction kam hota hai, isliye un pe chalna ya gaadi chalaana mushkil aur khatarnaak hai.
ncert_context: Notice what you do while walking or running. You push the ground backwards with your feet. The ground applies an opposite force on your feet to make you move forward. The force applied by the ground is in the form of friction. Thus, in this case friction helps you move rather than oppose you. While walking or running when you push the ground backwards with your foot, i.e., when your foot tries to slide backwards, the force of friction acts in the forward direction. Had there been no force of friction, your foot would have slipped backwards while attempting to push the ground and you would have fallen down. Grooves are made on the soles of footwear to increase the force of friction between the floor and soles. Similarly, treads on tyres of vehicles help increase the force of friction between the tyres and the road. It is difficult to walk on wet polished floors or ice, and it is risky to drive on roads covered with water or snow.

subject: Physics
question_english: Which forces act on a box being pushed along the floor? How can friction be reduced?
question_hinglish: Farsh pe dhakele ja rahe box pe kaun se forces lagte hain? Friction kaise kam kiya ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Forces on the box: the applied force; friction opposite to motion; its weight (gravitational force) acting downward; and the normal force from the surface acting upward, perpendicular to it. Weight and normal force balance each other, and air friction is usually negligible. Friction can be reduced using lubricants, coatings or texturing of surfaces, streamlining shapes, and magnetic levitation.
answer_hinglish: Box pe forces: lagaaya gaya force; motion ke ulta friction; neeche ki taraf uska weight (gurutvaakarshan bal); aur satah se upar ki taraf, usse lamb, normal force. Weight aur normal force ek-doosre ko balance karte hain, aur hawa ka friction aam taur pe nagany hota hai. Friction ko lubricants, satah pe coating ya texturing, aakaar ko streamline karke aur magnetic levitation se kam kiya ja sakta hai.
ncert_context: For an object being pushed, apart from the applied force and the force of friction, some other forces may also be acting on it. One of these is the gravitational force (weight) and the other is the force exerted by the surface on which it is placed called the normal force. The weight acts in the downwards direction, whereas the normal force acts in the upward direction perpendicular to the surface. However, the two forces are balanced. Air around the object also exerts a force of friction on the box when the box moves through the air, but in many cases its magnitude is so small that it can be neglected. In the real world, friction is always present whenever surfaces are in contact. Scientists have been trying to find ways to reduce friction between surfaces by using lubricants, coatings or texturing of surfaces, streamlining shapes of objects, and by using magnetic levitation.

subject: Physics
question_english: How did Galileo's thought experiment change the idea that a force is needed to keep an object moving?
question_hinglish: Galileo ke thought experiment ne is vichaar ko kaise badla ki object ko chalaate rehne ke liye force chahiye?
answer_english: For ages, it was wrongly believed that a force was needed to keep an object moving at constant velocity. In the 17th century, Galileo argued through thought experiments that if a body moves on a horizontal plane and all impediments are removed, it would keep moving forever. Imagine coins launched on a frictionless floor: with no friction, nothing would slow them, so they would never stop. A force is needed only to start, stop or change the velocity of an object.
answer_hinglish: Sadiyon tak galat maana gaya ki sthir velocity se chalaate rehne ke liye force chahiye. 17vi sadi mein Galileo ne thought experiments se kaha ki agar koi body horizontal samtal pe chale aur saari rukaavatein hata di jaayein, toh woh hamesha chalti rahegi. Bina friction wale farsh pe chhode sikkon ki kalpana karo: unhe dheema karne wala kuch nahi, isliye woh kabhi nahi rukenge. Force sirf object ko chalaane, rokne ya uski velocity badalne ke liye chahiye.
ncert_context: In ancient times, it was well recognised that a force was required to move a stationary object or to stop a moving object. It was only in the 17th century that Galileo Galilei argued through a series of thought experiments that if a body moves along a horizontal plane and all impediments to its motion are removed, it will continue to move indefinitely. But once the object is moving, no further force is required to keep it moving with a constant velocity. However, to change the velocity, or to stop a moving object, a force will have to be applied.

subject: Physics
question_english: State Newton's second law of motion and define one newton.
question_hinglish: Newton ka doosra niyam batao aur ek newton ki paribhasha do.
answer_english: Newton's second law: when a net force acts on an object, the object accelerates in the direction of the net force; the acceleration is proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass. Mathematically, a = F/m, or F = ma. One newton is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in an object of mass 1 kg: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 kg m/s².
answer_hinglish: Newton ka doosra niyam: jab kisi object pe net force lagta hai, toh object net force ki disha mein accelerate karta hai; acceleration net force ke anupaati aur mass ke vyutkramaanupaati hota hai. Ganit mein a = F/m, ya F = ma. Ek newton woh force hai jo 1 kg mass ke object mein 1 m/s² ka acceleration paida kare: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 kg m/s².
ncert_context: Newton's second law of motion can be stated as: When a net force acts on an object, the object accelerates in the direction of the net force. The magnitude of the acceleration is proportional to the magnitude of the net force and is inversely proportional to the mass of the object. Mathematically it can be expressed as a = F/m or F = ma where a denotes acceleration, F denotes force, and m denotes mass of the object. The direction of acceleration is the same as the direction of net force. The SI units of mass and acceleration are kg and m/s² respectively. If m = 1 kg, a = 1 m/s², then F = (1 kg) × (1 m/s²) = 1 kg m/s² = 1 N. One newton of force is defined as the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² on an object of mass 1 kg.

subject: Physics
question_english: How do the cart experiments show the relation between force, mass and acceleration?
question_hinglish: Cart wale experiments force, mass aur acceleration ka sambandh kaise dikhaate hain?
answer_english: A cart on a table is pulled by a thread attached to a hanging cup; the cup's weight provides the force. Doubling the mass in the cup (doubling the force) for the same cart makes it cover the same distance in less time, so acceleration increases with force. Keeping the force fixed and doubling the cart's mass makes it take longer, so acceleration decreases with mass. Since s = ½aT², a₁/a₂ = T₂²/T₁². Results may differ slightly from exact doubling or halving due to friction and measurement errors.
answer_hinglish: Mez pe rakhi cart ko latakte cup se bandhe dhaage se kheencha jaata hai; cup ka weight force deta hai. Friction aur naap ki galtiyon se nateeje theek double ya aadhe se thoda alag aa sakte hain.

question_english: A barbell has 10 kg fixed on each side of a 10 kg bar. How much force must a weightlifter apply to hold it steady? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
question_hinglish: Ek barbell mein 10 kg ki rod ke dono taraf 10-10 kg lage hain. Use sthir pakadne ke liye weightlifter ko kitna force lagaana hoga? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
answer_english:
Total mass = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 kg
Weight (downward) = mg = 30 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 294 N
To hold it steady, the net force must be zero, so she applies 294 N upward.

subject: Physics
question_english: A 25 kg block rests on a floor where the maximum friction is 50 N. Find its displacement in 2 s if pushed with a constant force of (i) 50 N and (ii) 55 N.
question_hinglish: 25 kg ka block farsh pe rakha hai jahan maximum friction 50 N hai. Agar use (i) 50 N aur (ii) 55 N ke sthir force se dhakela jaaye, toh 2 s mein uska displacement nikaalo.
answer_english:
(i) Applied force 50 N = friction 50 N, so the forces balance, net force = 0, and the block stays stationary: displacement = 0 m.
(ii) Net force = 55 − 50 = 5 N
a = F/m = 5 N ÷ 25 kg = 0.2 m/s²
s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 0.2 × 2² = 0.4 m, in the forward direction

subject: Physics
question_english: A 1500 kg sports car moving east speeds up from rest to 10 m/s in 5 s, moves at constant velocity from 5 s to 10 s, and slows to rest from 10 s to 15 s. Find the force on it in each interval.
question_hinglish: Poorab ki taraf chalti 1500 kg ki sports car 5 s mein rest se 10 m/s tak tez hoti hai, 5 se 10 s tak sthir velocity se chalti hai, aur 10 se 15 s mein rukti hai. Har antaraal mein us pe force nikaalo.
answer_english:
(i) 0–5 s: a = (10 − 0) ÷ 5 = 2 m/s²; F = 1500 × 2 = 3000 N, towards the east
(ii) 5–10 s: constant velocity, so a = 0 and net force = 0
(iii) 10–15 s: a = (0 − 10) ÷ 5 = −2 m/s²; F = 1500 × (−2) = −3000 N, i.e. 3000 N towards the west, opposite to the motion
answer_hinglish:

ncert_context: Example 6.6: A sports car of mass 1500 kg is moving towards the east. Calculate the force acting on the car during (i) 0 s to 5 s (ii) 5 s to 10 s (iii) 10 s to 15 s. (i) During 0 s to 5 s, the velocity-time graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis, with u = 0 m/s, v = 10 m/s and t = 5 s. Using v = u + at, a = 2 m/s². Using F = ma, F = 1500 kg × 2 m/s² = 3000 N acting towards the east. (ii) During 5 s to 10 s, the velocity-time graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis, indicating constant velocity. Hence, no force is acting on the sports car. (iii) During 10 s to 15 s, u = 10 m/s, v = 0 m/s and t = 5 s, so a = –2 m/s² and F = 1500 kg × (–2 m/s²) = –3000 N. The negative sign shows that the force is acting in a direction opposite to the direction of motion, that is towards the west.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why does a fielder pull the hands back while catching a fast ball? How do airbags and landing mats reduce injury?
question_hinglish: Tez gend pakadte waqt fielder haath peechhe kyun kheenchta hai? Airbags aur landing mats chot kaise kam karte hain?
answer_english: Pulling the hands back increases the time over which the ball's velocity drops to zero, which reduces its acceleration, so by F = ma a smaller force is needed and the fielder's hands are less hurt. An airbag inflates into a soft cushion in a collision so the passenger's head and chest stop over a longer time, lowering the force on them. A landing mat or sand bed does the same for a high jumper. Bubble wrap or hay protects glass items in transport the same way.
answer_hinglish: Haath peechhe kheenchne se gend ki velocity zero hone ka samay badhta hai, jisse uska acceleration ghat-ta hai, aur F = ma se kam force lagta hai, isliye fielder ke haath ko kam chot lagti hai. Takkar mein airbag naram gadde ki tarah phoolta hai taaki yaatri ka sir aur chhaati zyada samay mein rukein, jisse un pe force kam hota hai. High jumper ke liye landing mat ya ret ka bistar bhi yahi karta hai. Bubble wrap ya ghaas kaanch ke saamaan ko isi tarah bachaati hai.
ncert_context: While catching a fast-moving ball, the fielder gradually pulls their hands backwards with the moving ball just after catching it. In doing so, the time duration is increased during which the high velocity of the ball reduces to zero. This reduces the magnitude of the acceleration of the ball as it slows down, thus requiring a smaller force to be applied by the fielder to stop the ball. Applying a smaller force to the moving ball also minimises injury to the fielder. For a similar reason, airbags are provided in vehicles. In the event of a collision, the airbag inflates quickly into a soft compressible cushion. The passenger's head and chest push into the bag, and the time over which the hitting occurs increases. Smaller acceleration means a reduced force exerted on the person, lowering the risk of serious injuries. During a high jump event, a landing mat or sand bed is placed for the athlete to fall upon. How are glass items packed for transportation using a bubble wrap or hay protected from damage?

subject: Physics
question_english: State Newton's third law of motion. Why don't the action and reaction forces cancel each other?
question_hinglish: Newton ka teesra niyam batao. Action aur reaction forces ek-doosre ko cancel kyun nahi karte?
answer_english: Newton's third law: whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object simultaneously exerts an equal and opposite force on the first. Two connected spring balances pulled apart always show the same reading, confirming this. The two forces act on different objects, so they do not balance each other; only equal and opposite forces on the same object balance.
answer_hinglish: Newton ka teesra niyam: jab ek object doosre pe force lagata hai, toh doosra object usi samay pehle pe barabar aur ulta force lagata hai. Jode hue do spring balance kheenchne pe hamesha same reading dikhaate hain, jo ise confirm karta hai. Yeh do forces alag objects pe lagte hain, isliye ek-doosre ko balance nahi karte; sirf ek hi object pe lage barabar aur ulte forces balance hote hain.
ncert_context: Take two identical spring balances, connect them by their hooks, fix one and pull the other. The readings of the scales of two spring balances are the same every time. It indicates that the forces applied by them on each other in the opposite direction are equal in magnitude. Newton's third law of motion can be stated as: Whenever one object is exerting a force on a second object, the second object is simultaneously exerting an equal and opposite force on the first object. The forces always occur in pairs but these two forces act on two different objects. The pair of equal and opposite forces acts on two different objects, thus, they do not balance each other. On the other hand, if two equal and opposite forces act on the same object, they balance each other.

subject: Physics
question_english: Give everyday examples of Newton's third law.
question_hinglish: Newton ke teesre niyam ke roz ke examples do.
answer_english:
1. Pushing a table from a wheeled chair makes the chair move back.
2. Walking: we push the ground back, and friction from the ground pushes us forward.
3. A tree climber pushes down on the trunk, and friction pushes them up.
4. A canoeist pushes water back with the paddle, and the water pushes the paddle and canoe forward.
5. Air rushing out of a balloon pushes the balloon the opposite way; a rocket works similarly.
6. A fireperson is pushed back by the water rushing out of the pipe.

4. Naavik chappu se paani ko peechhe dhakelta hai, aur paani chappu aur naav ko aage dhakelta hai.
5. Gubbaare se nikalti hawa gubbaare ko ulti taraf dhakelti hai; rocket bhi aise hi kaam karta hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does a rocket lift off, and how did Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander use the same principle to land?
question_hinglish: Rocket kaise udaan bharta hai, aur Chandrayaan-3 ke Vikram lander ne utarne ke liye isi siddhaant ka use kaise kiya?
answer_english: A rocket's engine expels gas downward, and the gas exerts an equal and opposite force on the rocket upward. When this upward force is larger than the rocket's weight, the net force is upward and the rocket lifts off. In space, if a rocket fires its engine in its direction of motion, the exhaust pushes against the motion and slows it. The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 used this to slow down for a soft landing near the Moon's south pole.
answer_hinglish: Rocket ka engine gas ko neeche phenkta hai, aur gas rocket pe barabar aur ulta force upar ki taraf lagati hai. Jab yeh upar ka force rocket ke weight se zyada ho, toh net force upar hota hai aur rocket udaan bharta hai. Space mein agar rocket apni motion ki disha mein engine chalaaye, toh exhaust motion ke khilaaf dhakelta hai aur use dheema karta hai. Chandrayaan-3 ke Vikram lander ne isi se dheema hokar Chandrama ke dakshini dhruv ke paas soft landing ki.
ncert_context: The stretched material of the balloon applies a force on the air molecules inside to expel them as it shrinks in size. The air rushing out exerts an equal force on the balloon material in the opposite direction. This force causes the balloon to start moving in a direction opposite to the direction in which the air is rushing out. A rocket moves in a similar manner. Its engine produces gas and expels it in the downward direction, which in turn exerts an equal and opposite force on the rocket in the upward direction. This force on the rocket in the upward direction is larger than the weight of the rocket, so the net force is in the upward direction and the rocket lifts off. If the engine of a rocket moving in space fires in the direction of its motion, the exhaust gases will exert a force in the direction opposite to the direction of motion of the rocket, thereby slowing it down. This process was used by the Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 to slow down and attain the necessary velocity for a soft landing near the south pole of the Moon.

subject: Physics
question_english: A 0.1 kg bullet is fired from a 5 kg gun with a force of 2 N. Find the initial accelerations of the bullet and the gun.
question_hinglish: 5 kg ki bandook se 0.1 kg ki goli 2 N ke force se chalaayi jaati hai. Goli aur bandook ke shuruaati acceleration nikaalo.
answer_english:
By the third law, the recoil force on the gun is also 2 N, in the opposite direction.
Bullet: a = F/m = 2 N ÷ 0.1 kg = 20 m/s²
Gun: a = F/m = 2 N ÷ 5 kg = 0.4 m/s²
The forces are equal, but the accelerations differ because the masses are different.

subject: Physics
question_english: How can we find the acceleration of two boxes connected by a string and pulled by a force F on a frictionless surface?
question_hinglish: Bina friction wali satah pe dhaage se jude aur force F se kheenche ja rahe do boxes ka acceleration kaise nikaalte hain?
answer_english: Treat the two boxes and the string as a single system. The tension in the string is an internal force, acting equally and oppositely on both boxes, so it can be ignored. Only the external force F matters. By Newton's second law, the system's acceleration is a = F ÷ (m₁ + m₂), as if it were a single object of mass m₁ + m₂.
answer_hinglish: Dono boxes aur dhaage ko ek hi system maano. Dhaage ka tension andar ka force hai, jo dono boxes pe barabar aur ulta lagta hai, isliye ise chhod sakte hain. Sirf bahari force F maayne rakhta hai. Newton ke doosre niyam se system ka acceleration a = F ÷ (m₁ + m₂), jaise woh m₁ + m₂ mass ka ek hi object ho.
ncert_context: Consider two boxes of masses m₁ and m₂ placed on a frictionless horizontal surface and connected by a string. A force F pulls Box 1 to the right. Box 1 applies a force on Box 2 via the string. By Newton's third law, Box 2 applies an equal and opposite force via the string on Box 1. We call this force tension T. A simpler way is to consider the two boxes and the string as a single system. In this approach, the forces within the system (internal forces) need not be considered and only forces that act from the outside (external forces) matter. The tension T acting on both the boxes is the internal force, while the force F is the external force. Thus, using Newton's second law, the acceleration of the system is a = F/(m₁ + m₂). The system of two boxes accelerates just like a single object of mass m₁ + m₂.

question_hinglish: Ek tractor m₁ mass ke harrow ko force F se kheenchkar acceleration a₁ deta hai, aur m₂ mass ki trolley ko usi force se a₂ deta hai. Jab woh trolley pe harrow rakhkar kheenche, toh acceleration a₁ aur a₂ ke roop mein nikaalo. (Friction chhod do.)

subject: Physics
question_english: Define work done by a constant force. What is one joule?
question_hinglish: Sthir force dwara kiye gaye work ki paribhasha do. Ek joule kya hai?
answer_english: Work done on an object by a constant force = force × displacement in the direction of the force, W = F × s. Its SI unit is the joule (J). One joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force: 1 J = 1 N × 1 m = 1 kg m²/s². When describing work, the agency doing the work and the object on which it is done must be specified.

subject: Physics
question_english: Using the example of lifting wheat bags, explain why work depends on both force and displacement.
question_hinglish: Gehun ki boriyan uthaane ke example se samjhao ki work force aur displacement dono pe kyun nirbhar karta hai.
answer_english: Lifting one 5 kg bag by 1 m needs an upward force equal to its weight. Lifting three bags together to the same height needs 3 times the force and gives 3 times the work, so work is proportional to force over the same distance. Lifting one bag to 3 m instead of 1 m also gives 3 times the work, so work is proportional to displacement for the same force. A machine would need 3 times the fuel in both cases. This leads to W = F × s.
answer_hinglish: 5 kg ki ek bori 1 m uthaane ke liye uske weight jitna upar ka force chahiye. Teen boriyan ek saath usi oonchaai tak uthaane mein 3 guna force aur 3 guna work lagta hai, yaani same doori pe work force ke anupaati hai. Ek bori ko 1 m ki jagah 3 m uthaane pe bhi 3 guna work lagta hai, yaani same force pe work displacement ke anupaati hai. Dono cases mein machine ko 3 guna fuel lagega. Isi se W = F × s milta hai.
ncert_context: Consider a wheat bag of mass 5 kg kept on the floor. To lift the bag slowly to a height of 1 m, you must apply an upward force equal to mg. Suppose you lift all the 3 bags together to the same height. You would need to apply a force 3 times larger than that required for a single bag. The work done by you would be 3 times the work required to lift 1 bag. This shows that applying a larger force over the same distance allows you to proportionally do more work. Next, consider lifting a single 5 kg bag of wheat but to a height of 3 m. You would have carried out 3 times more work as compared to lifting the same bag by 1 m. If the same machine is used, it would require 3 times more fuel. Thus, applying the same force over a larger distance allows you to proportionally do more work.

subject: Physics
question_english: When is the work done by a force zero? Why do we feel tired pushing a wall even though no work is done?
question_hinglish: Force dwara kiya gaya work kab zero hota hai? Deewar dhakelne pe work zero hone ke baavjood hum thak kyun jaate hain?
answer_english: Work is zero if the force is zero, if there is no displacement (s = 0), or if the force is perpendicular to the displacement. Pushing a rigid wall does no work on it because the wall does not move. We still feel tired because our muscles repeatedly expand and contract to apply the force, using up the body's internal energy. Likewise, a girl carrying a box while walking does no work on it with her upward force, since the box moves horizontally.
answer_hinglish: Work zero hota hai agar force zero ho, displacement na ho (s = 0), ya force displacement ke lamb ho. Pakki deewar dhakelne pe us pe koi work nahi hota kyunki deewar hilti nahi. Phir bhi hum thakte hain kyunki force lagaane ke liye maanspeshiyan baar-baar phailti aur sikudti hain aur shareer ki andar ki urja khatm karti hain. Isi tarah chalte hue box uthaaye ladki ka upar ka force box pe work nahi karta, kyunki box horizontally chal raha hai.
ncert_context: If the force acting on an object is zero, i.e., F = 0, then no work is done on the object. The work done on an object is also zero if there is no displacement of the object, i.e., s = 0, regardless of the force being applied on it. For example, if you apply a force on an object, such as a rigid wall, there is no displacement in the wall and you have done no work on the wall. This may seem odd because you feel tired. To apply a force, the muscles in your body repeatedly expand and contract, and use up the internal energy of your body. If a force acts in a direction perpendicular to the displacement of an object, the work done by that force is zero because there is no displacement in the direction of the force. For example, when a girl carries a box while walking, she applies an upward force to balance its weight, while the box moves horizontally.

subject: Physics
question_english: A goalkeeper's hand moves back 15 cm as she stops a ball with a force of 200 N. How much work does she do on the ball?
question_hinglish: 200 N ke force se gend rokte hue goalkeeper ka haath 15 cm peechhe jaata hai. Woh gend pe kitna work karti hai?
answer_english:
The force opposes the ball's motion, so the displacement in the direction of the force is negative.
W = F × s = 200 N × (−0.15 m) = −30 J
The goalkeeper does −30 J of work on the ball, reducing its energy. By the third law, the ball does positive work on the goalkeeper.

Force gend ki motion ke khilaaf hai, isliye force ki disha mein displacement negative hai.

question_english: A constant force of 10 N acts on an object while it moves 1 m in the direction of the force. Find the work done using a force-displacement graph.
question_hinglish: Ek object pe 10 N ka sthir force lagta hai jab woh force ki disha mein 1 m chalta hai. Force-displacement graph se work nikaalo.
answer_english:
On a force-displacement graph, work equals the area under the graph.
The graph is a rectangle of height 10 N and width 1 m.
W = 10 N × 1 m = 10 J
Even for a varying force, work can be found as the area under the force-displacement graph.

Badalte force ke liye bhi work force-displacement graph ke neeche ke area se nikaala ja sakta hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is energy? State the work-energy theorem with examples.
question_hinglish: Urja kya hai? Examples ke saath work-energy theorem batao.
answer_english: Energy is the capacity to do work. When positive work is done on an object, it gains energy, which it can later use to do work on another object. A ball thrown by a fielder gains energy and knocks down the wicket; a flowerpot raised to a height gains energy and can damage an object below if it falls. The work-energy theorem states: work done on an object = change in its energy. It holds for systems and for non-constant forces too. Energy, like work, is measured in joules.
answer_hinglish: Urja work karne ki kshamta hai. Jab kisi object pe positive work hota hai, toh use urja milti hai, jisse woh baad mein doosre object pe work kar sakta hai. Fielder ki phenki gend urja paakar wicket gira deti hai; oonchaai pe rakha gamla urja paata hai aur girne pe neeche ki cheez ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai. Work-energy theorem kehta hai: object pe kiya gaya work = uski urja mein badlav. Yeh systems aur badalte forces ke liye bhi sahi hai. Urja bhi work ki tarah joule mein naapi jaati hai.
ncert_context: A fielder throws a cricket ball towards the wicket. The moving ball hits the wicket, making it fall. Similarly, a flowerpot raised to a height can damage an object below it if it falls. An object having the capacity to do work is said to possess energy. The ball gained energy from the work done by the fielder in throwing it. The pot gained energy from the work done in raising it to a height. When positive work is done on an object, it gains energy. Subsequently, the object can use that energy to apply a force on another object and cause it to move, thereby transferring energy. The relation between the work done on an object and the change in its energy is called the work-energy theorem: work done on an object = change in its energy. This theorem also holds for a system of objects or even when the forces applied on an object are not constant. The SI unit of energy is the same as the SI unit of work, the joule (J).

question_english: In a carrom shot, the striker hits a white coin which then hits the black coin. Who does work on whom, and how do the energies change?
question_hinglish: Carrom ke shot mein striker safed goti ko maarta hai jo phir kaali goti ko maarti hai. Kaun kis pe work karta hai, aur urja kaise badalti hai?
answer_english: The striker pushes the white coin in its direction of motion, doing positive work and increasing its energy; by the third law, the white coin does negative work on the striker, decreasing the striker's energy. Similarly, the white coin does positive work on the black coin, increasing its energy, while the black coin does negative work on the white coin, decreasing its energy. Energy is passed along by these collisions.
answer_hinglish: Striker safed goti ko uski motion ki disha mein dhakelta hai, positive work karke uski urja badhata hai; teesre niyam se safed goti striker pe negative work karti hai aur striker ki urja ghataati hai. Isi tarah safed goti kaali goti pe positive work karke uski urja badhati hai, jabki kaali goti safed pe negative work karke uski urja ghataati hai. In takkaron se urja aage badhti hai.
ncert_context: Example 7.3: In a game of carrom, a player played a shot to pocket the black coin. The moving striker collides with the white coin, which in turn collides with the black coin. The moving striker applies force in the direction of displacement of the white coin. The striker, thus, does positive work on the white coin, increasing its energy. By Newton's third law, the white coin applies an opposite force and does negative work on the striker, decreasing its energy. Similarly, the white coin does positive work on the black coin increasing its energy, while the black coin does negative work on the white coin, decreasing its energy.

subject: Physics
question_english: Besides mechanical work, how can energy be transferred? Give examples of conversion between forms of energy.
question_hinglish: Mechanical work ke alaava urja kaise transfer ho sakti hai? Urja ke roop badalne ke examples do.
answer_english:
Energy can also be transferred as heat (from a hotter to a colder object), by radiation (the Sun's energy reaching Earth), in electric circuits, through sound waves, and in nuclear reactions that power the Sun.
Conversions: a bulb turns electrical energy into light; an electric water heater turns electrical energy into thermal energy; food's chemical energy powers muscles as mechanical energy; a ringing bell turns mechanical energy into sound.
answer_hinglish:
Urja garmi ke roop mein (garam se thandi cheez ki taraf), radiation se (Sooraj ki urja Dharti tak), bijli ke circuits mein, aawaaz ki tarangon se, aur Sooraj ko chalaane wali nuclear reactions mein bhi transfer hoti hai.
Roop badalna: bulb bijli ki urja ko roshni mein badalta hai; electric water heater bijli ko garmi mein; khaane ki chemical urja maanspeshiyon mein mechanical urja banti hai; bajti ghanti mechanical urja ko aawaaz mein badalti hai.
ncert_context: Doing mechanical work is one way of transferring energy from one object to another. But that is not the only way! Energy can also be transferred as heat. When two objects at different temperatures come in contact, energy flows from the hotter one to the colder one. Energy can also move without direct contact. For example, the Sun's energy reaches the Earth through radiation. Energy is transferred in electric circuits, as well as via sound waves, and even in nuclear reactions that power the Sun. It is possible to change energy from one form to another. For example, electrical energy is converted into light energy in a bulb, and into thermal energy of the water in an electric water heater. The chemical energy in the food we eat powers our muscles and gets converted into mechanical energy. Similarly, a ringing bell converts mechanical energy into sound energy.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is kinetic energy? Derive the expression K = ½mv².
question_hinglish: Kinetic energy kya hai? K = ½mv² ka expression derive karo.
answer_english: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has due to its motion. Let a constant force F act on mass m, changing its velocity from u to v over displacement s. From v² = u² + 2as, s = (v² − u²)/2a. Work done W = F × s = ma × (v² − u²)/2a = ½m(v² − u²). By the work-energy theorem, this equals the change in energy. If the object starts from rest (u = 0), its kinetic energy is K = ½mv². Its unit is the joule, and it has no direction.
answer_hinglish: Kinetic energy woh urja hai jo object ke paas uski motion ki wajah se hoti hai. Maan lo mass m pe sthir force F lagta hai aur displacement s mein velocity u se v ho jaati hai. v² = u² + 2as se s = (v² − u²)/2a. Work W = F × s = ma × (v² − u²)/2a = ½m(v² − u²). Work-energy theorem se yeh urja ka badlav hai. Agar object rest se shuru ho (u = 0), toh uski kinetic energy K = ½mv². Iski unit joule hai, aur iski koi disha nahi hoti.
ncert_context: The energy possessed by an object due to its motion is called kinetic energy. Consider an object of mass m, starting from an initial velocity u. Let v be its final velocity and it undergoes a displacement s. Assume the force F acting on the object is constant. Then v² = u² + 2as, or s = (v² − u²)/2a. From the definition of work, W = F × s. Using Newton's second law, F = ma, we get W = ma × s. Substituting the value of s, W = ½m(v² − u²). From the work-energy theorem, the work done by the force acting on the object translates into the change in the energy of the object. If the initial velocity of the object is u = 0, the change in the energy of the object is equal to its final kinetic energy. Thus, the kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with a velocity v is K = ½mv². The SI unit of kinetic energy is the joule (J). The kinetic energy has no direction.

subject: Physics
question_english: If the velocity of a vehicle doubles, how does its kinetic energy change? Two objects A and B of masses m and 4m have the same kinetic energy; find the ratio of their speeds.
question_hinglish: Gaadi ki velocity double ho jaaye toh uski kinetic energy kaise badlegi? m aur 4m mass ke do objects A aur B ki kinetic energy same hai; unki speeds ka anupaat nikaalo.
answer_english:
K = ½mv². With velocity 2v: K' = ½m(2v)² = 4 × ½mv², so kinetic energy becomes 4 times.
Same KE for A and B: ½m v_A² = ½(4m) v_B², so v_A² = 4v_B² and v_A : v_B = 2 : 1.
answer_hinglish:
K = ½mv². Velocity 2v pe: K' = ½m(2v)² = 4 × ½mv², yaani kinetic energy 4 guna ho jaati hai.
A aur B ki same KE: ½m v_A² = ½(4m) v_B², isliye v_A² = 4v_B² aur v_A : v_B = 2 : 1.

Its initial kinetic energy will be ½mv². If the vehicle travels with a velocity 2v, its kinetic energy will be ½m(2v)² = 4 × ½mv². The new value of the kinetic energy will be 4 times the previous value. Two objects A and B of mass m and 4m have the same kinetic energy. What is the ratio of the magnitude of velocities of A and B?

subject: Physics
question_english: An Indian bowler delivers a 0.2 kg cricket ball at about 154.8 km/h. Find its kinetic energy.
question_hinglish: Ek Indian bowler 0.2 kg ki cricket gend lagbhag 154.8 km/h se phenkta hai. Uski kinetic energy nikaalo.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle velocity ko m/s mein badlo: v = 154.8 km/h = 154.8 × 1000 ÷ 3600 = 43 m/s
K = ½mv² = ½ × 0.2 × 43² = 0.1 × 1849 = 184.9 J
Yaani gend ke paas lagbhag 185 J kinetic energy hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: A 15000 kg jet lands on an aircraft carrier and is stopped within 100 m by a wire exerting a constant backward force of 367500 N. What was its velocity just before the wire caught it?
question_hinglish: 15000 kg ka jet aircraft carrier pe utarta hai aur 367500 N ka sthir peechhe ka force lagaane wale taar se 100 m mein ruk jaata hai. Taar pakadne se theek pehle uski velocity kya thi?
answer_english:
Work done by the wire = F × s = 367500 N × (−100 m) = −36750000 J (negative, as force opposes motion)
Change in KE = 0 − ½ × 15000 × v²
By the work-energy theorem: −½ × 15000 × v² = −36750000
v² = 36750000 ÷ 7500 = 4900, so v = 70 m/s = 252 km/h
answer_hinglish:
Taar ka work = F × s = 367500 N × (−100 m) = −36750000 J (negative, kyunki force motion ke khilaaf hai)
KE ka badlav = 0 − ½ × 15000 × v²
Work-energy theorem se: −½ × 15000 × v² = −36750000

subject: Physics
question_english: What is potential energy? Explain with a stretched band, a bow, a spring and a pair of magnets.
question_hinglish: Potential energy kya hai? Kheenche band, dhanush, spring aur magnets ke jode se samjhao.
answer_english: Potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its deformation, or in a system of objects due to their relative positions. A stretched slingshot band or a bent bow stores the work done to deform it; on release, it returns to shape and gives kinetic energy to the stone or arrow. A compressed spring does the same. Unlike magnetic poles pulled apart store energy due to their positions; released, they rush together and gain kinetic energy. Systems interacting through gravitational, electric or magnetic forces store energy this way.
answer_hinglish: Potential energy woh urja hai jo kisi object mein uske aakaar badalne se, ya objects ke system mein unki saapeksh sthiti se jama hoti hai. Kheencha gulel ka band ya mudaa dhanush use mode mein lage work ko jama karta hai; chhodne pe woh waapas aakaar mein aakar patthar ya teer ko kinetic energy deta hai. Dabi spring bhi yahi karti hai. Alag kiye ulte magnetic poles apni sthiti se urja jama karte hain; chhodne pe woh paas daudte hain aur kinetic energy paate hain. Gurutvaakarshan, bijli ya chumbakiya balon se jude systems aise hi urja jama karte hain.
ncert_context: When you release the stretched elastic band of a slingshot, the object in contact with it shoots in the forward direction. The archer pulls on the string of the bow bending its arms. When released, the bow comes back along with the string to its original position, and the arrow flies off the bow. This energy must have come from the stretched band and the bent bow, which have the capacity to do work due to their shape. The work done by the force which was applied to cause these deformations was stored in the band or the bow. When you stretch or compress a spring, you do work on the spring to change its shape. In turn, the spring stores energy while it is in a deformed state. When unlike poles of two magnets are separated from each other and released, they move towards each other and gain kinetic energy. Whenever a system of objects interacts through forces, such as gravitational, electric or magnetic forces, the system can store energy due to the relative positions of the objects. The energy stored by an object as a result of its deformation or in a system of objects due to their relative positions is called the potential energy.

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the expression for gravitational potential energy, U = mgh. What does the sand-bed activity show?
question_hinglish: Gravitational potential energy U = mgh ka expression derive karo. Ret ke bistar wali activity kya dikhaati hai?
answer_english: Take potential energy as zero for an object of mass m on the ground. To raise it slowly to height h, a force equal to its weight mg must be applied over displacement h, so the work done is W = mg × h. By the work-energy theorem, this work is stored as potential energy: U = mgh, in joules. Dropping a heavy ball on sand from greater heights makes deeper depressions, showing that potential energy increases with height. U = mgh is valid only near the Earth's surface.
answer_hinglish: Zameen pe rakhe m mass ke object ki potential energy zero maano. Use dheere h oonchaai tak uthaane ke liye uske weight mg ke barabar force h displacement tak lagaana padta hai, isliye work W = mg × h. Work-energy theorem se yeh work potential energy ke roop mein jama hota hai: U = mgh, joule mein. Bhaari gend ko zyada oonchaai se ret pe giraane pe gehra gaddha banta hai, jo dikhata hai ki oonchaai ke saath potential energy badhti hai. U = mgh sirf Dharti ki satah ke paas sahi hai.
ncert_context: Raise the ball over the sand bed to a height of about 1 m and drop it. Now, raise the ball to the height of 2 m and release it. You find that the depression is deepest when the ball is dropped from the greatest height. Raising a ball to a greater height from the surface of the Earth requires more work. Thus, the greater the height of the ball above the Earth's surface, the greater is its potential energy. Consider an object of mass m lying on the ground. We can define the potential energy to be zero in this configuration. To raise the object gradually to a height h, we need to apply a force equal to the force mg. The work done W by this applied force on the object is W = mg × h = mgh. According to the work-energy theorem, the work done on the object appears as a change in its potential energy. Thus, the potential energy U of the object at a height h is given by U = mgh. The expression for the potential energy of an object at height h is valid only near the Earth's surface.

question_english: A 50 kg student is lifted 72.5 m to the top of a building in an elevator, and later climbs the stairs to the same top. Find the gain in potential energy in both cases. (g = 10 m/s²) What do you conclude?
question_hinglish: 50 kg ke student ko lift se 72.5 m oonchi building ke top tak le jaaya jaata hai, aur baad mein woh seedhiyon se usi top tak chadhta hai. Dono cases mein potential energy ki badhat nikaalo. (g = 10 m/s²) Tum kya nishkarsh nikaalte ho?
answer_english:
Elevator: U = mgh = 50 × 10 × 72.5 = 36250 J
Stairs: the student reaches the same height, so U = 36250 J again
The gain in potential energy depends only on the height reached, not on the path taken.

subject: Physics
question_english: State the law of conservation of mechanical energy and show it for a freely falling object.
question_hinglish: Mechanical energy ke sanrakshan ka niyam batao aur aazaad girte object ke liye ise dikhao.
answer_english: Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy. An object of mass m dropped from height h has PE = mgh and KE = 0 at the top, so total = mgh. After falling for time t, its velocity is gt and it has fallen ½gt². PE becomes mgh − ½mg²t² and KE becomes ½mg²t², so the total is still mgh. The potential energy lost equals the kinetic energy gained. So mechanical energy is conserved if no other external forces act.
answer_hinglish: Mechanical energy kinetic aur potential energy ka jod hai. h oonchaai se giraaye m mass ke object ki top pe PE = mgh aur KE = 0, isliye kul = mgh. t samay girne ke baad uski velocity gt hai aur woh ½gt² gir chuka hai. PE mgh − ½mg²t² aur KE ½mg²t² ho jaati hai, isliye kul ab bhi mgh hai. Ghati potential energy badhi kinetic energy ke barabar hai. Yaani koi aur bahari force na lage toh mechanical energy sanrakshit rehti hai.
ncert_context: The sum of the kinetic energy and the potential energy of the object is called its mechanical energy. Consider an object with mass m which has been lifted to a Point A at height h and dropped. Its initial velocity u is equal to zero. At point A: potential energy of the object = mgh, kinetic energy of the object = 0, mechanical energy = mgh. As the object falls due to the gravitational force for a time t till point B, its velocity increases to v = gt and it falls ½gt². At point B: potential energy = mgh − ½mg²t², kinetic energy = ½mv² = ½mg²t², mechanical energy = mgh. As the object falls down with time t, its potential energy decreases while its kinetic energy increases. The lost potential energy of the object is converted into kinetic energy during motion, while its mechanical energy remains constant and equal to mgh. The mechanical energy of the object is conserved if no other external forces act on it. This is called the conservation of mechanical energy.
