subject: Physics
question_english: How does a simple pendulum show conservation of mechanical energy? Why does it eventually stop?
question_hinglish: Simple pendulum mechanical energy ka sanrakshan kaise dikhata hai? Yeh aakhir ruk kyun jaata hai?
answer_english: At the extreme point P, the bob is at height h with potential energy mgh and zero kinetic energy. At the lowest point Q, potential energy is zero and kinetic energy is maximum. At the other extreme R, kinetic energy is again zero and the potential energy is regained, as the bob rises to almost the same height. This shows mechanical energy stays constant. In real life, the pendulum slowly stops because of energy lost to friction at the support and air resistance.
answer_hinglish: Kinaare ke point P pe bob h oonchaai pe hai jisme potential energy mgh aur kinetic energy zero hai. Sabse neeche ke point Q pe potential energy zero aur kinetic energy sabse zyada hai. Doosre kinaare R pe kinetic energy phir zero hai aur potential energy waapas aa jaati hai, kyunki bob lagbhag same oonchaai tak chadhta hai. Yeh dikhata hai ki mechanical energy sthir rehti hai. Asal mein pendulum support ke friction aur hawa ke virodh se urja khone ki wajah se dheere-dheere ruk jaata hai.
ncert_context: Set up a simple pendulum. Draw a horizontal line above the position of the bob when it is not oscillating. Take the bob to one side to a point P, which is at the level of the horizontal line and let it go. At point P, the pendulum bob has the potential energy equal to mgh, where h is the height from the bottom-most point. At point Q, the potential energy is zero, but the pendulum has kinetic energy. Finally at point R, on the other side of the pendulum where it stops, the kinetic energy is zero but the pendulum bob regains its potential energy. The pendulum bob reaches almost the same height it started with. This demonstrates that the mechanical energy of the bob remains constant. However, in real life, the pendulum slows down and eventually stops because of energy loss due to friction at the support and air resistance.

subject: Physics
question_english: Neglecting friction, find the speed of a child at the bottom of a slide of height h. If h = 5 m and g = 10 m/s², what is the speed? Does the mass of the child or the shape of the slide matter?
question_hinglish: Friction chhodkar h oonchaai ki slide ke neeche bachche ki speed nikaalo. Agar h = 5 m aur g = 10 m/s² ho toh speed kya hai? Kya bachche ka mass ya slide ka aakaar maayne rakhta hai?
answer_english:
Potential energy at the top converts fully into kinetic energy at the bottom:
mgh = ½mv², so v = √(2gh)
For h = 5 m: v = √(2 × 10 × 5) = √100 = 10 m/s
Since m cancels and only h appears, neither the child's mass nor the slide's shape affects the speed at the bottom.
answer_hinglish:
Top ki potential energy neeche poori kinetic energy ban jaati hai:
mgh = ½mv², isliye v = √(2gh)
h = 5 m ke liye: v = √(2 × 10 × 5) = √100 = 10 m/s
m kat jaata hai aur sirf h bachta hai, isliye bachche ka mass ya slide ka aakaar neeche ki speed pe asar nahi karta.
ncert_context: Example 7.8: What will be the magnitude of velocity of the child on reaching the bottom of the slide of height h? Potential energy of the child at the top of the slide = mgh. Let the magnitude of velocity of the child on reaching the bottom of the slide be v. Then, the kinetic energy of the child at the bottom of the slide is ½mv². The potential energy of the child at the top of the slide gets converted entirely to the child's kinetic energy at the bottom of the slide (neglecting the effects of friction). Thus, equating the two, we obtain v = √(2gh). As this velocity of the child at the bottom of the slide depends only upon the height h, the shape of the slide or the mass of the child should not matter.

subject: Physics
question_english: A 2 kg ball is thrown up at 20 m/s and reaches a height of 19.4 m. What is the sign of the work done by gravity going up and coming down? How much work was done by air resistance? (g = 10 m/s²)
question_hinglish: 2 kg ki gend 20 m/s se upar phenki jaati hai aur 19.4 m oonchaai tak pahunchti hai. Upar jaate aur neeche aate gravity ke work ka chinh kya hai? Hawa ke virodh ne kitna work kiya? (g = 10 m/s²)
answer_english:
Going up, gravity acts down opposite to the motion, so its work is negative; coming down, it acts along the motion, so its work is positive.
Initial KE = ½ × 2 × 20² = 400 J
PE at the top = mgh = 2 × 10 × 19.4 = 388 J (KE = 0 at the top)
Work by air resistance = final energy − initial energy = 388 − 400 = −12 J
answer_hinglish:
Upar jaate gravity motion ke ulta neeche lagti hai, isliye uska work negative hai; neeche aate woh motion ke saath lagti hai, isliye positive.
Shuruaati KE = ½ × 2 × 20² = 400 J
Top pe PE = mgh = 2 × 10 × 19.4 = 388 J (top pe KE = 0)
Hawa ke virodh ka work = antim urja − shuruaati urja = 388 − 400 = −12 J

question_english: A 1.5 kg coconut falls from a 10 m tree onto wet sand and stops by making a depression. Find (i) its speed just before impact and (ii) the depth of the depression if the sand's average resistive force is 3000 N. (g = 10 m/s²)
question_hinglish: 1.5 kg ka nariyal 10 m oonche ped se geeli ret pe girkar gaddha banakar ruk jaata hai. (i) Takraane se theek pehle uski speed aur (ii) agar ret ka average virodhi force 3000 N ho toh gaddhe ki gehraai nikaalo. (g = 10 m/s²)
answer_english:
(i) mgh = ½mv², so v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 10) = √200 ≈ 14.1 m/s
(ii) Energy at impact = mgh = 1.5 × 10 × 10 = 150 J
The sand does work equal to this energy: 3000 N × d = 150 J
d = 150 ÷ 3000 = 0.05 m = 5 cm

question_english: A 10000 kg truck at 72 km/h with failed brakes enters an escape ramp inclined at 30°, rising 1 m for every 2 m along the ramp. The sand exerts 50000 N against its motion. Find the minimum ramp length to stop it. (g = 10 m/s²)
question_hinglish: Brake fail hone pe 72 km/h se chalta 10000 kg ka truck 30° jhuke escape ramp pe chadhta hai, jo ramp pe har 2 m pe 1 m oonchaai deta hai. Ret motion ke khilaaf 50000 N lagati hai. Use rokne ke liye ramp ki kam se kam lambaai nikaalo. (g = 10 m/s²)
answer_english:
v = 72 km/h = 20 m/s; initial KE = ½ × 10000 × 20² = 2000000 J
If it travels d along the ramp, height gained = d/2, so final PE = 10000 × 10 × d/2 = 50000d J
Work by sand = −50000 × d = change in energy = 50000d − 2000000
100000d = 2000000, so d = 20 m

subject: Physics
question_english: Identify the energy transformation in: a truck moving uphill, an unwinding watch spring, photosynthesis, water flowing from a dam, a burning matchstick, a solar panel and a glowing bulb.
question_hinglish: In sthitiyon mein urja ka roop badalna batao: chadhaai chadhta truck, khulti ghadi ki spring, photosynthesis, dam se behta paani, jalti maachis ki teeli, solar panel aur jalta bulb.
answer_english:
Truck moving uphill: chemical energy of fuel → kinetic and potential energy.
Unwinding watch spring: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.
Photosynthesis: light energy → chemical energy.
Water flowing from a dam: potential energy → kinetic energy (then electrical energy).
Burning matchstick: chemical energy → heat and light energy.
Solar panel: light energy → electrical energy.
Glowing bulb: electrical energy → light (and heat) energy.
answer_hinglish:
Chadhaai chadhta truck: fuel ki chemical urja → kinetic aur potential urja.
Khulti ghadi ki spring: elastic potential urja → kinetic urja.
Photosynthesis: roshni ki urja → chemical urja.
Dam se behta paani: potential urja → kinetic urja (phir bijli).
Jalti maachis: chemical urja → garmi aur roshni.
Solar panel: roshni ki urja → bijli ki urja.
Jalta bulb: bijli ki urja → roshni (aur garmi).
ncert_context: It is possible to change energy from one form to another. For example, electrical energy is converted into light energy in a bulb, and into thermal energy of the water in an electric water heater. The chemical energy in the food we eat powers our muscles and gets converted into mechanical energy. When a spring is released, it transfers its stored energy to the kinetic energy of the object in contact. Water flowing downhill converts its potential energy into kinetic energy. In modern times, the potential energy of the water stored in dams is similarly converted into kinetic energy to generate electricity. Identify the energy transformation in: a truck moving uphill, unwinding of a watch spring, photosynthesis in green leaves, water flowing from a dam, burning of a matchstick, a glowing electric bulb, and a solar panel.

question_english: When a ball thrown upward reaches its highest point, which statement is correct? (i) The force on the ball is zero (ii) Its acceleration is zero (iii) Its kinetic energy is zero (iv) Its potential energy is maximum. Options: (a) (i) and (ii) (b) (iii) and (iv) (c) only (ii) (d) all four
question_hinglish: Upar phenki gend sabse oonche point pe pahunche toh kaun sa kathan sahi hai? (i) Gend pe force zero hai (ii) Uska acceleration zero hai (iii) Uski kinetic energy zero hai (iv) Uski potential energy maximum hai. Vikalp: (a) (i) aur (ii) (b) (iii) aur (iv) (c) sirf (ii) (d) chaaron
answer_english: (b) (iii) and (iv). At the highest point, the ball is momentarily at rest, so its kinetic energy is zero, and it is at maximum height, so its potential energy is maximum. Gravity still acts on it, so the force and the acceleration (g) are not zero.
answer_hinglish: (b) (iii) aur (iv). Sabse oonche point pe gend pal bhar ke liye rukti hai, isliye kinetic energy zero hai, aur sabse zyada oonchaai pe hai, isliye potential energy maximum hai. Gravity ab bhi lagti hai, isliye force aur acceleration (g) zero nahi hain.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is power? What are its SI unit and the horsepower?
question_hinglish: Power kya hai? Iski SI unit aur horsepower kya hain?
answer_english: Power is the rate at which work is done: average power P = W ÷ t. Doing more work in the same time, or the same work in less time, needs more power; running up stairs needs more power than walking up slowly, though the work is the same. The SI unit is the watt (W): 1 W = 1 J/s, named after James Watt, who invented an efficient steam engine. One horsepower (hp) = 746 W.

answer_english:

subject: Physics
question_english: What are simple machines? Define effort, load and mechanical advantage. What is the mechanical advantage of a fixed pulley?
question_hinglish: Simple machines kya hain? Effort, load aur mechanical advantage ki paribhasha do. Fixed pulley ka mechanical advantage kitna hai?
answer_english: Simple machines make a task easier by changing the magnitude or direction of the force needed, though they cannot reduce the total work. The force we apply is the effort, and the force to be overcome is the load. Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort. A fixed pulley only changes the direction of the force, letting us pull down to lift a load up; since effort equals load, its mechanical advantage is 1. Movable pulleys or pulley systems can have a mechanical advantage greater than 1 and are used in elevators and cranes.
answer_hinglish: Simple machines zaroori force ka magnitude ya disha badalkar kaam aasaan karti hain, par kul work kam nahi kar sakti. Hum jo force lagaate hain woh effort hai, aur jis force ko paar karna hai woh load hai. Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort. Fixed pulley sirf force ki disha badalti hai, jisse hum neeche kheenchkar load upar uthaate hain; effort load ke barabar hai, isliye iska mechanical advantage 1 hai. Movable pulleys ya pulley systems ka mechanical advantage 1 se zyada ho sakta hai aur yeh lift aur crane mein use hote hain.
ncert_context: Although the total work required for a task cannot be reduced, it can be made easier by changing the magnitude or direction of the force that needs to be applied. The devices that help us do this are called simple machines. The force we apply to a machine is called the effort, and force that needs to be overcome is called the load. To describe how a machine changes the magnitude of the applied force, we define mechanical advantage as the ratio of the load to the effort: mechanical advantage = load/effort. A pulley is a wheel with a groove that guides a rope. A fixed pulley does not reduce the magnitude of the force required, it only changes its direction. It is easier for us to pull downward than to lift a load by applying an upward force directly. Since the effort and the load are equal in magnitude, the mechanical advantage of a fixed pulley is 1. Movable pulleys or a system of pulleys can have a mechanical advantage greater than 1. Pulleys are widely used in elevators and cranes.

question_english: Derive the mechanical advantage of an inclined plane. Why does a gentler slope need less effort?
question_hinglish: Inclined plane ka mechanical advantage derive karo. Kam dhalaan pe kam effort kyun lagta hai?
answer_english: To move a load of weight mg up an inclined plane of length L to height h at constant speed with effort F′, the work done is F′ × L, and the potential energy gained is mgh. Ignoring friction, by the work-energy theorem, F′ × L = mgh. So mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = mg ÷ F′ = L ÷ h. Since L > h, the effort is less than the weight. A longer, gentler slope increases L and reduces the effort further, but the force must be applied over a longer distance, so the total work stays the same.

question_english: A ramp is used to raise an object over a 30 cm high step, with the ramp's base 40 cm wide. Find the mechanical advantage of the ramp.
question_hinglish: Ek ramp se object ko 30 cm oonchi seedhi pe chadhaaya jaata hai, ramp ka aadhaar 40 cm chauda hai. Ramp ka mechanical advantage nikaalo.

Height h = 30 cm, base = 40 cm
Ramp length L = √(30² + 40²) = √(900 + 1600) = √2500 = 50 cm (right-angled triangle)
Mechanical advantage = L ÷ h = 50 ÷ 30 ≈ 1.67

subject: Physics
question_english: Why are roads on hills built to wind around in gentle slopes? Why is an inclined ladder easier to climb than a vertical one?
question_hinglish: Pahaadon pe sadkein seedhi upar jaane ki jagah halki dhalaan mein ghoomti hui kyun banaayi jaati hain? Tirchhi seedhi chadhna seedhi khadi seedhi se aasaan kyun hai?
answer_english: A winding road or inclined ladder acts as an inclined plane. A gentle slope has a large length compared with the height, so its mechanical advantage (L ÷ h) is high and the force needed to go up is much less than lifting the weight straight up. The total work to reach the top is the same, but it is spread over a longer distance, making the climb easier for vehicles and people.
answer_hinglish: Ghoomti sadak ya tirchhi seedhi inclined plane ka kaam karti hai. Halki dhalaan ki lambaai oonchaai ke mukaable zyada hoti hai, isliye uska mechanical advantage (L ÷ h) zyada hota hai aur upar jaane ka force weight seedha uthaane se bahut kam lagta hai. Top tak pahunchne ka kul work same hai, par lambi doori mein bant jaata hai, jisse gaadiyon aur logon ke liye chadhna aasaan ho jaata hai.
ncert_context: An inclined plane is a simple machine that helps move a heavy load to a higher (or lower) level. Mechanical advantage of an inclined plane = L/h. The force required to pull up the cart decreases as the plank becomes less steep. However, you have to apply the force over a larger distance to bring it to the same height. subject: Physics
question_english: What is a lever? State the principle of the lever and its mechanical advantage.
question_hinglish: Lever kya hai? Lever ka siddhaant aur uska mechanical advantage batao.
answer_english: A lever is a rigid bar that can rotate about a fixed point called the fulcrum. Its parts are the fulcrum, the load and the effort; the load arm and effort arm are the distances of the load and effort from the fulcrum. A lever balances when effort × effort arm = load × load arm. So mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = effort arm ÷ load arm. A longer effort arm needs less effort, but the effort end moves farther, so the total work stays the same.
answer_hinglish: Lever ek kada dand hai jo ek sthir point, fulcrum, ke chaaron or ghoom sakta hai. Iske hisse hain fulcrum, load aur effort; load arm aur effort arm fulcrum se load aur effort ki dooriyan hain. Lever tab santulit hota hai jab effort × effort arm = load × load arm. Isliye mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = effort arm ÷ load arm. Lamba effort arm kam effort maangta hai, par effort wala sira zyada door chalta hai, isliye kul work same rehta hai.
ncert_context: A lever is a rigid bar that can rotate about a fixed point. A lever has three main parts: (i) Fulcrum: a fixed point about which the lever rotates, (ii) Load: the force to be overcome, and (iii) Effort: the force applied. The distance of the load from the fulcrum is called the load arm, and the distance of the effort from the fulcrum is called the effort arm. The end of the lever on which the smaller force is applied, moves a larger distance, while the other end which applies a larger force moves a smaller distance. The work done on one end of the lever is transferred to the other end. effort × effort arm = load × load arm. Mechanical advantage = load/effort = effort arm/load arm. If the effort arm is increased, the effort required to move the same load is reduced. With the use of a lever, the effort required is generally smaller but it has to move by a larger distance such that the total work done remains the same.

question_english: A seesaw has seats A and E at 2 m and B and D at 1 m from the fulcrum C, on opposite sides (A, B on one side; D, E on the other). Where should children of 15 kg and 30 kg sit to balance it?
question_hinglish: Ek seesaw pe fulcrum C se 2 m pe seats A aur E aur 1 m pe B aur D hain, ulti taraf (A, B ek taraf; D, E doosri taraf). Ise balance karne ke liye 15 kg aur 30 kg ke bachche kahan baithein?
answer_english:
Balance condition: effort × effort arm = load × load arm
Let the 15 kg child sit at A (2 m): 15 × 2 = 30 × L, so L = 1 m.
The 30 kg child should sit 1 m from the fulcrum on the other side, at seat D.
The lighter child sits farther from the fulcrum to balance the heavier one.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why do we push a hard object closer to the fulcrum of scissors to cut it? Why do all real machines eventually slow down and stop?
question_hinglish: Sakht cheez kaatne ke liye use kainchi ke fulcrum ke paas kyun dhakelte hain? Saari asli machines aakhir dheemi hokar ruk kyun jaati hain?
answer_english: Moving the object closer to the scissors' fulcrum shortens the load arm. Since effort × effort arm = load × load arm, a shorter load arm lets the same effort apply a larger cutting force. Real machines stop because some energy is always lost to friction and air resistance; machines do not create energy, so without a continuous energy supply, perpetual motion is impossible.
answer_hinglish: Cheez ko kainchi ke fulcrum ke paas le jaane se load arm chhota hota hai. Kyunki effort × effort arm = load × load arm, chhota load arm same effort se zyada kaatne ka force deta hai. Asli machines isliye rukti hain kyunki kuch urja hamesha friction aur hawa ke virodh mein kho jaati hai; machines urja nahi banaati, isliye lagaataar urja ke bina hamesha chalne wali machine sambhav nahi.
ncert_context: effort × effort arm = load × load arm. Mechanical advantage = load/effort = effort arm/load arm. Scissors are a Class I lever with the fulcrum in between. Why do you push an object closer to scissors fulcrum when you want to cut an object which is hard? In all cases, the conservation of mechanical energy holds. The work we put in is equal to the useful work done on the load, ignoring friction. Machines do not create energy, they only help us use it more effectively. In real life, the pendulum slows down and eventually stops because of energy loss due to friction at the support and air resistance. Throughout history, many designs of perpetual machines have been proposed but none actually work.

subject: Physics
question_english: True or False: A simple machine reduces the total work needed to do a task.
question_hinglish: True ya False: Simple machine kisi kaam ke liye zaroori kul work kam kar deti hai.
answer_english: False. A simple machine reduces the force needed or changes its direction, but the effort must act over a larger distance, so the total work stays the same (ignoring friction).
answer_hinglish: False. Simple machine zaroori force kam karti hai ya uski disha badalti hai, par effort ko zyada doori tak lagaana padta hai, isliye kul work same rehta hai (friction chhodkar).
ncert_context: Although the total work required for a task cannot be reduced, it can be made easier by changing the magnitude or direction of the force that needs to be applied. The devices that help us do this are called simple machines. A lever reduces the force required to perform a task but not the total work done. The work done, that is the product of force and displacement, is the same in all cases. If the force decreases, the displacement increases, thereby the work done remains constant. Simple machines are devices that make work easier by changing the magnitude or direction of the force that needs to be applied, though they do not reduce total work.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does a traditional gharat (panchakki) use energy, and how is the same idea used today?
question_hinglish: Paaramparik gharat (panchakki) urja ka use kaise karti hai, aur aaj yahi vichaar kaise use hota hai?
answer_english: In the Himalayan region, water flowing downhill has potential energy, which becomes kinetic energy as it rushes down a pipe. This kinetic energy turns a wheel connected to a grinding stone, which grinds grain. Today, the potential energy of water stored in dams is similarly converted into kinetic energy to generate electricity.
answer_hinglish: Himalayan ilaake mein dhalaan se behte paani ke paas potential energy hoti hai, jo pipe mein neeche aate hue kinetic energy ban jaati hai. Yeh kinetic energy chakki ke pathar se jude pahiye ko ghumaati hai, jo anaaj peesta hai. Aaj dams mein jama paani ki potential energy ko isi tarah kinetic energy mein badalkar bijli banaayi jaati hai.
ncert_context: In the Himalayan region, water flowing downhill converts its potential energy into kinetic energy. Traditionally, this energy was used in devices, such as the gharat or panchakki — a water mill used to grind grain. These can still be found in hilly regions. The water starts from the top with potential energy. This potential energy gets converted to kinetic energy as it comes down the pipe. The kinetic energy of the water drives the wheel and sets it into rotational motion. The wheel is connected to the grinding stone at the top. In modern times, the potential energy of the water stored in dams is similarly converted into kinetic energy to generate electricity.

subject: Physics
question_english: How is sound produced? Explain with the rubber band activity and other examples.
question_hinglish: Aawaaz kaise paida hoti hai? Rubber band activity aur doosre examples se samjhao.
answer_english: Sound is produced by vibrations, the periodic to-and-fro motion of an object. A rubber band stretched over a box makes sound only while it vibrates; when the vibration stops, so does the sound, and changing its tension changes the sound. Plucked strings, struck metal, and the air column inside a bansuri vibrate to produce sound. Sound can come from vibrating strings, membranes, air columns and other objects; the object producing it is the source.
answer_hinglish: Aawaaz kampan (vibration) se paida hoti hai, yaani kisi object ka niyamit aage-peechhe hilna. Box pe kheencha rubber band sirf tab tak aawaaz karta hai jab tak woh kaanpta hai; kampan rukte hi aawaaz ruk jaati hai, aur tension badalne se aawaaz badal jaati hai. Chhede taar, maara gaya metal, aur bansuri ke andar ki hawa kaanpkar aawaaz paida karte hain. Aawaaz kaanpte taaron, jhilliyon, hawa ke column aur doosri cheezon se aa sakti hai; aawaaz paida karne wali cheez source kehlaati hai.
ncert_context: Stretch the rubber band across the open side of the box. Pluck the rubber band with a finger. Do you hear any sound? Is it vibrating? Wait till the rubber band stops vibrating. Do you still hear the sound? Change the tension in the rubber band by stretching it more or loosening it slightly. As long as the rubber band is stretched and vibrating, sound is produced. Once the vibration stops, so does the sound. From this activity, we conclude that sound is produced by vibrations. Vibration refers to the periodic to and fro motion (oscillations) of an object. Pulling a stretched string or striking a metal object makes them vibrate, which produces sound. Likewise, when you blow through a bansuri (flute), vibration of the air inside the hollow pipe produces sound. Sound can be produced by vibrating strings, membranes, air columns, and many other vibrating objects. The object that produces sound is called the 'source' of the sound.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is a tuning fork? How does it show that sound is produced by vibrating objects?
question_hinglish: Tuning fork kya hai? Yeh kaise dikhata hai ki aawaaz kaanpti cheezon se paida hoti hai?
answer_english: A tuning fork is a U-shaped metal bar of steel or aluminium with a stem; its two sides are called prongs or tines. When a prong is struck gently on a rubber pad and held near the ear, a sound is heard. When a vibrating prong touches a water surface, waves form on the water, showing the prongs are vibrating. This supports the idea that sound is produced by vibrating objects. A tuning fork gives a nearly single-frequency sound.
answer_hinglish: Tuning fork steel ya aluminium ki U-aakaar ki metal ki chhad hai jisme ek dandi hoti hai; iske do sire prongs ya tines kehlaate hain. Prong ko rubber pad pe halke se maarkar kaan ke paas laane pe aawaaz sunaayi deti hai. Kaanpte prong se paani ki satah chhoone pe paani pe lehrein banti hain, jo dikhaati hain ki prongs kaanp rahe hain. Isse is vichaar ko samarthan milta hai ki aawaaz kaanpti cheezon se banti hai. Tuning fork lagbhag ek hi frequency ki aawaaz deta hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: Can sound travel through solids and liquids? How can you show this?
question_hinglish: Kya aawaaz solids aur liquids se guzar sakti hai? Ise kaise dikhaoge?
answer_english: Yes, sound travels through solids, liquids and gases; the material it travels through is called a medium. With your ear pressed against a desk and the other ear closed, you can hear a friend gently knock or scratch the desk, showing sound travels through solids. Two metal spoons tapped together under water in a bucket can still be heard, showing sound travels through liquids.
answer_hinglish: Haan, aawaaz solids, liquids aur gases se guzarti hai; jis padaarth se guzarti hai use medium kehte hain. Ek kaan desk se lagaakar aur doosra band karke dost ke halke se desk thokne ya khurachne ki aawaaz sun sakte ho, jo dikhata hai ki aawaaz solids se guzarti hai. Balti ke paani mein dubaakar takraaye do steel ke chammach bhi sunaayi dete hain, jo dikhata hai ki aawaaz liquids se guzarti hai.
ncert_context: You and your friend stand on opposite sides of a desk. Let your friend gently knock or scratch on the desk. Now, place your ear against the desk, close your other ear and listen again. Are you able to hear the sound through the table? This shows that sound can also travel through solids. Take a large tub or bucket of water and two metal spoons. Submerge the two metal spoons in water without touching the sides or bottom of the bucket and tap them against one another. The sound of the submerged spoons tells you that the sound has reached you after travelling through water and air. Sound can travel or propagate through solids, liquids and gases. The material through which sound propagates is called a medium.

subject: Physics
question_english: Describe the vacuum bell jar experiment. What does it show, and why can't astronauts hear each other during a spacewalk?
question_hinglish: Vacuum bell jar experiment ka varnan karo. Yeh kya dikhata hai, aur spacewalk ke dauraan astronauts ek-doosre ko kyun nahi sun sakte?
answer_english: An electric bell rings inside a bell jar. As a vacuum pump removes the air, the sound becomes fainter, and near vacuum almost no sound is heard, though the bell is seen ringing. When air is let back in, the sound returns. This shows that sound cannot travel through vacuum; it needs a medium. Outer space is nearly a vacuum, so astronauts cannot directly hear each other or metal clanking, and communicate through devices in their spacesuits.
answer_hinglish: Bell jar ke andar bijli ki ghanti bajti hai. Vacuum pump se hawa nikaalne pe aawaaz dheemi hoti jaati hai, aur lagbhag vacuum hone pe ghanti bajti dikhne ke baavjood aawaaz lagbhag nahi aati. Hawa waapas daalne pe aawaaz laut aati hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki aawaaz vacuum mein nahi chal sakti; use medium chahiye. Antariksh lagbhag vacuum hai, isliye astronauts seedhe ek-doosre ko ya metal takraane ki aawaaz nahi sun sakte, aur spacesuit ke devices se baat karte hain.
ncert_context: A common experiment to show that sound needs a medium to propagate is the vacuum bell jar experiment. An electric bell kept in a bell jar is switched on and the loudness of the sound is noted. As air is sucked out from the bell jar using a vacuum pump, the sound becomes fainter. Once a near vacuum is reached, almost no sound can be heard even though the bell can be seen ringing. When air is let back into the jar, the sound can be heard again and it gradually becomes as loud as before. This experiment shows that sound cannot propagate in vacuum. Sound needs a medium to propagate. In outer space, there is a near vacuum, and thus, sound cannot propagate. Hence, astronauts in spacesuits doing spacewalks cannot directly hear each other speak or hear sounds like two metal objects clanking together. Instead, they communicate through special devices fitted into their spacesuits.

subject: Physics
question_english: A movie shows a spacecraft exploding in space with a flash of light and a loud sound at the same moment. What is wrong with this?
question_hinglish: Ek film mein antariksh mein spacecraft ke phatne pe ek hi pal mein roshni ki chamak aur tez aawaaz dikhaayi jaati hai. Isme kya galat hai?
answer_english: Space is nearly a vacuum, and sound needs a medium to travel, so no sound of the explosion could be heard; only the flash of light would be seen, since light can travel through vacuum. Even on Earth, the light and sound would not reach a viewer together, because sound travels much more slowly than light.
answer_hinglish: Antariksh lagbhag vacuum hai, aur aawaaz ko chalne ke liye medium chahiye, isliye dhamaake ki koi aawaaz nahi sunaayi degi; sirf roshni ki chamak dikhegi, kyunki roshni vacuum se guzar sakti hai. Dharti pe bhi roshni aur aawaaz ek saath nahi pahunchti, kyunki aawaaz roshni se bahut dheemi chalti hai.
ncert_context: Sound cannot propagate in vacuum. Sound needs a medium to propagate. In outer space, there is a near vacuum, and thus, sound cannot propagate. Not all waves are mechanical waves, i.e., not all waves need a medium to propagate. Light, which is a transverse wave, can travel through vacuum. This is why light from the Sun and other stars can reach the Earth. During a thunderstorm, lightning is seen before thunder is heard because sound travels much slower than light. In a movie, while showing the explosion of a spacecraft in space, a flash of light is shown along with sound at the same time.

question_english: In the slinky activity, a mark on one turn does not travel along the slinky. What does this tell us about sound waves?
question_hinglish: Slinky activity mein ek turn pe laga nishaan slinky ke saath aage nahi badhta. Isse sound waves ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer_english: When one end of the slinky is pushed and pulled repeatedly, regions of closely spaced and spread-out turns travel along it, but the marked turn only oscillates about its rest position, parallel to the disturbance. Similarly, in a sound wave the compressions and rarefactions travel through the medium, but the particles of the medium only vibrate about their mean positions; they do not travel with the wave. What is transferred is energy, not the particles.
answer_hinglish: Slinky ka ek sira baar-baar dhakelne aur kheenchne pe paas-paas aur faile turns wale hisse uske saath chalte hain, par nishaan wala turn sirf apni rest wali jagah pe gadbadi ke parallel aage-peechhe hilta hai. Isi tarah sound wave mein compressions aur rarefactions medium mein chalte hain, par medium ke kan sirf apni jagah pe kaanpte hain; woh wave ke saath nahi chalte. Jo transfer hota hai woh urja hai, kan nahi.
ncert_context: Lay out a slinky horizontally. Make a mark on a turn of the slinky. Give the slinky at your end a sharp push and then quickly pull it back again, multiple times in quick succession. subject: Physics
question_english: What are longitudinal and transverse waves? Why is sound called a longitudinal mechanical wave?
question_hinglish: Longitudinal aur transverse waves kya hain? Aawaaz ko longitudinal mechanical wave kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation; in a transverse wave, they vibrate perpendicular to it. Sound is longitudinal because air particles move back and forth along the direction the sound travels. Waves that need a material medium are mechanical waves; sound is mechanical because it cannot travel without a medium. Light, a transverse wave, is not mechanical and can travel through vacuum. Earthquake seismic waves can be longitudinal or transverse.
answer_hinglish: Longitudinal wave mein medium ke kan wave ke chalne ki disha ke parallel kaanpte hain; transverse wave mein uske lamb. Aawaaz longitudinal hai kyunki hawa ke kan aawaaz ke chalne ki disha mein hi aage-peechhe hilte hain. Jin waves ko material medium chahiye woh mechanical waves hain; aawaaz mechanical hai kyunki bina medium nahi chal sakti. Roshni, ek transverse wave, mechanical nahi hai aur vacuum se guzar sakti hai. Bhookamp ki seismic waves longitudinal ya transverse ho sakti hain.
ncert_context: In sound waves, the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth parallel to the direction of propagation of disturbance. Mechanical waves are of two types: longitudinal waves and transverse waves. In a transverse wave, the particles vibrate in a direction perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. Earthquakes produce seismic waves that travel through the Earth. These waves could be longitudinal or transverse. Not all waves are mechanical waves. Light, which is a transverse wave, can travel through vacuum.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does the grains-on-a-sheet activity show that sound carries energy? How do microphones and speakers use this?
question_hinglish: Chaadar pe daane wali activity kaise dikhaati hai ki aawaaz urja le jaati hai? Microphone aur speaker ise kaise use karte hain?
answer_english: Grains sprinkled on a sheet stretched over a container jump when a loud sound is made nearby without touching it. The sound wave reaches the sheet and makes it vibrate, so sound must carry energy. A vibrating source transfers energy to the medium, and the vibrating, colliding particles pass it on. A microphone's diaphragm is vibrated by sound waves, converting sound energy into an electrical signal; a speaker does the reverse, using an electrical signal to vibrate a cone and produce sound.
answer_hinglish: Bartan pe kasi chaadar pe chhidke daane paas mein bina chhue tez aawaaz karne pe uchhalte hain. Sound wave chaadar tak pahunchkar use kaampaati hai, isliye aawaaz urja le jaati hai. Kaanpta source medium ko urja deta hai, aur kaanpte, takraate kan use aage badhaate hain. Microphone ka diaphragm sound waves se kaanpta hai aur aawaaz ki urja ko bijli ke signal mein badalta hai; speaker ulta karta hai, bijli ke signal se cone ko kaampaakar aawaaz banata hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: How is a sound wave shown on a density-distance graph? What are the crest and trough?
question_hinglish: Density-distance graph pe sound wave kaise dikhaayi jaati hai? Crest aur trough kya hain?
answer_english: At a given instant, the density of the medium varies periodically with distance from the source. On a graph of density (y-axis) against distance (x-axis), the average density is a horizontal dashed line. In a compression, the density rises above average; the highest point, maximum density, is the crest. In a rarefaction, it falls below average; the lowest point, minimum density, is the trough. A sound wave can also be shown as density against time at one location.
answer_hinglish: Kisi pal pe medium ki density source se doori ke saath niyamit roop se badalti hai. Density (y-axis) aur doori (x-axis) ke graph pe average density ek horizontal dotted line hai. Compression mein density average se upar jaati hai; sabse ooncha point, maximum density, crest hai. Rarefaction mein woh average se neeche girti hai; sabse neecha point, minimum density, trough hai. Sound wave ko ek jagah pe density aur samay ke graph se bhi dikhaa sakte hain.
ncert_context: As a sound wave propagates, at any given instant of time the density of the medium varies periodically with distance from the source. In the graph, the distance is plotted on the x-axis, while the density of the medium is plotted on the y-axis. The average density is marked as a horizontal dashed line. In the region of a compression, the density of the medium increases above the average density and the highest point represents the maximum density. Thereafter, the density decreases and eventually falls below the average density in the region of rarefaction and the lowest point represents the minimum density. The highest point is called the crest and the lowest point is called the trough of the wave. Another way to make a graphical representation of a sound wave is to plot the variation of density of the medium with time, at a particular location in the medium.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define wavelength, frequency and time period of a sound wave, with their units. How are frequency and time period related?
question_hinglish: Sound wave ki wavelength, frequency aur time period ki units ke saath paribhasha do. Frequency aur time period kaise jude hain?
answer_english: Wavelength (λ) is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs; SI unit metre (m). Frequency (ν) is the number of density oscillations per unit time at a fixed point; SI unit hertz (Hz), or per second. Time period (T) is the time for one complete density oscillation at a point; SI unit second (s). They are inversely related: ν = 1/T, so a shorter time period means a higher frequency.
answer_hinglish: Wavelength (λ) do lagaataar crests ya troughs ke beech ki doori hai; SI unit metre (m). Frequency (ν) kisi tay point pe per unit samay density oscillations ki sankhya hai; SI unit hertz (Hz), yaani per second. Time period (T) ek point pe ek poore density oscillation ka samay hai; SI unit second (s). Yeh vyutkramaanupaati hain: ν = 1/T, isliye chhota time period matlab zyada frequency.
ncert_context: The distance between the two consecutive crests or two consecutive troughs is called the wavelength of a wave. The wavelength is usually represented by λ (Greek letter lambda). Its SI unit is the metre (m). The change in the density of the medium at a fixed point, from maximum to minimum and then again to maximum (or vice versa), makes one complete oscillation. The number of density oscillations at a fixed point per unit time is the frequency of the sound wave. It is usually represented by ν (Greek letter nu). Its SI unit is per second also called a hertz (symbol Hz). The time taken for one complete density oscillation at a fixed point is defined as the time period of the wave, represented by T. Its SI unit is second (s). The time period and frequency are inversely related; a shorter time period corresponds to a higher frequency: ν = 1/T.

subject: Physics
question_english: What are the amplitude and intensity of a sound wave? Why does sound get fainter with distance?
question_hinglish: Sound wave ka amplitude aur intensity kya hain? Doori ke saath aawaaz dheemi kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: Amplitude is the maximum change in air density in a compression or rarefaction compared to the average density; a larger amplitude carries more energy, as when a plate struck harder makes the grains jump higher. Intensity is the sound energy passing through a unit area perpendicular to the direction of propagation per unit time. As sound spreads out from its source, the same energy spreads over a larger area, so intensity decreases with distance. Sounds with larger initial amplitude travel farther before fading out.
answer_hinglish: Amplitude compression ya rarefaction mein average density ke mukaable hawa ki density ka sabse bada badlav hai; bada amplitude zyada urja laata hai, jaise thaali zor se maarne pe daane zyada uchhalte hain. Intensity per unit samay, chalne ki disha ke lamb ek unit area se guzarne wali aawaaz ki urja hai. Source se failne pe wahi urja bade area mein bant jaati hai, isliye doori ke saath intensity ghat-ti hai. Zyada shuruaati amplitude wali aawaaz khatm hone se pehle zyada door jaati hai.
ncert_context: The amplitude of a sound wave is the maximum change in the density of air in a compression (or a rarefaction) compared to the average density. A larger change in density corresponds to a larger amplitude. A wave with a larger amplitude carries more energy than the one with a smaller amplitude. When the plate is struck harder, more energy is transferred to the particles of surrounding medium. As a result, the sheet vibrates to a larger displacement and the grains jump higher. The amount of sound energy passing through a unit area perpendicular to the direction of the propagation of sound wave in a unit time is called the intensity of sound. As sound wave travels away from its source, it spreads over a larger area. Since the energy must be conserved, the same amount of energy is now spread over a larger area. Hence, the intensity decreases with distance from the source. Sounds produced with initial larger amplitude carry more energy and can travel a larger distance before intensity reduces to zero.

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the relation between the speed, wavelength and frequency of a sound wave. On what does the speed of sound depend?
question_hinglish: Sound wave ki speed, wavelength aur frequency ka sambandh derive karo. Aawaaz ki speed kis pe nirbhar karti hai?
answer_english: The speed of sound is the distance a crest travels per unit time. In one time period T, a crest travels one wavelength λ, so v = λ/T. Since ν = 1/T, v = λν: speed = wavelength × frequency. The speed depends on the medium: fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases; it is about 4–5 times faster in water and 15–20 times faster in solids than in air. In air it also increases with temperature and humidity: about 331 m/s at 0 °C and nearly 344 m/s at 22 °C.
answer_hinglish: Aawaaz ki speed woh doori hai jo crest per unit samay mein tay karta hai. Ek time period T mein crest ek wavelength λ chalta hai, isliye v = λ/T. Kyunki ν = 1/T, v = λν: speed = wavelength × frequency. Speed medium pe nirbhar karti hai: solids mein sabse tez, liquids mein dheemi aur gases mein sabse dheemi; paani mein hawa se lagbhag 4–5 guna aur solids mein 15–20 guna tez. Hawa mein temperature aur nami badhne pe bhi badhti hai: 0 °C pe lagbhag 331 m/s aur 22 °C pe lagbhag 344 m/s.
ncert_context: The speed of sound can be defined as the distance which a point on a wave, such as a crest (or a trough), travels in unit time. For a sound wave of given frequency, the distance between two consecutive crests is one wavelength (λ). This distance is covered by the disturbance in one time period (T). Therefore, the speed of sound v = λ/T. We know that frequency ν = 1/T. Thus, v = λν, speed = wavelength × frequency. The speed of sound depends on the medium through which it travels. It travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases. Sound travels about 4 – 5 times faster in water and typically 15 – 20 times faster in solids than in the air. The speed of sound in air also depends on the temperature and humidity. As we increase the temperature or humidity, the speed of sound increases. The speed of sound in dry air is about 331 m/s at 0 ºC and nearly 344 m/s at 22 ºC.

The speed of sound in air also depends on the temperature and humidity. As we increase the temperature or humidity, the speed of sound increases. The speed of sound in dry air is about 331 m/s at 0 ºC and nearly 344 m/s at 22 ºC.

question_english: Gunjan and her friend stand 340 m apart along a steel fence. Her ear is on the fence when the friend knocks it. Find the time difference between the sound arriving through steel (5000 m/s) and through air (340 m/s). Can she hear the two separately?
question_hinglish: Gunjan aur uski dost steel ki baadh ke saath 340 m door khadi hain. Dost ke baadh thokne pe Gunjan ka kaan baadh pe hai. Steel (5000 m/s) aur hawa (340 m/s) se aane wali aawaaz ke samay ka antar nikaalo. Kya woh dono alag sun sakti hai?
answer_english:
Through air: t = 340 ÷ 340 = 1 s
Through steel: t = 340 ÷ 5000 = 0.068 s
Time difference = 1 − 0.068 = 0.932 s
Since 0.932 s is more than 0.1 s, she can hear the two sounds separately.

subject: Physics
question_english: What are pitch and loudness? How are they related to the physical properties of sound?
question_hinglish: Pitch aur loudness kya hain? Yeh aawaaz ke physical gunon se kaise jude hain?
answer_english: Pitch is how humans perceive frequency: shrill sounds like a whistle or siren have high pitch and generally higher frequency, while deep sounds like thunder have low pitch and lower frequency. Loudness is how humans perceive amplitude: larger amplitude sounds louder, and loudness decreases with distance from the source. Intensity is measurable, but pitch and loudness depend on the listener, so they have no simple relation to physical properties.
answer_hinglish: Pitch woh hai jaise insaan frequency ko mehsoos karte hain: seeti ya siren jaisi teekhi aawaazon ki pitch oonchi aur frequency aam taur pe zyada hoti hai, jabki bijli ki kadak jaisi gehri aawaazon ki pitch neechi aur frequency kam. Loudness woh hai jaise insaan amplitude ko mehsoos karte hain: zyada amplitude zyada tez sunaayi deta hai, aur source se door jaane pe loudness ghat-ti hai. Intensity naapi ja sakti hai, par pitch aur loudness sunne wale pe nirbhar hain, isliye inka physical gunon se saral sambandh nahi.
ncert_context: The physical properties of sound, such as time period, wavelength, frequency, amplitude and speed are well-defined and can be measured. However, how we experience sound is subjective. Human perception of sound is described by terms, such as loudness and pitch which do not have simple relations with the physical properties. How frequency is perceived by humans is called pitch. Sounds perceived to be shrill, such as a whistle or a siren are said to have high pitch, while deep sounds like thunder or an aircraft rumble have low pitch. In general, high pitch sounds have higher frequency and low pitch sounds have lower frequency. Humans perceive the amplitude of a sound wave as loudness. Sounds with larger amplitude are heard louder, while those with smaller amplitude sound softer. The loudness decreases as we move farther away from the source. Intensity is a measurable quantity, whereas loudness depends on the listener's hearing ability.

question_english: What is the human audible range? What are infrasonic and ultrasonic waves, and which animals can hear them?
question_hinglish: Insaan ki sunne ki range kya hai? Infrasonic aur ultrasonic waves kya hain, aur kaun se jaanwar inhe sun sakte hain?
answer_english: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz); this range varies between people and decreases with age. subject: Physics
question_english: What is the difference between a tone and a musical note? What are timbre and an octave?
question_hinglish: Tone aur musical note mein kya fark hai? Timbre aur octave kya hain?
answer_english: A tone is a sound of a single frequency, like that of a tuning fork or oral whistling. A musical note, such as from a tanpura string or singing, is a combination of a lowest frequency (the fundamental) and higher frequencies (overtones), making a rich sound. Timbre is the quality that makes a flute, ektara or tabla sound different even at the same note and loudness; it comes from shape, material and construction. An octave is the interval between two notes where one has double the frequency of the other, like 200 Hz and 400 Hz.
answer_hinglish: Tone ek hi frequency ki aawaaz hai, jaise tuning fork ya muh ki seeti ki. Musical note, jaise tanpura ke taar ya gaane ki aawaaz, sabse kam frequency (fundamental) aur oonchi frequencies (overtones) ka mel hai, jo samriddh aawaaz banata hai. Timbre woh gun hai jisse same note aur loudness pe bhi bansuri, ektara ya tabla alag sunaayi dete hain; yeh aakaar, padaarth aur banaavat se aata hai. Octave do notes ka antaraal hai jahan ek ki frequency doosre ki double ho, jaise 200 Hz aur 400 Hz.
ncert_context: A tone is a sound of a single frequency like that produced by a tuning fork or by oral whistling. A musical note like the sound produced by plucking a tanpura string or singing is a combination of a lowest frequency called the fundamental and higher frequencies called overtones, which together create a rich and pleasant sound. Indian string instruments like the sarangi, sitar, and veena often use extra strings to enrich this combination. Even when different instruments like a flute, ektara, or tabla play the same note at the same loudness each sounds unique. This quality is called timbre, and comes from their shape, material and construction, which determine the pattern and intensity of the overtones. An octave is the interval between two notes where one has double the frequency of the other (for example, 200 Hz and 400 Hz).

subject: Physics
question_english: How is loudness measured, and why is noise pollution harmful?
question_hinglish: Loudness kaise naapi jaati hai, aur shor pradooshan nuksaandeh kyun hai?
answer_english: Loudness is commonly measured in decibels (dB): rustling leaves are a few dB, normal conversation is about 60 dB, and firecrackers can exceed 100 dB; even a small rise in dB means a large rise in intensity. Unwanted or harmful sound is noise. Long exposure to sound above recommended limits can affect health, sleep and hearing, and can cause hearing loss, tested by audiograms. Hearing aids, with a microphone, amplifier and speaker, help people with hearing loss.
answer_hinglish: Loudness aam taur pe decibel (dB) mein naapi jaati hai: patton ki sarsarahat kuch dB, saadharan baatcheet lagbhag 60 dB, aur pataakhe 100 dB se zyada ho sakte hain; dB mein thodi badhat bhi intensity mein badi badhat hai. Anchaahi ya nuksaandeh aawaaz shor hai. Seema se zyada aawaaz mein lambe samay rehna sehat, neend aur sunne pe asar daal sakta hai aur bahrapan la sakta hai, jiski jaanch audiogram se hoti hai. Microphone, amplifier aur speaker wale hearing aids bahrepan wale logon ki madad karte hain.
ncert_context: Sound loudness is commonly measured in decibels (dB). Very soft sounds like rustling leaves are around a few dB, normal conversation is about 60 dB, while very loud sounds, such as firecrackers can exceed 100 dB. Even a small increase in the dB level means a large increase in the sound intensity. Unwanted or harmful sound is called noise. Noise pollution is a severe problem. Exposure to sound levels above recommended limits, especially for long durations can affect health, sleep, and hearing. Prolonged exposure to loud sound can lead to hearing loss, which can be tested using audiograms. People with hearing loss may use hearing aids, which consist of a microphone, amplifier, and speaker to help the wearer hear and communicate better.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is an echo? Find the minimum distance of a reflecting surface needed to hear an echo, taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s.
question_hinglish: Echo (gunj) kya hai? Aawaaz ki speed 340 m/s lekar echo sunne ke liye reflect karne wali satah ki kam se kam doori nikaalo.
answer_english: An echo is a reflected sound heard back after some time, as near a cliff or in a long corridor; sound reflects following the same laws as light. We hear two sounds separately only if they arrive at least 0.1 s apart. In 0.1 s, sound travels 340 × 0.1 = 34 m, which is the distance to the surface and back. So the minimum distance is 34 ÷ 2 = 17 m. Echoes are clearer from hard, smooth surfaces; soft curtains absorb sound and rough surfaces scatter it.

question_english: You clap in an empty corridor and hear the echo after 0.5 s. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far is the wall? Also, how far should a surface be for an echo to arrive 0.2 s after the sound, at 343 m/s?
question_hinglish: Khaali galiyaare mein taali bajaane pe 0.5 s baad echo sunaayi deti hai. Aawaaz 340 m/s se chale toh deewar kitni door hai? 343 m/s pe echo aawaaz ke 0.2 s baad aaye, iske liye satah kitni door honi chahiye?
answer_english:
The sound travels to the wall and back, so distance = (v × t) ÷ 2.
Corridor: d = (340 × 0.5) ÷ 2 = 170 ÷ 2 = 85 m
Experiment: d = (343 × 0.2) ÷ 2 = 68.6 ÷ 2 = 34.3 m

subject: Physics
question_english: What is reverberation? How are auditoriums designed to control it? Will a reflection arriving 0.05 s after the sound produce an echo?
question_hinglish: Reverberation kya hai? Auditoriums ko ise niyantrit karne ke liye kaise design kiya jaata hai? Aawaaz ke 0.05 s baad aane wala reflection kya echo banayega?
answer_english: Reverberation is the persistence of sound after the source stops, caused by multiple reflections from walls in a large hall when reflections arrive less than 0.05 s apart. Auditoriums are designed for desirable reverberation so everyone hears clearly; sound-absorbing panels, upholstered chairs, curtains and soft porous surfaces reduce unwanted reverberation that would garble sound. A reflection arriving after just 0.05 s cannot be heard as a separate echo, since an echo needs at least 0.1 s; it adds to reverberation instead.
answer_hinglish: Reverberation source rukne ke baad bhi aawaaz ka bana rehna hai, jo bade hall ki deewaron se kai baar reflection hone se hota hai jab reflections 0.05 s se kam antar pe aayein. Auditoriums aise banaaye jaate hain ki sahi maatra mein reverberation ho aur sab saaf sun sakein; aawaaz soakhne wale panels, gaddedaar kursiyan, parde aur naram chhidredaar satahein anchaaha reverberation kam karti hain jo aawaaz ko gadbad kar deta. Sirf 0.05 s baad aane wala reflection alag echo nahi sunaayi dega, kyunki echo ke liye kam se kam 0.1 s chahiye; balki woh reverberation badhaata hai.
ncert_context: Sometimes the emitted sound can undergo multiple reflections from the walls in a large hall or auditorium. Multiple reflections make sound persist after the source stops emitting sound, a phenomenon called reverberation. This occurs when sound reflections from surfaces arrive with a time difference less than 0.05 s. Modern auditoriums and large concert halls are architecturally designed to have desirable reverberations, which allow the audience everywhere to hear speech, music, and other sounds clearly without any distortions. Sound absorbing panels, upholstered chairs, curtains and other soft, porous surfaces reduce reverberations otherwise it could lead to a garbled sound. If the time gap between two sounds reaching us is at least 0.1 s, we can hear them as separate sounds. In a room, the reflected sound reaches the ear 0.05 s after its production. Will it produce an echo or reverberation?

subject: Physics
question_english: What is echolocation? How do bats use it, and how is the same principle used in sonar?
question_hinglish: Echolocation kya hai? Chamgaadad ise kaise use karte hain, aur sonar mein yahi siddhaant kaise use hota hai?
answer_english: Echolocation is locating objects using reflected sound. Most bats emit short bursts of ultrasonic waves, which reflect from nearby objects; by sensing the echoes, a bat finds the position of obstacles and prey in the dark. Dolphins, whales and some birds also use it. Sonar (sound navigation and ranging) uses the same idea underwater: ultrasonic waves are sent into water and the reflected waves are analysed to find the distance, direction and speed of objects like submarines or shipwrecks.
answer_hinglish: Echolocation reflect hui aawaaz se cheezon ki jagah pata karna hai. Zyadatar chamgaadad ultrasonic waves ke chhote jhonke chhodte hain, jo paas ki cheezon se reflect hote hain; echo pakadkar chamgaadad andhere mein rukaavaton aur shikaar ki jagah jaan leta hai. Dolphin, whale aur kuch pakshi bhi ise use karte hain. Sonar (sound navigation and ranging) paani ke andar yahi karta hai: ultrasonic waves paani mein bhejkar reflect hui waves se submarine ya doobe jahaz jaisi cheezon ki doori, disha aur speed pata ki jaati hai.
ncert_context: Bats are nocturnal creatures that fly and search for their prey in the dark without colliding into objects. Most bats emit short bursts of ultrasonic waves which are reflected from nearby objects. By sensing the echoes the bat can determine the position of obstacles and prey. This ability to locate objects using reflected sound waves is called echolocation. Besides bats, animals such as dolphins, whales, and some birds also use echolocation for navigation and hunting. Humans have adapted the same principle in underwater exploration through sonar (sound navigation and ranging). In sonar, ultrasonic waves are sent into water and the reflected waves are analysed to determine the distance, direction, and speed of underwater objects, such as submarines or shipwrecks.

By sensing the echoes the bat can determine the position of obstacles and prey. This ability to locate objects using reflected sound waves is called echolocation. Besides bats, animals such as dolphins, whales, and some birds also use echolocation for navigation and hunting. Humans have adapted the same principle in underwater exploration through sonar (sound navigation and ranging). In sonar, ultrasonic waves are sent into water and the reflected waves are analysed to determine the distance, direction, and speed of underwater objects, such as submarines or shipwrecks.

question_english: A naval sonar signal returns after 0.90 s in seawater where sound travels at 1530 m/s. How far is the object? If another sonar signal returns after 4 s with sound at 1500 m/s, what is the ocean depth?
question_hinglish: Samudri paani mein navy ka sonar signal 0.90 s baad lautta hai jahan aawaaz 1530 m/s se chalti hai. Object kitni door hai? Agar doosra sonar signal 1500 m/s pe 4 s baad laute, toh samudra ki gehraai kya hai?
answer_english:
The signal goes to the object and back, so use half the time.
Object: d = 1530 × (0.90 ÷ 2) = 1530 × 0.45 = 688.5 m

question_english: A ship's sonar detects an echo from a sunken wreck after 5 s, with ultrasound travelling at 1525 m/s in seawater. How deep is the wreck? A car's parking sensor beeps at 1.2 m from an obstacle; how long does its ultrasound take for the round trip at 345 m/s?
question_hinglish: Ek jahaz ka sonar doobe jahaz se 5 s baad echo pakadta hai, jahan ultrasound samudri paani mein 1525 m/s se chalta hai. Doobe jahaz ki gehraai kitni hai? answer_english:
Wreck: depth = 1525 × (5 ÷ 2) = 1525 × 2.5 = 3812.5 m
Parking sensor: round-trip distance = 2 × 1.2 = 2.4 m
t = 2.4 ÷ 345 ≈ 0.007 s (about 7 milliseconds)

subject: Physics
question_english: List the applications of ultrasonic and infrasonic waves.
question_hinglish: Ultrasonic aur infrasonic waves ke upyog batao.
answer_english:
Ultrasonic waves (above 20 kHz):
1. Imaging internal organs without surgery (ultrasonography).
2. Breaking kidney stones into smaller pieces.
3. Ultrasonic welding and cleaning delicate machine parts.
4. Detecting defects inside metal blocks.
5. Locating objects by reflection (sonar, echolocation).
Infrasonic waves (below 20 Hz):
1. Detecting earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
2. Detecting severe storms, as they travel long distances through air and the Earth.
answer_hinglish:
Ultrasonic waves (20 kHz se zyada):
1. Bina surgery ke andar ke angon ki tasveer (ultrasonography).
2. Gurde ki pathri ko chhote tukdon mein todna.
3. Ultrasonic welding aur naazuk machine parts ki safaai.
4. Metal blocks ke andar ki khaamiyan pakadna.
5. Reflection se cheezein dhundhna (sonar, echolocation).
Infrasonic waves (20 Hz se kam):
1. Bhookamp aur jwaalamukhi phatna pakadna.
2. Tez toofan pakadna, kyunki yeh hawa aur Dharti mein lambi doori tak jaati hain.
ncert_context: Sound waves with frequencies outside the human audible range have important applications in science, medicine, and technology. Ultrasonic waves (more than 20 kHz): used for imaging internal organs without surgery (known as ultrasonography); used for breaking kidney stones into smaller pieces, which can then be passed out of the body; used for ultrasonic welding and for cleaning delicate machine parts in industries; used for detecting defects inside metal blocks during construction and industrial testing; used for locating objects when sound waves get reflected off them. Infrasonic waves (less than 20 Hz): used for detecting natural events, such as earthquakes and volcanic eruptions; used for detecting severe storms as such waves travel long distances through air and the Earth.

question_english: Assertion (A): We cannot hear a bell ringing in a closed jar after most of the air is pumped out. Reason (R): Sound requires a medium to travel. Choose: (i) Both true, R does not explain A (ii) Both true, R explains A (iii) A true, R false (iv) A false, R true
question_hinglish: Assertion (A): Band jar se zyadatar hawa nikaalne ke baad usme bajti ghanti sunaayi nahi deti. Reason (R): Aawaaz ko chalne ke liye medium chahiye. Chuno: (i) Dono sahi, R A ko nahi samjhata (ii) Dono sahi, R A ko samjhata hai (iii) A sahi, R galat (iv) A galat, R sahi
answer_english: (ii) Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. With almost no air left, there is no medium to carry the sound, so it cannot reach us even though the bell is ringing.
answer_hinglish: (ii) A aur R dono sahi hain, aur R A ko sahi samjhata hai. Lagbhag hawa na bachne pe aawaaz le jaane wala koi medium nahi hai, isliye ghanti bajne ke baavjood aawaaz hum tak nahi pahunchti.
ncert_context: A common experiment to show that sound needs a medium to propagate is the vacuum bell jar experiment. As air is sucked out from the bell jar using a vacuum pump, the sound becomes fainter. Once a near vacuum is reached, almost no sound can be heard even though the bell can be seen ringing. This experiment shows that sound cannot propagate in vacuum. Sound needs a medium to propagate. The medium can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas.

subject: Physics
question_english: Fill in the blanks: Speed of sound = ______ × ______. Sound travels fastest in ______ and slowest in ______. A reflected sound is heard as a separate echo only if it arrives at least ______ s after the original sound.
question_hinglish: Blank bharo: Aawaaz ki speed = ______ × ______. Aawaaz ______ mein sabse tez aur ______ mein sabse dheemi chalti hai. Reflect hui aawaaz alag echo tabhi sunaayi deti hai jab woh asli aawaaz ke kam se kam ______ s baad aaye.
answer_english: Wavelength; frequency; solids; gases; 0.1. So the reflecting surface must be at least 17 m away in air.
answer_hinglish: Wavelength; frequency; solids; gases; 0.1. Isliye hawa mein reflect karne wali satah kam se kam 17 m door honi chahiye.
ncert_context: Speed = wavelength × frequency, v = λν. The speed of sound depends on the medium through which it travels. It travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases. If the time gap between two sounds reaching us is at least 0.1 s, we can hear them as separate sounds. If it is less than 0.1 s, then we cannot clearly distinguish between them. The minimum echo distance is half of 34 m or 17 m.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does the human ear work, and how do two ears help locate the direction of a sound?
question_hinglish: Insaan ka kaan kaise kaam karta hai, aur do kaan aawaaz ki disha pata karne mein kaise madad karte hain?
answer_english: Sound entering the ear makes a thin membrane, the eardrum, vibrate. Tiny bones amplify these vibrations, and the cochlea converts them into electrical signals that go to the brain, which perceives them as sound. With two ears, the brain compares which ear hears a sound first, using a time gap often less than a thousandth of a second, to work out the direction of the sound.
answer_hinglish: Kaan mein aayi aawaaz eardrum naam ki patli jhilli ko kaampaati hai. Chhoti haddiyan in kampanon ko badhaati hain, aur cochlea inhe bijli ke signals mein badalkar dimaag ko bhejta hai, jo inhe aawaaz ki tarah samajhta hai. Do kaanon se dimaag dekhta hai ki kaun sa kaan aawaaz pehle sunta hai, aksar ek second ke hazaarve hisse se bhi kam ke antar se, aur aawaaz ki disha pata karta hai.
ncert_context: When sound enters the ear, it causes a thin membrane called the eardrum to vibrate. Tiny bones quickly amplify these vibrations and the cochlea converts them into electrical signals that rush to the brain, which perceives them as sound. Having two ears allows the brain to pinpoint the direction of the origin of sound. By comparing which ear hears the sound first, it figures out where the sound came from based on the tiny time gap between the two (often less than a thousandth of a second). Animals hear in different ways. Snakes and fish sense vibrations through their bodies, while some insects have ear-like organs on their body parts.

subject: Physics
question_english: State the laws of reflection of light. What are the properties of the image formed by a plane mirror?
question_hinglish: Light ke reflection ke niyam batao. Plane mirror se bane image ki kya properties hain?
answer_english:
Laws of reflection: (i) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. (ii) The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane. These laws apply to all reflecting surfaces, including spherical ones.
Image by a plane mirror: always virtual and erect, same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it, and laterally inverted.
answer_hinglish:
Reflection ke niyam: (i) Angle of incidence, angle of reflection ke barabar hota hai. (ii) Incident ray, point of incidence pe mirror ka normal aur reflected ray, teeno ek hi plane mein hote hain. Ye niyam spherical surfaces samet har reflecting surface pe lagte hain.
Plane mirror ka image: hamesha virtual aur erect, object jitna hi size, mirror ke peechhe utni hi doori pe jitna object aage hai, aur laterally inverted.

Let us recall these laws – (i) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, and (ii) The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence and the reflected ray, all lie in the same plane. These laws of reflection are applicable to all types of reflecting surfaces including spherical surfaces. Image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual and erect. The size of the image is equal to that of the object. The image formed is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it. Further, the image is laterally inverted.

subject: Physics
question_english: What evidence shows that light travels in straight lines, and when does this straight-line (ray) treatment fail?
question_hinglish: Kaun sa saboot dikhata hai ki light seedhi line mein chalti hai, aur ye straight-line (ray) treatment kab fail hota hai?
answer_english: A small source of light casts a sharp shadow of an opaque object, which shows that light travels in a straight line, shown as a ray. But if the opaque object in its path is very small, light bends around it instead of going straight. This is called diffraction of light. To explain diffraction, light is treated as a wave, and the straight-line ray treatment fails.
answer_hinglish: Light ka chhota source kisi opaque object ki sharp shadow banata hai, jo dikhata hai ki light seedhi line mein chalti hai, jise ray se dikhate hain. Lekin agar raaste ka opaque object bahut chhota ho, toh light seedhi jaane ki jagah uske aas-paas mud jaati hai. Ise diffraction of light kehte hain. Diffraction samjhaane ke liye light ko wave maana jaata hai, aur ray waala treatment fail ho jaata hai.
ncert_context: By observing the common optical phenomena around us, we may conclude that light seems to travel in straight lines. The fact that a small source of light casts a sharp shadow of an opaque object points to this straight-line path of light, usually indicated as a ray of light. If an opaque object on the path of light becomes very small, light has a tendency to bend around it and not walk in a straight line – an effect known as the diffraction of light. Then the straight-line treatment of optics using rays fails. To explain phenomena such as diffraction, light is thought of as a wave.

subject: Physics
question_english: How does the modern quantum theory describe the nature of light?
question_hinglish: Modern quantum theory light ki nature ko kaise batati hai?
answer_english: The wave theory of light was found inadequate to explain how light interacts with matter, where light often behaves like a stream of particles. The modern quantum theory says light is neither a 'wave' nor a 'particle'. It reconciles the particle properties of light with its wave nature.
answer_hinglish: Light aur matter ke interaction ko samjhaane mein wave theory kaafi nahi thi, kyunki wahan light aksar particles ki stream jaisi behave karti hai. Modern quantum theory kehti hai ki light na 'wave' hai na 'particle'. Ye light ki particle properties aur wave nature dono ko jodti hai.
ncert_context: To explain phenomena such as diffraction, light is thought of as a wave. Again, at the beginning of the 20th century, it became known that the wave theory of light often becomes inadequate for treatment of the interaction of light with matter, and light often behaves somewhat like a stream of particles. This confusion about the true nature of light continued for some years till a modern quantum theory of light emerged in which light is neither a 'wave' nor a 'particle' – the new theory reconciles the particle properties of light with the wave nature.

subject: Physics
question_english: Differentiate between a concave mirror and a convex mirror.
question_hinglish: Concave mirror aur convex mirror mein antar batao.
answer_english:
Concave mirror: reflecting surface is curved inwards, facing the centre of the sphere. Its centre of curvature lies in front of the mirror. Parallel rays converge at its principal focus after reflection. The inner side of a spoon acts like one.
Convex mirror: reflecting surface is curved outwards. Its centre of curvature lies behind the mirror. Parallel rays appear to diverge from its principal focus after reflection. The bulged side of a spoon acts like one.
answer_hinglish:
Concave mirror: reflecting surface andar ki taraf mudi hoti hai, sphere ke centre ki taraf. Iska centre of curvature mirror ke aage hota hai. Parallel rays reflection ke baad principal focus pe milti hain. Chammach ka andar waala hissa aisa hota hai.
Convex mirror: reflecting surface bahar ki taraf mudi hoti hai. Iska centre of curvature mirror ke peechhe hota hai. Parallel rays reflection ke baad principal focus se phailti hui lagti hain. Chammach ka ubhra hissa aisa hota hai.
ncert_context: The reflecting surface of a spherical mirror may be curved inwards or outwards. A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, that is, faces towards the centre of the sphere, is called a concave mirror. A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards, is called a convex mirror. The surface of the spoon curved inwards can be approximated to a concave mirror and the surface of the spoon bulged outwards can be approximated to a convex mirror. The centre of curvature of a concave mirror lies in front of it. However, it lies behind the mirror in case of a convex mirror. Rays parallel to the principal axis meet at a point after reflection from a concave mirror; for a convex mirror the reflected rays appear to come from a point on the principal axis.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define pole, centre of curvature, radius of curvature and principal axis of a spherical mirror.
question_hinglish: Spherical mirror ke pole, centre of curvature, radius of curvature aur principal axis ki paribhasha do.
answer_english:
Pole (P): the centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror. It lies on the surface of the mirror.
Centre of curvature (C): the centre of the sphere of which the reflecting surface is a part. It is not part of the mirror.
Radius of curvature (R): the radius of that sphere. The distance PC equals R.
Principal axis: the straight line through the pole and the centre of curvature. It is normal to the mirror at its pole.
answer_hinglish:
Pole (P): spherical mirror ki reflecting surface ka centre. Ye mirror ki surface pe hi hota hai.
Centre of curvature (C): us sphere ka centre jiska hissa reflecting surface hai. Ye mirror ka hissa nahi hota.
Radius of curvature (R): us sphere ka radius. Doori PC, R ke barabar hoti hai.
Principal axis: pole aur centre of curvature se guzarne waali seedhi line. Ye pole pe mirror ke normal hoti hai.
ncert_context: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is a point called the pole. It lies on the surface of the mirror. The pole is usually represented by the letter P. The reflecting surface of a spherical mirror forms a part of a sphere. This sphere has a centre. This point is called the centre of curvature of the spherical mirror. It is represented by the letter C. Please note that the centre of curvature is not a part of the mirror. The radius of the sphere of which the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror forms a part, is called the radius of curvature of the mirror. It is represented by the letter R. The distance PC is equal to the radius of curvature. Imagine a straight line passing through the pole and the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror. This line is called the principal axis. Principal axis is normal to the mirror at its pole.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why does a sheet of paper start burning when sunlight reflected from a concave mirror is focused on it?
question_hinglish: Concave mirror se reflect hui dhoop ko kaagaz pe focus karne se kaagaz jalne kyun lagta hai?
answer_english: The concave mirror converges the parallel rays of sunlight to a point as a sharp, bright spot, which is the image of the Sun and lies at the mirror's focus. The concentration of sunlight at this point produces heat, which ignites the paper. The distance of this spot from the mirror gives the approximate focal length.
answer_hinglish: Concave mirror dhoop ki parallel rays ko ek point pe sharp, bright spot ki tarah ikattha karta hai, jo Sun ka image hai aur mirror ke focus pe hota hai. ncert_context: Hold a concave mirror in your hand and direct its reflecting surface towards the Sun. Direct the light reflected by the mirror on to a sheet of paper held close to the mirror. Move the sheet of paper back and forth gradually until you find on the paper sheet a bright, sharp spot of light. The paper at first begins to burn producing smoke. Eventually it may even catch fire. Why does it burn? The light from the Sun is converged at a point, as a sharp, bright spot by the mirror. In fact, this spot of light is the image of the Sun on the sheet of paper. This point is the focus of the concave mirror. The heat produced due to the concentration of sunlight ignites the paper. The distance of this image from the position of the mirror gives the approximate value of focal length of the mirror.

question_english: The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 20 cm. What is its focal length? Also find the focal length of a convex mirror of radius of curvature 32 cm.
question_hinglish: Ek spherical mirror ka radius of curvature 20 cm hai. Uski focal length kya hai? 32 cm radius of curvature waale convex mirror ki focal length bhi nikaalo.

For spherical mirrors of small aperture, R = 2f, so f = R/2.

question_english: List the rays used for locating the image formed by a spherical mirror in a ray diagram.
question_hinglish: Ray diagram mein spherical mirror ka image dhoondhne ke liye kaun si rays use hoti hain?
answer_english:
(i) A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through F after reflection (concave), or appears to diverge from F (convex).
(ii) A ray through F (concave), or directed towards F (convex), emerges parallel to the principal axis after reflection.
(iii) A ray through C (concave), or directed towards C (convex), is reflected back along the same path, because it falls along the normal.
(iv) A ray incident obliquely at the pole P is reflected obliquely, making equal angles with the principal axis.
Any two of these rays are enough; their intersection gives the image.
answer_hinglish:
(i) Principal axis ke parallel ray reflection ke baad F se guzarti hai (concave), ya F se phailti hui lagti hai (convex).

(iii) C se guzarne waali ray (concave), ya C ki taraf jaati ray (convex), usi raaste wapas laut aati hai, kyunki woh normal ke along girti hai.
(iv) Pole P pe tirchhi girne waali ray tirchhi reflect hoti hai, principal axis se barabar angle banaate hue.
Inmein se koi do rays kaafi hain; jahan ye milti hain wahi image hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: Name the type of mirror used in (a) headlights of a car, (b) side/rear-view mirror of a vehicle, (c) solar furnace. Give reasons.
question_hinglish: (a) Car ki headlights, (b) gaadi ka side/rear-view mirror, (c) solar furnace mein kaun sa mirror use hota hai? Kaaran batao.
answer_english:
(a) Headlights: concave mirror. With the bulb at the focus, it gives a powerful parallel beam of light.
(b) Rear-view mirror: convex mirror. It always gives an erect, though diminished, image and has a wider field of view because it is curved outwards, so the driver sees a much larger area.
(c) Solar furnace: large concave mirror. It concentrates sunlight to a point to produce heat.
answer_hinglish:
(a) Headlights: concave mirror. Bulb focus pe ho toh ye light ki powerful parallel beam deta hai.
(b) Rear-view mirror: convex mirror. Ye hamesha erect image deta hai, bhale chhota ho, aur bahar mude hone se iska field of view wide hota hai, toh driver bahut bada area dekh paata hai.
(c) Solar furnace: bada concave mirror. Ye dhoop ko ek point pe ikattha karke garmi paida karta hai.
ncert_context: Concave mirrors are commonly used in torches, search-lights and vehicles headlights to get powerful parallel beams of light. They are often used as shaving mirrors to see a larger image of the face. Large concave mirrors are used to concentrate sunlight to produce heat in solar furnaces. Convex mirrors are commonly used as rear-view (wing) mirrors in vehicles. Convex mirrors are preferred because they always give an erect, though diminished, image. Also, they have a wider field of view as they are curved outwards. Thus, convex mirrors enable the driver to view much larger area than would be possible with a plane mirror.
