subject: Physics
question_english: State the New Cartesian Sign Convention for reflection by spherical mirrors.
question_hinglish: Spherical mirrors ke reflection ke liye New Cartesian Sign Convention batao.
answer_english:
The pole P is the origin and the principal axis is the x-axis.
(i) The object is always placed to the left of the mirror, so light falls on the mirror from the left.
(ii) All distances parallel to the principal axis are measured from the pole.
(iii) Distances to the right of the origin (+x) are positive; those to the left (−x) are negative.
(iv) Distances perpendicular to and above the principal axis (+y) are positive.
(v) Distances perpendicular to and below the principal axis (−y) are negative.
answer_hinglish:
Pole P origin hai aur principal axis x-axis hai.
(i) Object hamesha mirror ke left mein rakha jaata hai, yaani light mirror pe left se aati hai.
(ii) Principal axis ke parallel saari dooriyan pole se naapi jaati hain.
(iii) Origin ke right (+x) ki dooriyan positive; left (−x) ki negative.
(iv) Principal axis ke upar perpendicular dooriyan (+y) positive.
(v) Principal axis ke neeche perpendicular dooriyan (−y) negative.

(iv) Distances measured perpendicular to and above the principal axis (along + y-axis) are taken as positive. (v) Distances measured perpendicular to and below the principal axis (along –y-axis) are taken as negative.

subject: Physics
question_english: Write the mirror formula and define magnification produced by a spherical mirror. What does the sign of m tell us?
question_hinglish: Mirror formula likho aur spherical mirror ke magnification ki paribhasha do. m ka sign kya batata hai?
answer_english:
Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, where u is object distance, v is image distance and f is focal length, all measured from the pole with the New Cartesian Sign Convention. It is valid for all spherical mirrors and all object positions.
Magnification m = height of image/height of object = h′/h = −v/u.
A negative m means the image is real (and inverted); a positive m means the image is virtual (and erect).
answer_hinglish:
Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, jahan u object distance, v image distance aur f focal length hai, sab pole se New Cartesian Sign Convention ke saath naape gaye. Ye har spherical mirror aur har object position ke liye sahi hai.
Magnification m = image ki height/object ki height = h′/h = −v/u.
Negative m ka matlab image real (aur inverted) hai; positive m ka matlab image virtual (aur erect) hai.
ncert_context: In a spherical mirror, the distance of the object from its pole is called the object distance (u). The distance of the image from the pole of the mirror is called the image distance (v). There is a relationship between these three quantities given by the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. This formula is valid in all situations for all spherical mirrors for all positions of the object. Magnification produced by a spherical mirror is expressed as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, m = h′/h. It can also be expressed as m = h′/h = −v/u. The height of the image should be taken as positive for virtual images and negative for real images. A negative sign in the value of the magnification indicates that the image is real. A positive sign indicates that the image is virtual.

question_hinglish: Gaadi ke rear-view ke liye use hone waale convex mirror ka radius of curvature 3.00 m hai. Agar bus mirror se 5.00 m door hai, toh image ki position, nature aur size nikaalo.

f = R/2 = +1.50 m

v = +1.15 m (behind the mirror)

subject: Physics
question_english: What is refraction of light? Give everyday examples of it.
question_hinglish: Light ka refraction kya hai? Iske rozmarra ke examples do.
answer_english:
When light travels obliquely from one transparent medium into another, its direction of propagation changes in the second medium. This is called refraction of light. It happens because the speed of light changes from one medium to another.
Examples: the bottom of a tank or pond appears raised; letters under a thick glass slab appear raised; a pencil partly in water appears displaced at the surface; a lemon in a glass of water looks bigger than it is.
answer_hinglish:
Jab light ek transparent medium se doosre mein tirchhi jaati hai, toh doosre medium mein uski disha badal jaati hai. Ise refraction of light kehte hain. Ye isliye hota hai kyunki ek medium se doosre mein light ki speed badal jaati hai.
Examples: tank ya taalaab ka tala upar utha dikhta hai; moti glass slab ke neeche akshar upar uthe dikhte hain; paani mein aadhi doobi pencil surface pe khiski hui lagti hai; paani ke glass mein nimbu asal se bada dikhta hai.
ncert_context: You might have observed that the bottom of a tank or a pond containing water appears to be raised. Similarly, when a thick glass slab is placed over some printed matter, the letters appear raised when viewed through the glass slab. Have you seen a pencil partly immersed in water in a glass tumbler? It appears to be displaced at the interface of air and water. A lemon kept in water in a glass tumbler appears to be bigger than its actual size, when viewed from the sides. These observations indicate that light does not travel in the same direction in all media. It appears that when travelling obliquely from one medium to another, the direction of propagation of light in the second medium changes. This phenomenon is known as refraction of light. Refraction is due to change in the speed of light as it enters from one transparent medium to another.

subject: Physics
question_english: Explain the refraction of light through a rectangular glass slab. Why does the emergent ray come out parallel to the incident ray?
question_hinglish: Rectangular glass slab se light ka refraction samjhao. Emergent ray incident ray ke parallel kyun nikalti hai?
answer_english: At the first surface (air to glass), light goes from a rarer to a denser medium and bends towards the normal. At the opposite surface (glass to air), it goes from a denser to a rarer medium and bends away from the normal. The bending at the two opposite parallel faces is equal and opposite, so the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray. However, the ray is shifted slightly sideways.
answer_hinglish: Pehli surface pe (hawa se glass), light rarer se denser medium mein jaati hai aur normal ki taraf mudti hai. Saamne waali surface pe (glass se hawa), denser se rarer mein jaati hai aur normal se door mudti hai. Do aamne-saamne parallel faces pe ye mudna barabar aur ulta hota hai, isliye emergent ray incident ray ke parallel nikalti hai. Lekin ray thodi side mein khisak jaati hai.
ncert_context: The light ray at point O has entered from a rarer medium to a denser medium, that is, from air to glass. Note that the light ray has bent towards the normal. At O′, the light ray has entered from glass to air, that is, from a denser medium to a rarer medium. The light here has bent away from the normal. In Fig. 9.10, a ray EO is obliquely incident on surface AB, called incident ray. OO′ is the refracted ray and O′H is the emergent ray. You may observe that the emergent ray is parallel to the direction of the incident ray. The extent of bending of the ray of light at the opposite parallel faces AB (air-glass interface) and CD (glass-air interface) of the rectangular glass slab is equal and opposite. This is why the ray emerges parallel to the incident ray. However, the light ray is shifted sideward slightly.

subject: Physics
question_english: State the laws of refraction of light.
question_hinglish: Light ke refraction ke niyam batao.
answer_english:
(i) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of two transparent media at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
(ii) The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant for light of a given colour and a given pair of media: sin i/sin r = constant. This is Snell's law of refraction. The constant is the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.
answer_hinglish:
(i) Incident ray, refracted ray aur point of incidence pe do transparent media ke interface ka normal, teeno ek hi plane mein hote hain.
(ii) Angle of incidence ke sine aur angle of refraction ke sine ka ratio, ek rang ki light aur ek media pair ke liye constant hota hai: sin i/sin r = constant. Ye Snell's law of refraction hai. Ye constant doosre medium ka pehle medium ke respect mein refractive index hai.
ncert_context: Refraction is due to change in the speed of light as it enters from one transparent medium to another. Experiments show that refraction of light occurs according to certain laws. The following are the laws of refraction of light. (i) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of two transparent media at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane. (ii) The ratio of sine of angle of incidence to the sine of angle of refraction is a constant, for the light of a given colour and for the given pair of media. This law is also known as Snell's law of refraction. If i is the angle of incidence and r is the angle of refraction, then, sin i/sin r = constant. This constant value is called the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define relative refractive index and absolute refractive index in terms of the speed of light.
question_hinglish: Light ki speed ke roop mein relative refractive index aur absolute refractive index ki paribhasha do.
answer_english:
Relative refractive index of medium 2 with respect to medium 1: n₂₁ = speed of light in medium 1/speed of light in medium 2 = v₁/v₂. Similarly, n₁₂ = v₂/v₁.
Absolute refractive index: when medium 1 is vacuum or air, n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in air (vacuum) and v is the speed in the medium. The absolute refractive index is simply called the refractive index.
answer_hinglish:
Medium 2 ka medium 1 ke respect mein relative refractive index: n₂₁ = medium 1 mein light ki speed/medium 2 mein light ki speed = v₁/v₂. Isi tarah n₁₂ = v₂/v₁.
Absolute refractive index: jab medium 1 vacuum ya hawa ho, toh n = c/v, jahan c hawa (vacuum) mein light ki speed aur v medium mein speed hai. Absolute refractive index ko seedha refractive index kehte hain.
ncert_context: The value of the refractive index for a given pair of media depends upon the speed of light in the two media. Let v₁ be the speed of light in medium 1 and v₂ be the speed of light in medium 2. The refractive index of medium 2 with respect to medium 1 is given by the ratio of the speed of light in medium 1 and the speed of light in medium 2: n₂₁ = v₁/v₂. By the same argument, the refractive index of medium 1 with respect to medium 2 is n₁₂ = v₂/v₁. If medium 1 is vacuum or air, then the refractive index of medium 2 is considered with respect to vacuum. This is called the absolute refractive index of the medium. If c is the speed of light in air and v is the speed of light in the medium, then n = c/v. The absolute refractive index of a medium is simply called its refractive index.

question_english: How is optical density different from mass density? Explain with an example.
question_hinglish: Optical density mass density se kaise alag hai? Example se samjhao.
answer_english: Optical density is the ability of a medium to refract light, judged by its refractive index: the medium with the larger refractive index is optically denser. Mass density is mass per unit volume. The two are not the same. For example, kerosene has a higher refractive index (1.44) than water (1.33), so it is optically denser than water, although its mass density is less than that of water.

question_english: Differentiate between a convex lens and a concave lens.
question_hinglish: Convex lens aur concave lens mein antar batao.
answer_english:
Convex lens (double convex): two spherical surfaces bulging outwards; thicker at the middle than at the edges; converges parallel rays to a real principal focus, so it is a converging lens; focal length and power are positive.
Concave lens (double concave): two spherical surfaces curved inwards; thicker at the edges than at the middle; diverges parallel rays so they appear to come from the principal focus, so it is a diverging lens; focal length and power are negative.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define a lens, its centres of curvature, principal axis, optical centre and aperture.
question_hinglish: Lens, uske centres of curvature, principal axis, optical centre aur aperture ki paribhasha do.
answer_english:
Lens: a transparent material bound by two surfaces, of which one or both are spherical.
Centres of curvature (C₁, C₂): centres of the spheres of which the two surfaces are parts.
Principal axis: the imaginary straight line through the two centres of curvature.
Optical centre (O): the central point of the lens; a ray through it passes without deviation.
Aperture: the effective diameter of the circular outline of the lens.
answer_hinglish:
Lens: do surfaces se ghira transparent material, jisme ek ya dono surfaces spherical hon.
Centres of curvature (C₁, C₂): un spheres ke centre jinke hisse dono surfaces hain.
Principal axis: dono centres of curvature se guzarne waali kaalpanik seedhi line.
Optical centre (O): lens ka beech ka point; isse guzarne waali ray bina mude nikal jaati hai.
Aperture: lens ki golaakar outline ka effective diameter.
ncert_context: A transparent material bound by two surfaces, of which one or both surfaces are spherical, forms a lens. A lens, either a convex lens or a concave lens, has two spherical surfaces. Each of these surfaces forms a part of a sphere. The centres of these spheres are called centres of curvature of the lens. Since there are two centres of curvature, we may represent them as C₁ and C₂. An imaginary straight line passing through the two centres of curvature of a lens is called its principal axis. The central point of a lens is its optical centre. It is usually represented by the letter O. A ray of light through the optical centre of a lens passes without suffering any deviation. The effective diameter of the circular outline of a spherical lens is called its aperture.

subject: Physics
question_english: How can you find the approximate focal length of a convex lens using sunlight? Why does a paper burn in this activity?
question_hinglish: Dhoop se convex lens ki approximate focal length kaise nikaal sakte ho? Is activity mein kaagaz kyun jalta hai?
answer_english: Hold a convex lens towards the Sun and focus sunlight on a sheet of paper to get a sharp, bright image of the Sun. The distance between the lens and this image gives the approximate focal length. The paper burns because the lens converges the parallel rays of sunlight to a point; this concentration of sunlight generates heat.
answer_hinglish: Convex lens ko Sun ki taraf karke dhoop ko kaagaz pe focus karo taaki Sun ka sharp, bright image bane. Lens aur is image ke beech ki doori approximate focal length deti hai. Kaagaz isliye jalta hai kyunki lens dhoop ki parallel rays ko ek point pe ikattha karta hai; dhoop ke is jamaav se garmi banti hai.
ncert_context: Hold a convex lens in your hand. Direct it towards the Sun. Focus the light from the Sun on a sheet of paper. Obtain a sharp bright image of the Sun. The paper begins to burn producing smoke. It may even catch fire after a while. The light from the Sun constitutes parallel rays of light. These rays were converged by the lens at the sharp bright spot formed on the paper. In fact, the bright spot you got on the paper is a real image of the Sun. The concentration of the sunlight at a point generated heat. This caused the paper to burn. In this Activity, the distance between the position of the lens and the position of the image of the Sun gives the approximate focal length of the lens.

question_english: Describe the position, size and nature of the image formed by a convex lens for various positions of the object.
question_hinglish: Object ki alag-alag positions ke liye convex lens se bane image ki position, size aur nature batao.
answer_english:
1. At infinity: at F₂; highly diminished, point-sized; real and inverted.
2. Beyond 2F₁: between F₂ and 2F₂; diminished; real and inverted.
3. At 2F₁: at 2F₂; same size; real and inverted.
4. Between F₁ and 2F₁: beyond 2F₂; enlarged; real and inverted.
5. At F₁: at infinity; highly enlarged; real and inverted.
6. Between F₁ and O: on the same side as the object; enlarged; virtual and erect.

4. F₁ aur 2F₁ ke beech: 2F₂ se aage; bada; real aur inverted.
5. F₁ pe: infinity pe; bahut bada; real aur inverted.
6. F₁ aur O ke beech: object ki taraf hi; bada; virtual aur erect.

subject: Physics
question_english: Which rays are used to draw ray diagrams for image formation by lenses?
question_hinglish: Lens ke image formation ke ray diagram banane ke liye kaun si rays use hoti hain?
answer_english:
(i) A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the principal focus on the other side after refraction from a convex lens; for a concave lens it appears to diverge from the principal focus on the same side.
(ii) A ray through the principal focus of a convex lens, or appearing to meet at the principal focus of a concave lens, emerges parallel to the principal axis.
(iii) A ray through the optical centre emerges without any deviation.
Any two of these rays locate the image.
answer_hinglish:
(i) Principal axis ke parallel ray convex lens se refraction ke baad doosri taraf principal focus se guzarti hai; concave lens mein usi taraf ke principal focus se phailti hui lagti hai.
(ii) Convex lens ke principal focus se guzarne waali ray, ya concave lens ke principal focus pe milti hui lagne waali ray, principal axis ke parallel nikalti hai.
(iii) Optical centre se guzarne waali ray bina mude nikalti hai.
Inmein se koi do rays image ki jagah batati hain.

subject: Physics
question_english: Write the lens formula and the formula for magnification produced by a lens. What are the sign conventions for lenses?
question_hinglish: Lens formula aur lens ke magnification ka formula likho. Lens ke liye sign convention kya hai?
answer_english:
Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, relating object distance u, image distance v and focal length f.
Magnification: m = h′/h = v/u.
Sign convention: same as for mirrors, but all distances are measured from the optical centre. The focal length of a convex lens is positive and that of a concave lens is negative. Negative m and h′ mean a real, inverted image; positive m means virtual and erect.
answer_hinglish:
Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, jo object distance u, image distance v aur focal length f ko jodta hai.
Magnification: m = h′/h = v/u.
Sign convention: mirrors jaisa hi, bas saari dooriyan optical centre se naapi jaati hain. Convex lens ki focal length positive aur concave lens ki negative. Negative m aur h′ matlab real, inverted image; positive m matlab virtual aur erect.
ncert_context: For lenses, we follow sign convention, similar to the one used for spherical mirrors. We apply the rules for signs of distances, except that all measurements are taken from the optical centre of the lens. According to the convention, the focal length of a convex lens is positive and that of a concave lens is negative. The lens formula is expressed as 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. The lens formula is general and is valid in all situations for any spherical lens. The magnification produced by a lens is defined as the ratio of the height of the image and the height of the object, m = h′/h. Magnification produced by a lens is also related to the object-distance u, and the image-distance v: m = h′/h = v/u.

subject: Physics
question_english: A concave lens has focal length 15 cm. At what distance should the object be placed so that it forms an image 10 cm from the lens? Also find the magnification.
question_hinglish: Concave lens ki focal length 15 cm hai. Object kitni doori pe rakhein ki image lens se 10 cm pe bane? Magnification bhi nikaalo.
answer_english:
A concave lens forms a virtual, erect image on the same side as the object.
Given: v = −10 cm, f = −15 cm
1/u = 1/v − 1/f = −1/10 + 1/15 = (−3 + 2)/30 = −1/30
u = −30 cm
m = v/u = (−10)/(−30) = +1/3 ≈ +0.33
Answer: The object is 30 cm from the lens. The image is virtual, erect and one-third the size of the object.

question_english: Define the power of a lens. What is its SI unit? Define 1 dioptre.
question_hinglish: Lens ki power ki paribhasha do. Iski SI unit kya hai? 1 dioptre ki paribhasha do.
answer_english: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length, P = 1/f. It expresses the degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by the lens. subject: Physics
question_english: How is the power of lenses in contact found, and why do opticians and instrument makers find this useful?
question_hinglish: Ek doosre se jude lenses ki power kaise nikaalte hain, aur opticians aur instrument banane waalon ke liye ye kyun kaam ka hai?
answer_english: The net power of lenses placed in contact is the algebraic sum of their individual powers: P = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + … For example, lenses of +2.0 D and +0.25 D together act like a single +2.25 D lens. During eye-testing, an optician places combinations of lenses of known power in the testing frame and finds the required power by simple addition. Lens systems in cameras, microscopes and telescopes use this to increase magnification and sharpness and to minimise defects of a single lens.
answer_hinglish: Jude hue lenses ki net power unki alag-alag powers ka algebraic jod hoti hai: P = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + … Jaise +2.0 D aur +0.25 D ke lens milkar ek +2.25 D lens jaise kaam karte hain. Aankh ki jaanch mein optician testing frame mein jaani-pehchaani power ke lens lagaata hai aur seedhe jodkar zaroori power nikaal leta hai. Camera, microscope aur telescope ke lens systems isse magnification aur sharpness badhaate hain aur ek lens ke defects kam karte hain.
ncert_context: Many optical instruments consist of a number of lenses. They are combined to increase the magnification and sharpness of the image. The net power (P) of the lenses placed in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the individual powers P₁, P₂, P₃, … as P = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + … The use of powers, instead of focal lengths, for lenses is quite convenient for opticians. During eye-testing, an optician puts several different combinations of corrective lenses of known power, in contact, inside the testing spectacles' frame. The optician calculates the power of the lens required by simple algebraic addition. For example, a combination of two lenses of power + 2.0 D and + 0.25 D is equivalent to a single lens of power + 2.25 D. Such a lens system is commonly used in the design of lenses of camera, microscopes and telescopes.

question_english:
A spherical mirror and a thin spherical lens each have a focal length of −15 cm. The mirror and the lens are likely to be
(a) both concave
(b) both convex
(c) the mirror concave and the lens convex
(d) the mirror convex and the lens concave
question_hinglish:
Ek spherical mirror aur ek patle spherical lens dono ki focal length −15 cm hai. Mirror aur lens shaayad hain
(a) dono concave
(b) dono convex
(c) mirror concave aur lens convex
(d) mirror convex aur lens concave
answer_english: (a) both concave. For a mirror, the focus of a concave mirror lies in front of it (to the left), so its f is negative. For a lens, the focal length of a concave lens is negative by convention.
answer_hinglish: (a) dono concave. Mirror mein concave mirror ka focus uske aage (left mein) hota hai, isliye f negative. Lens mein convention ke hisaab se concave lens ki focal length negative hoti hai.
ncert_context: In the New Cartesian Sign Convention, distances measured to the left of the origin are taken as negative. The principal focus of a concave mirror lies in front of the mirror, so its focal length is negative, while the principal focus of a convex mirror is behind the mirror, so its focal length is positive. For lenses, all measurements are taken from the optical centre of the lens. According to the convention, the focal length of a convex lens is positive and that of a concave lens is negative.

question_english: True or False: (a) A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a lens suffers no deviation. (b) A concave lens can form a real image on a screen. (c) Clay cannot be used to make a lens.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Describe the functions of the cornea, iris, pupil, eye lens and retina in the human eye.
question_hinglish: Human eye mein cornea, iris, pupil, eye lens aur retina ke kaam batao.
answer_english:
Cornea: thin transparent membrane through which light enters; most of the refraction of light entering the eye occurs at its outer surface.
Iris: dark muscular diaphragm behind the cornea that controls the size of the pupil.
Pupil: regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Eye lens: forms an inverted real image on the retina and provides the finer adjustment of focal length for objects at different distances.
Retina: delicate membrane with an enormous number of light-sensitive cells; they generate electrical signals that go to the brain via the optic nerves.
answer_hinglish:
Cornea: patli transparent membrane jisse light andar aati hai; aankh mein aane waali light ka zyaadatar refraction iski bahari surface pe hota hai.
Iris: cornea ke peechhe dark muscular diaphragm jo pupil ka size control karta hai.
Pupil: aankh mein jaane waali light ki maatra control karti hai.
Eye lens: retina pe inverted real image banata hai aur alag dooriyon ki cheezon ke liye focal length ki fine adjustment karta hai.
Retina: naazuk membrane jisme bahut saari light-sensitive cells hoti hain; ye electrical signals banakar optic nerves se brain ko bhejti hain.
ncert_context: The human eye is like a camera. Its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the retina. Light enters the eye through a thin membrane called the cornea. It forms the transparent bulge on the front surface of the eyeball. Most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the outer surface of the cornea. The crystalline lens merely provides the finer adjustment of focal length required to focus objects at different distances on the retina. We find a structure called iris behind the cornea. Iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil. The pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye. The eye lens forms an inverted real image of the object on the retina. The retina is a delicate membrane having enormous number of light-sensitive cells. The light-sensitive cells get activated upon illumination and generate electrical signals. These signals are sent to the brain via the optic nerves.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What is meant by the power of accommodation of the eye? How do the ciliary muscles help us see near and distant objects?
question_hinglish: Aankh ki power of accommodation ka kya matlab hai? Ciliary muscles paas aur door ki cheezein dekhne mein kaise madad karti hain?
answer_english:
The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called accommodation. The eye lens is made of fibrous, jelly-like material whose curvature the ciliary muscles can change.
Distant objects: ciliary muscles relax, the lens becomes thin, and its focal length increases.
Nearby objects: ciliary muscles contract, the curvature increases, the lens becomes thicker, and its focal length decreases.
answer_hinglish:
Eye lens ki apni focal length badalne ki kshamata ko accommodation kehte hain. Eye lens fibrous, jelly jaise material ka bana hota hai jiski curvature ciliary muscles badal sakti hain.
Door ki cheezein: ciliary muscles relax hoti hain, lens patla hota hai, aur focal length badh jaati hai.
Paas ki cheezein: ciliary muscles contract hoti hain, curvature badhti hai, lens mota hota hai, aur focal length ghat jaati hai.
ncert_context: The eye lens is composed of a fibrous, jelly-like material. Its curvature can be modified to some extent by the ciliary muscles. The change in the curvature of the eye lens can thus change its focal length. When the muscles are relaxed, the lens becomes thin. Thus, its focal length increases. This enables us to see distant objects clearly. When you are looking at objects closer to the eye, the ciliary muscles contract. This increases the curvature of the eye lens. The eye lens then becomes thicker. Consequently, the focal length of the eye lens decreases. This enables us to see nearby objects clearly. The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called accommodation.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Define near point and far point of the eye. What are their values for a normal eye?
question_hinglish: Aankh ke near point aur far point ki paribhasha do. Normal aankh ke liye inki value kya hai?
answer_english:
Near point (least distance of distinct vision): the minimum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain. For a young adult with normal vision, it is about 25 cm.
Far point: the farthest point up to which the eye can see objects clearly. It is infinity for a normal eye.
So a normal eye sees clearly objects between 25 cm and infinity.

Yaani normal aankh 25 cm se infinity tak ki cheezein saaf dekhti hai.

question_english: Why is a normal eye not able to see clearly objects placed closer than 25 cm?
question_hinglish: Normal aankh 25 cm se paas rakhi cheezein saaf kyun nahi dekh paati?
answer_english: To focus a nearby object, the ciliary muscles contract and the eye lens becomes thicker, decreasing its focal length. But the focal length cannot be decreased below a certain minimum limit. For objects closer than about 25 cm (the near point), the lens cannot shorten its focal length enough to form the image on the retina, so the image is blurred and the eye feels strain.
answer_hinglish: Paas ki cheez focus karne ke liye ciliary muscles contract hoti hain aur eye lens mota hokar focal length ghata deta hai. Lekin focal length ek minimum limit se kam nahi ho sakti. Lagbhag 25 cm (near point) se paas ki cheezon ke liye lens focal length itni kam nahi kar paata ki image retina pe bane, isliye image dhundhla dikhta hai aur aankh pe zor padta hai.
ncert_context: When you are looking at objects closer to the eye, the ciliary muscles contract. This increases the curvature of the eye lens. The eye lens then becomes thicker. Consequently, the focal length of the eye lens decreases. However, the focal length of the eye lens cannot be decreased below a certain minimum limit. Try to read a printed page by holding it very close to your eyes. You may see the image being blurred or feel strain in the eye. To see an object comfortably and distinctly, you must hold it at about 25 cm from the eyes. The minimum distance, at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain, is called the least distance of distinct vision.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What happens to the image distance in the eye when we increase the distance of an object from the eye?
question_hinglish: Jab hum object ki aankh se doori badhaate hain toh aankh mein image distance ka kya hota hai?
answer_english: The image distance does not change. The image must always form on the retina, whose distance from the eye lens is fixed. When the object moves farther, the ciliary muscles relax and the lens becomes thinner, increasing its focal length, so the image still forms on the retina. This adjustment is accommodation.
answer_hinglish: Image distance nahi badalti. Image hamesha retina pe hi banna chahiye, jiski eye lens se doori fixed hai. Object door jaane pe ciliary muscles relax hoti hain aur lens patla hokar focal length badha deta hai, taaki image phir bhi retina pe bane. Isi adjustment ko accommodation kehte hain.
ncert_context: The human eye is like a camera. Its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the retina. The crystalline lens merely provides the finer adjustment of focal length required to focus objects at different distances on the retina. The change in the curvature of the eye lens can thus change its focal length. When the muscles are relaxed, the lens becomes thin. Thus, its focal length increases. This enables us to see distant objects clearly. The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called accommodation.

question_english: What is cataract? How can vision be restored?
question_hinglish: Cataract kya hai? Vision kaise wapas laaya ja sakta hai?
answer_english: In old age, the crystalline lens of some people becomes milky and cloudy. This condition is called cataract. It causes partial or complete loss of vision. Vision can be restored through cataract surgery.
answer_hinglish: Budhaape mein kuch logon ka crystalline lens doodhiya aur dhundhla ho jaata hai. Is condition ko cataract kehte hain. Isse aankh ki roshni aanshik ya poori tarah chali jaati hai. Cataract surgery se vision wapas laaya ja sakta hai.
ncert_context: Sometimes, the crystalline lens of people at old age becomes milky and cloudy. This condition is called cataract. This causes partial or complete loss of vision. It is possible to restore vision through a cataract surgery. The eye lens is composed of a fibrous, jelly-like material. The eye lens forms an inverted real image of the object on the retina.

question_english: Name the three common refractive defects of vision. How can they be corrected?
question_hinglish: Vision ke teen aam refractive defects ke naam batao. Inhe kaise theek kiya jaata hai?
answer_english:
When the eye gradually loses its power of accommodation, vision becomes blurred. The three common refractive defects are:
1. Myopia (near-sightedness): corrected by a concave lens of suitable power.
2. Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): corrected by a convex lens of appropriate power.
3. Presbyopia: corrected by corrective eye-glasses; if combined with myopia, bi-focal lenses are used.
Defects can also be corrected with contact lenses or surgery.
answer_hinglish:
Jab aankh dheere-dheere power of accommodation kho deti hai, toh vision dhundhla ho jaata hai. Teen aam refractive defects hain:
1. Myopia (near-sightedness): sahi power ke concave lens se theek hota hai.
2. Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): sahi power ke convex lens se theek hota hai.
3. Presbyopia: corrective eye-glasses se; agar myopia bhi ho toh bi-focal lenses use hote hain.
Contact lenses ya surgery se bhi defects theek ho sakte hain.

These days, it is possible to correct the refractive defects with contact lenses or through surgical interventions.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What is myopia? What are its causes and how is it corrected?
question_hinglish: Myopia kya hai? Iske kaaran kya hain aur ise kaise theek karte hain?
answer_english:
Myopia (near-sightedness): the person sees nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly. The far point is nearer than infinity, maybe a few metres. The image of a distant object forms in front of the retina instead of on it.
Causes: (i) excessive curvature of the eye lens, or (ii) elongation of the eyeball.
Correction: a concave lens of suitable power, which brings the image back on to the retina.
answer_hinglish:
Myopia (near-sightedness): insaan paas ki cheezein saaf dekhta hai par door ki cheezein saaf nahi dekh paata. Far point infinity se paas hota hai, shaayad kuch metre. Door ki cheez ka image retina pe nahi, uske aage banta hai.
Kaaran: (i) eye lens ki zyada curvature, ya (ii) eyeball ka lamba ho jaana.
Ilaaj: sahi power ka concave lens, jo image ko wapas retina pe le aata hai.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What is hypermetropia? What are its causes and how is it corrected?
question_hinglish: Hypermetropia kya hai? Iske kaaran kya hain aur ise kaise theek karte hain?
answer_english:
Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): the person sees distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly. The near point is farther than the normal 25 cm, so reading material has to be held much beyond 25 cm. Light rays from a nearby object are focussed at a point behind the retina.
Causes: (i) the focal length of the eye lens is too long, or (ii) the eyeball has become too small.
Correction: a convex lens of appropriate power; the converging lens provides the additional focusing power needed to form the image on the retina.
answer_hinglish:
Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): insaan door ki cheezein saaf dekhta hai par paas ki cheezein saaf nahi dekh paata. Near point normal 25 cm se door hota hai, isliye padhne ki cheez 25 cm se kaafi door rakhni padti hai. Paas ki cheez ki rays retina ke peechhe focus hoti hain.
Kaaran: (i) eye lens ki focal length bahut lambi hona, ya (ii) eyeball ka bahut chhota ho jaana.
Ilaaj: sahi power ka convex lens; ye converging lens retina pe image banaane ke liye extra focusing power deta hai.
ncert_context: Hypermetropia is also known as far-sightedness. A person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly. The near point, for the person, is farther away from the normal near point (25 cm). Such a person has to keep a reading material much beyond 25 cm from the eye for comfortable reading. This is because the light rays from a closeby object are focussed at a point behind the retina. This defect arises either because (i) the focal length of the eye lens is too long, or (ii) the eyeball has become too small. This defect can be corrected by using a convex lens of appropriate power. Eye-glasses with converging lenses provide the additional focussing power required for forming the image on the retina.

question_english: What is presbyopia and why does it occur? Explain how bi-focal lenses help.
question_hinglish: Presbyopia kya hai aur kyun hota hai? Bi-focal lenses kaise madad karte hain, samjhao.
answer_english:
With ageing, the power of accommodation usually decreases and the near point gradually recedes, so nearby objects cannot be seen comfortably without glasses. This is presbyopia. It arises from gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens.
A person with both myopia and hypermetropia needs bi-focal lenses: the upper part is a concave lens for distant vision and the lower part is a convex lens for near vision.
answer_hinglish:
Umar badhne ke saath power of accommodation aam taur pe ghat jaati hai aur near point dheere-dheere door khisak jaata hai, isliye bina chashme paas ki cheezein aaram se nahi dikhti. Ye presbyopia hai. Ye ciliary muscles ke dheere-dheere kamzor hone aur eye lens ki lachak kam hone se hota hai.
Jise myopia aur hypermetropia dono hon use bi-focal lenses chahiye: upar ka hissa concave lens hai jo door dekhne mein, aur neeche ka hissa convex lens hai jo paas dekhne mein madad karta hai.

subject: Physics

question_english: List the key facts about eye donation given in the chapter.
question_hinglish: Chapter mein eye donation ke baare mein di gayi mukhya baatein batao.
answer_english:
1. Donors can be of any age group or sex; spectacle users, cataract-operated people, and people with diabetes, hypertension or asthma (without communicable diseases) can donate.
2. Eyes must be removed within 4–6 hours after death; inform the nearest eye bank immediately.
3. Removal takes only 10–15 minutes and causes no disfigurement.
4. People infected with or who died of AIDS, Hepatitis B or C, rabies, acute leukaemia, tetanus, cholera, meningitis or encephalitis cannot donate.
5. One pair of eyes gives vision to up to four corneal blind people.

4. AIDS, Hepatitis B ya C, rabies, acute leukaemia, tetanus, cholera, meningitis ya encephalitis se sankramit log donate nahi kar sakte.
5. Ek jodi aankhein chaar tak corneal blind logon ko roshni de sakti hain.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Explain the refraction of light through a triangular glass prism. What is the angle of deviation?
question_hinglish: Triangular glass prism se light ka refraction samjhao. Angle of deviation kya hai?
answer_english: A triangular prism has two triangular bases and three rectangular lateral surfaces inclined to each other; the angle between two lateral faces is the angle of the prism. At the first surface (air to glass), the ray bends towards the normal. At the second surface (glass to air), it bends away from the normal. Unlike a glass slab, the faces are not parallel, so the peculiar shape of the prism makes the emergent ray bend at an angle to the incident ray. This angle is the angle of deviation.
answer_hinglish: Triangular prism mein do triangular bases aur teen rectangular lateral surfaces hoti hain jo ek doosre pe jhuki hoti hain; do lateral faces ke beech ka angle angle of the prism hai. Pehli surface pe (hawa se glass) ray normal ki taraf mudti hai. Doosri surface pe (glass se hawa) normal se door mudti hai. Glass slab ke ulat, yahan faces parallel nahi hain, isliye prism ka khaas shape emergent ray ko incident ray se ek angle pe mod deta hai. Yahi angle of deviation hai.
ncert_context: For parallel refracting surfaces, as in a glass slab, the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray. Consider a triangular glass prism. It has two triangular bases and three rectangular lateral surfaces. These surfaces are inclined to each other. The angle between its two lateral faces is called the angle of the prism. Here PE is the incident ray, EF is the refracted ray and FS is the emergent ray. A ray of light is entering from air to glass at the first surface AB. The light ray on refraction has bent towards the normal. At the second surface AC, the light ray has entered from glass to air. Hence it has bent away from normal. The peculiar shape of the prism makes the emergent ray bend at an angle to the direction of the incident ray. This angle is called the angle of deviation.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What is dispersion of white light? Why does a prism split white light into colours?
question_hinglish: White light ka dispersion kya hai? Prism white light ko rangon mein kyun baant deta hai?
answer_english: The splitting of light into its component colours is called dispersion. A glass prism disperses white light into seven colours: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red (VIBGYOR). This band of colours is called a spectrum. It happens because different colours bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray as they pass through the prism: red bends the least and violet the most. So each colour emerges along a different path and becomes distinct.
answer_hinglish: Light ka apne component rangon mein bantna dispersion kehlaata hai. Glass prism white light ko saat rangon mein baant deta hai: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange aur Red (VIBGYOR). Rangon ki is patti ko spectrum kehte hain. Aisa isliye hota hai kyunki prism se guzarte waqt alag rang incident ray ke respect mein alag angle se mudte hain: red sabse kam aur violet sabse zyada. Isliye har rang alag raaste se nikalta hai aur alag dikhta hai.
ncert_context: The prism has probably split the incident white light into a band of colours. The various colours seen are Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red. The acronym VIBGYOR will help you to remember the sequence of colours. The band of the coloured components of a light beam is called its spectrum. The splitting of light into its component colours is called dispersion. You have seen that white light is dispersed into its seven-colour components by a prism. Why do we get these colours? Different colours of light bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray, as they pass through a prism. The red light bends the least while the violet the most. Thus the rays of each colour emerge along different paths and thus become distinct.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Describe Newton's experiment with two prisms. What did it show?
question_hinglish: Newton ka do prisms waala experiment batao. Isse kya pata chala?
answer_english: Isaac Newton was the first to use a glass prism to get the spectrum of sunlight. He tried to split the colours further with a second similar prism but got no more colours. He then placed a second identical prism inverted with respect to the first. All the colours passed through it and a beam of white light emerged from the other side. This showed that sunlight is made up of seven colours.
answer_hinglish: Isaac Newton ne sabse pehle glass prism se sunlight ka spectrum paaya. Unhone ek aur waise hi prism se rangon ko aur baantne ki koshish ki par aur rang nahi mile. Phir unhone doosra identical prism pehle ke ulta rakha. Saare rang usse guzre aur doosri taraf white light ki beam nikli. Isse pata chala ki sunlight saat rangon se bani hai.
ncert_context: Isaac Newton was the first to use a glass prism to obtain the spectrum of sunlight. He tried to split the colours of the spectrum of white light further by using another similar prism. However, he could not get any more colours. He then placed a second identical prism in an inverted position with respect to the first prism. This allowed all the colours of the spectrum to pass through the second prism. He found a beam of white light emerging from the other side of the second prism. This observation gave Newton the idea that the sunlight is made up of seven colours. Any light that gives a spectrum similar to that of sunlight is often referred to as white light.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: How is a rainbow formed? In which direction is it seen?
question_hinglish: Rainbow kaise banta hai? Ye kis disha mein dikhta hai?
answer_english: A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky after a rain shower. Tiny water droplets in the atmosphere act like small prisms: they refract and disperse the incident sunlight, reflect it internally, and refract it again as it comes out of the raindrop. Due to dispersion and internal reflection, different colours reach the observer's eye. A rainbow always forms in the direction opposite to the Sun, so it is seen with the Sun behind you.
answer_hinglish: Rainbow baarish ke baad aasmaan mein dikhne waala natural spectrum hai. Hawa mein maujood paani ki chhoti boondein chhote prisms ki tarah kaam karti hain: ye sunlight ko refract aur disperse karti hain, andar reflect karti hain, aur boond se nikalte waqt phir refract karti hain. Dispersion aur internal reflection ki wajah se alag rang dekhne waale ki aankh tak pahunchte hain. Rainbow hamesha Sun ki ulti disha mein banta hai, isliye Sun aapke peechhe ho tab dikhta hai.
ncert_context: A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky after a rain shower. It is caused by dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets, present in the atmosphere. A rainbow is always formed in a direction opposite to that of the Sun. The water droplets act like small prisms. They refract and disperse the incident sunlight, then reflect it internally, and finally refract it again when it comes out of the raindrop. Due to the dispersion of light and internal reflection, different colours reach the observer's eye. You can also see a rainbow on a sunny day when you look at the sky through a waterfall or through a water fountain, with the Sun behind you.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Why do objects seen through hot air rising above a fire appear to waver or flicker?
question_hinglish: Aag ke upar uthti garam hawa ke paar dekhi gayi cheezein hilti ya timtimaati kyun lagti hain?
answer_english: The air just above the fire is hotter than the air further up. Hotter air is lighter (less dense) and has a slightly lower refractive index than the cooler air above it. Since the physical conditions of this refracting medium keep changing, the apparent position of the object seen through the hot air fluctuates. This is atmospheric refraction on a small scale.
answer_hinglish: Aag ke theek upar ki hawa upar ki hawa se zyada garam hoti hai. Garam hawa halki (kam dense) hoti hai aur iska refractive index upar ki thandi hawa se thoda kam hota hai. Is refracting medium ki physical conditions lagaataar badalti rehti hain, isliye garam hawa ke paar dikhne waali cheez ki apparent position hilti rehti hai. Ye chhote level pe atmospheric refraction hai.
ncert_context: You might have observed the apparent random wavering or flickering of objects seen through a turbulent stream of hot air rising above a fire or a radiator. The air just above the fire becomes hotter than the air further up. The hotter air is lighter (less dense) than the cooler air above it, and has a refractive index slightly less than that of the cooler air. Since the physical conditions of the refracting medium (air) are not stationary, the apparent position of the object, as seen through the hot air, fluctuates. This wavering is thus an effect of atmospheric refraction (refraction of light by the earth's atmosphere) on a small scale in our local environment.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: Why do stars twinkle?
question_hinglish: Taare kyun timtimaate hain?
answer_english: Starlight undergoes continuous refraction in the earth's atmosphere, whose refractive index changes gradually. The atmosphere bends starlight towards the normal, so the star appears slightly higher than its actual position near the horizon. Since atmospheric conditions keep changing, this apparent position keeps changing slightly. Stars are very distant and act as point-sized sources, so the amount of starlight entering the eye flickers: the star appears brighter at one moment and fainter at another. This is twinkling.
answer_hinglish: Taaron ki light earth ke atmosphere mein lagaataar refract hoti hai, jiska refractive index dheere-dheere badalta hai. Atmosphere light ko normal ki taraf modta hai, isliye horizon ke paas taara apni asli jagah se thoda upar dikhta hai. Atmosphere ki conditions badalti rehti hain, isliye ye apparent position bhi thodi-thodi badalti rehti hai. Taare bahut door hain aur point-sized sources jaise hain, isliye aankh mein aane waali light ghatti-badhti hai: taara kabhi zyada chamakdaar, kabhi dhundhla dikhta hai. Yahi timtimaana hai.
ncert_context: The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight, on entering the earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the earth. The atmospheric refraction occurs in a medium of gradually changing refractive index. Since the atmosphere bends starlight towards the normal, the apparent position of the star is slightly different from its actual position. The star appears slightly higher (above) than its actual position when viewed near the horizon. Further, this apparent position of the star is not stationary, but keeps on changing slightly, since the physical conditions of the earth's atmosphere are not stationary. Since the stars are very distant, they approximate point-sized sources of light. As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the apparent position of the star fluctuates and the amount of starlight entering the eye flickers – the star sometimes appears brighter, and at some other time, fainter, which is the twinkling effect.

The atmospheric refraction occurs in a medium of gradually changing refractive index. Since the atmosphere bends starlight towards the normal, the apparent position of the star is slightly different from its actual position. The star appears slightly higher (above) than its actual position when viewed near the horizon. Further, this apparent position of the star is not stationary, but keeps on changing slightly, since the physical conditions of the earth's atmosphere are not stationary. Since the stars are very distant, they approximate point-sized sources of light. As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the apparent position of the star fluctuates and the amount of starlight entering the eye flickers – the star sometimes appears brighter, and at some other time, fainter, which is the twinkling effect.

question_english: Why do we see the Sun about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and about 2 minutes after actual sunset?
question_hinglish: Hum Sun ko asli sunrise se lagbhag 2 minute pehle aur asli sunset ke lagbhag 2 minute baad tak kyun dekhte hain?
answer_english: Because of atmospheric refraction. Sunlight bends as it passes through the atmosphere, so the Sun appears above the horizon even when it has not yet actually crossed it (actual sunrise) or has already gone below it (actual sunset). The time difference between the actual and apparent sunrise or sunset is about 2 minutes. The apparent flattening of the Sun's disc at sunrise and sunset is due to the same phenomenon.
answer_hinglish: Atmospheric refraction ki wajah se. Asli aur apparent sunrise ya sunset mein lagbhag 2 minute ka fark hota hai. Sunrise aur sunset pe Sun ki disc chapti dikhna bhi isi wajah se hai.

subject: Physics
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question_english: What is the Tyndall effect? Where can it be observed, and how does particle size affect the colour of scattered light?
question_hinglish: Tyndall effect kya hai? Ye kahan dikhta hai, aur particle ka size scattered light ke rang ko kaise badalta hai?
answer_english: When a beam of light strikes fine particles like smoke, tiny water droplets, dust and air molecules, its path becomes visible because the particles scatter (diffusely reflect) light towards us. This scattering of light by colloidal particles is the Tyndall effect. It is seen when a fine beam of sunlight enters a smoke-filled room through a small hole, or when sunlight passes through the canopy of a dense forest with mist. Very fine particles scatter mainly blue light; larger particles scatter longer wavelengths; large enough particles make the scattered light appear white.
answer_hinglish: Jab light ki beam dhuan, paani ki chhoti boondein, dhool aur hawa ke molecules jaise fine particles se takraati hai, toh uska raasta dikhne lagta hai kyunki particles light ko hamari taraf scatter (diffusely reflect) karte hain. Colloidal particles se light ka ye scattering Tyndall effect hai. Ye tab dikhta hai jab chhote chhed se sunlight ki patli beam dhuen bhare kamre mein aaye, ya jab dhund waale ghane jungle ki chhatri se dhoop guzre. Bahut fine particles zyaadatar blue light scatter karte hain; bade particles lambi wavelengths; aur kaafi bade particles se scattered light safed dikh sakti hai.
ncert_context: The earth's atmosphere is a heterogeneous mixture of minute particles. These particles include smoke, tiny water droplets, suspended particles of dust and molecules of air. When a beam of light strikes such fine particles, the path of the beam becomes visible. The light reaches us, after being reflected diffusely by these particles. The phenomenon of scattering of light by the colloidal particles gives rise to Tyndall effect. This phenomenon is seen when a fine beam of sunlight enters a smoke-filled room through a small hole. Tyndall effect can also be observed when sunlight passes through a canopy of a dense forest. Here, tiny water droplets in the mist scatter light. The colour of the scattered light depends on the size of the scattering particles. Very fine particles scatter mainly blue light while particles of larger size scatter light of longer wavelengths. If the size of the scattering particles is large enough, then, the scattered light may even appear white.

question_english: Why is the colour of the clear sky blue?
question_hinglish: Saaf aasmaan ka rang neela kyun hota hai?
answer_english: Air molecules and other fine particles in the atmosphere are smaller than the wavelength of visible light. They scatter light of shorter wavelengths (blue end) more effectively than longer wavelengths (red end). Red light has a wavelength about 1.8 times that of blue light. So when sunlight passes through the atmosphere, blue light is scattered much more strongly than red, and this scattered blue light enters our eyes, making the sky look blue.
answer_hinglish: Atmosphere mein hawa ke molecules aur doosre fine particles visible light ki wavelength se chhote hain. Ye chhoti wavelength (blue end) ki light ko lambi wavelength (red end) se zyada achhe se scatter karte hain. Red light ki wavelength blue se lagbhag 1.8 guna hai. Isliye sunlight atmosphere se guzarte waqt blue light red se kahin zyada scatter hoti hai, aur ye scattered blue light hamari aankhon mein aati hai, jisse aasmaan neela dikhta hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is an electric circuit? Define electric current and its SI unit.
question_hinglish: Electric circuit kya hai? Electric current aur uski SI unit ki paribhasha do.
answer_english:
A continuous and closed path of an electric current is called an electric circuit. If it breaks anywhere (e.g. the switch is off), the current stops.
Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge: the amount of charge flowing through a particular area in unit time, I = Q/t.
Its SI unit is the ampere (A). One ampere is the flow of one coulomb of charge per second: 1 A = 1 C/1 s.
answer_hinglish:
Electric current ka lagaataar aur band raasta electric circuit kehlaata hai. Ye kahin bhi toot jaaye (jaise switch off ho), toh current ruk jaata hai.
Electric current charge ke behne ki dar hai: unit time mein kisi area se guzarne waala charge, I = Q/t.
Iski SI unit ampere (A) hai. Ek ampere matlab ek second mein ek coulomb charge ka behna: 1 A = 1 C/1 s.
ncert_context: A switch makes a conducting link between the cell and the bulb. A continuous and closed path of an electric current is called an electric circuit. Now, if the circuit is broken anywhere (or the switch of the torch is turned off), the current stops flowing and the bulb does not glow. Electric current is expressed by the amount of charge flowing through a particular area in unit time. In other words, it is the rate of flow of electric charges. If a net charge Q, flows across any cross-section of a conductor in time t, then the current I, through the cross-section is I = Q/t. The electric current is expressed by a unit called ampere (A), named after the French scientist, Andre-Marie Ampere. One ampere is constituted by the flow of one coulomb of charge per second, that is, 1 A = 1 C/1 s.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why is the conventional direction of electric current opposite to the direction of flow of electrons?
question_hinglish: Electric current ki conventional direction electrons ke behne ki direction ke ulti kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: In metallic wires, electrons constitute the flow of charge. But electrons were not known when electricity was first observed, so current was considered to be a flow of positive charges, and the direction of flow of positive charges was taken as the direction of current. Electrons are negative charges, so conventionally the current direction is opposite to their flow: from the positive terminal of the cell to the negative terminal through the circuit.

Electrons negative hain, isliye convention se current ki direction unke behaav ke ulti hoti hai: circuit mein cell ke positive terminal se negative terminal ki taraf.

subject: Physics
question_english: A current of 0.5 A is drawn by the filament of an electric bulb for 10 minutes. Find the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit.
question_hinglish: Bulb ka filament 10 minute tak 0.5 A current leta hai. Circuit se kitna electric charge guzarta hai?
answer_english:
Given: I = 0.5 A, t = 10 min = 600 s
Formula: I = Q/t, so Q = I × t
Q = 0.5 A × 600 s = 300 C
Answer: 300 coulomb of charge flows.

subject: Physics
question_english: What makes electric charge flow in a conductor? Explain using the water-flow analogy.
question_hinglish: Conductor mein electric charge ko behne ke liye kya majboor karta hai? Paani ke behaav ki misaal se samjhao.
answer_english: Water in a perfectly horizontal tube does not flow by itself; it flows only when there is a pressure difference, e.g. when one end is connected to a tank at a higher level. Similarly, charges in a copper wire do not flow by themselves. Electrons move only if there is a difference of electric pressure, called potential difference, along the conductor. A battery produces it: chemical action in the cell creates a potential difference across its terminals, which sets charges in motion. To maintain the current, the cell spends its stored chemical energy.
answer_hinglish: Bilkul horizontal tube mein paani apne aap nahi behta; ye tabhi behta hai jab pressure difference ho, jaise ek sira oonchi tank se juda ho. Isi tarah copper wire mein charges apne aap nahi behte. Electrons tabhi chalte hain jab conductor ke along electric pressure ka fark ho, jise potential difference kehte hain. Battery ise banaati hai: cell ke andar chemical action terminals ke beech potential difference banata hai, jo charges ko chala deta hai. Current banaaye rakhne ke liye cell apni stored chemical energy kharch karta hai.
ncert_context: What makes the electric charge to flow? Let us consider the analogy of flow of water. Charges do not flow in a copper wire by themselves, just as water in a perfectly horizontal tube does not flow. If one end of the tube is connected to a tank of water kept at a higher level, such that there is a pressure difference between the two ends of the tube, water flows out of the other end of the tube. For flow of charges in a conducting metallic wire, the gravity, of course, has no role to play; the electrons move only if there is a difference of electric pressure – called the potential difference – along the conductor. This difference of potential may be produced by a battery, consisting of one or more electric cells. The chemical action within a cell generates the potential difference across the terminals of the cell. In order to maintain the current in a given electric circuit, the cell has to expend its chemical energy stored in it.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define electric potential difference and the volt. What is meant by saying the potential difference between two points is 1 V?
question_hinglish: Electric potential difference aur volt ki paribhasha do. Do points ke beech 1 V potential difference ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english:
Potential difference between two points in a current-carrying circuit is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to the other: V = W/Q.
Its SI unit is the volt (V). 1 V = 1 J/1 C.
A potential difference of 1 V means 1 joule of work is done to move a charge of 1 coulomb from one point to the other.

Current waale circuit mein do points ke beech potential difference, ek unit charge ko ek point se doosre tak le jaane mein kiya gaya work hai: V = W/Q.
Iski SI unit volt (V) hai. 1 V = 1 J/1 C.
1 V potential difference ka matlab 1 coulomb charge ko ek point se doosre tak le jaane mein 1 joule work hota hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: How much work is done in moving a charge of 2 C across two points having a potential difference of 12 V? Also, how much energy is given to each coulomb of charge passing through a 6 V battery?
question_hinglish: 12 V potential difference waale do points ke beech 2 C charge le jaane mein kitna work hota hai? Saath hi, 6 V battery se guzarne waale har coulomb ko kitni energy milti hai?
answer_english:
Part 1: Given Q = 2 C, V = 12 V
W = V × Q = 12 V × 2 C = 24 J
Part 2: V = W/Q, so for Q = 1 C, W = 6 V × 1 C = 6 J
Answer: 24 J of work; each coulomb gets 6 J of energy from the 6 V battery.

Pehla hissa: Diya hai Q = 2 C, V = 12 V

Jawab: 24 J work; 6 V battery har coulomb ko 6 J energy deti hai.

Solution: The amount of charge Q, that flows between two points at potential difference V (= 12 V) is 2 C. Thus, the amount of work W, done in moving the charge is W = VQ = 12 V × 2 C = 24 J. question_english: What does an electric circuit comprise? List the components whose symbols are given in Table 11.1.

subject: Physics
question_english: State Ohm's law. What is resistance and what is its SI unit?
question_hinglish: Ohm's law batao. Resistance kya hai aur iski SI unit kya hai?
answer_english:
Ohm's law: the potential difference V across the ends of a given metallic wire is directly proportional to the current I through it, provided its temperature remains the same. V ∝ I, so V/I = constant = R, or V = IR.
R is the resistance: the property of a conductor to resist the flow of charges through it. Its SI unit is the ohm (Ω). 1 Ω = 1 V/1 A, i.e. a conductor has 1 Ω resistance if 1 A flows through it when the potential difference across it is 1 V.
answer_hinglish:
Ohm's law: kisi metal wire ke siron ke beech potential difference V usme behne waale current I ke seedhe anupaati hota hai, bashart temperature same rahe. V ∝ I, toh V/I = constant = R, yaani V = IR.
R resistance hai: conductor ki woh property jo charges ke behaav ko rokti hai. Iski SI unit ohm (Ω) hai. 1 Ω = 1 V/1 A, yaani agar 1 V potential difference pe 1 A current bahe toh resistance 1 Ω hai.
ncert_context: In 1827, a German physicist Georg Simon Ohm found out the relationship between the current I, flowing in a metallic wire and the potential difference across its terminals. The potential difference, V, across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is called Ohm's law. In other words V ∝ I, or V/I = constant = R, or V = IR. R is a constant for the given metallic wire at a given temperature and is called its resistance. It is the property of a conductor to resist the flow of charges through it. Its SI unit is ohm, represented by the Greek letter Ω. If the potential difference across the two ends of a conductor is 1 V and the current through it is 1 A, then the resistance R, of the conductor is 1 Ω. That is, 1 ohm = 1 volt/1 ampere.

subject: Physics
question_english: Describe the activity used to verify Ohm's law. What does the V–I graph look like?
question_hinglish: Ohm's law verify karne ki activity batao. V–I graph kaisa dikhta hai?
answer_english: A nichrome wire XY (say 0.5 m) is connected in a circuit with an ammeter in series, a voltmeter across the wire, and first one cell of 1.5 V, then two, three and four cells. For each case the current I and potential difference V are noted and V/I is calculated. Approximately the same value of V/I is obtained each time. So the V–I graph is a straight line passing through the origin, showing V/I is constant, i.e. V ∝ I.
answer_hinglish: Nichrome wire XY (maan lo 0.5 m) ko circuit mein joda jaata hai, ammeter series mein, voltmeter wire ke across, aur pehle 1.5 V ka ek cell, phir do, teen aur chaar cells. Har baar current I aur potential difference V note karke V/I nikaala jaata hai. Har baar V/I lagbhag same aata hai. Isliye V–I graph origin se guzarne waali seedhi line hai, jo dikhata hai ki V/I constant hai, yaani V ∝ I.
ncert_context: Set up a circuit consisting of a nichrome wire XY of length, say 0.5 m, an ammeter, a voltmeter and four cells of 1.5 V each. (Nichrome is an alloy of nickel, chromium, manganese, and iron metals.) First use only one cell as the source in the circuit. Note the reading in the ammeter I, for the current and reading of the voltmeter V for the potential difference across the nichrome wire XY. Next connect two cells in the circuit and note the respective readings. Repeat the above steps using three cells and then four cells in the circuit separately. Calculate the ratio of V to I for each pair. In this Activity, you will find that approximately the same value for V/I is obtained in each case. Thus the V–I graph is a straight line that passes through the origin of the graph. Thus, V/I is a constant ratio.

subject: Physics
question_english: How much current will (a) an electric bulb with filament resistance 1200 Ω and (b) an electric heater coil with resistance 100 Ω draw from a 220 V source?
question_hinglish: 220 V source se (a) 1200 Ω filament resistance waala bulb aur (b) 100 Ω resistance waali heater coil kitna current legi?
answer_english:
Formula: I = V/R
(a) Bulb: I = 220 V/1200 Ω ≈ 0.18 A
(b) Heater: I = 220 V/100 Ω = 2.2 A
Note: from the same 220 V source, the heater draws about 12 times more current than the bulb.

subject: Physics
question_english: The potential difference across an electric heater is 60 V when it draws 4 A. What current will it draw if the potential difference is increased to 120 V?
question_hinglish: Ek electric heater 4 A current leta hai jab uske across 60 V hota hai. Potential difference 120 V karne pe woh kitna current lega?
answer_english:
Given: V = 60 V, I = 4 A
R = V/I = 60 V/4 A = 15 Ω
New current: I = V/R = 120 V/15 Ω = 8 A
Answer: The heater draws 8 A (doubling V doubles I, as R is constant).
answer_hinglish:
Diya hai: V = 60 V, I = 4 A
R = V/I = 60 V/4 A = 15 Ω

question_english: For a resistor, the current I and potential difference V are: I = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 A and V = 1.6, 3.4, 6.7, 10.2, 13.2 V. Find the resistance from the V–I graph.

question_english: The resistance of a component stays constant while the potential difference across it is halved. What happens to the current? What if the resistance is doubled at the same voltage?

subject: Physics
question_english: On what factors does the resistance of a conductor depend? Describe the observations that show this.
question_hinglish: Conductor ka resistance kin factors pe nirbhar karta hai? Ye dikhaane waale observations batao.
answer_english:
Resistance depends on (i) the length of the conductor, (ii) its area of cross-section, and (iii) the nature of its material.
Observations with a nichrome wire in a circuit: when its length is doubled, the ammeter reading falls to half (resistance doubles); a thicker wire of the same material and length gives a larger current (lower resistance); a wire of a different material (copper) of the same length and thickness gives a different current.
Resistance of a uniform metallic conductor: R ∝ l and R ∝ 1/A, so R = ρl/A.
answer_hinglish:
Resistance (i) conductor ki lambaai, (ii) uske cross-section ke area, aur (iii) uske material ki nature pe nirbhar karta hai.
Circuit mein nichrome wire ke observations: lambaai double karne pe ammeter reading aadhi (resistance double); same material aur lambaai ki moti wire se zyada current (kam resistance); same lambaai aur motaai ki doosre material (copper) ki wire se alag current.
Uniform metal conductor ke liye: R ∝ l aur R ∝ 1/A, toh R = ρl/A.
ncert_context: It is observed that the ammeter reading decreases to one-half when the length of the wire is doubled. The ammeter reading is increased when a thicker wire of the same material and of the same length is used in the circuit. A change in ammeter reading is observed when a wire of different material of the same length and the same area of cross-section is used. On applying Ohm's law, we observe that the resistance of the conductor depends (i) on its length, (ii) on its area of cross-section, and (iii) on the nature of its material. Precise measurements have shown that resistance of a uniform metallic conductor is directly proportional to its length (l) and inversely proportional to the area of cross-section (A). That is, R ∝ l and R ∝ 1/A. Combining these we get R = ρ l/A.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is electrical resistivity? Give its SI unit and typical values for conductors and insulators.
question_hinglish: Electrical resistivity kya hai? Iski SI unit aur conductors aur insulators ki typical values batao.
answer_english:
In R = ρl/A, the constant of proportionality ρ (rho) is the electrical resistivity of the material. It is a characteristic property of the material. Its SI unit is Ω m.
Metals and alloys have very low resistivity, about 10⁻⁸ Ω m to 10⁻⁶ Ω m, so they are good conductors. Insulators like rubber and glass have resistivity of the order of 10¹² to 10¹⁷ Ω m. Both resistance and resistivity vary with temperature.
answer_hinglish:
R = ρl/A mein anupaat ka constant ρ (rho) material ki electrical resistivity hai. Ye material ki khaas property hai. Iski SI unit Ω m hai.
Metals aur alloys ki resistivity bahut kam hoti hai, lagbhag 10⁻⁸ Ω m se 10⁻⁶ Ω m, isliye ye achhe conductors hain. Rubber aur glass jaise insulators ki resistivity 10¹² se 10¹⁷ Ω m ke order ki hoti hai. Resistance aur resistivity dono temperature ke saath badalte hain.

question_english: A copper wire has diameter 0.5 mm and resistivity 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. What length of this wire gives a resistance of 10 Ω? How does the resistance change if the diameter is doubled?
question_hinglish: Copper wire ka diameter 0.5 mm aur resistivity 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m hai. 10 Ω resistance ke liye wire kitni lambi honi chahiye? Diameter double karne pe resistance kaise badlega?
answer_english:
Given: d = 0.5 mm = 5 × 10⁻⁴ m, ρ = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m, R = 10 Ω
A = πd²/4 = 3.14 × (5 × 10⁻⁴)²/4 ≈ 1.96 × 10⁻⁷ m²
l = RA/ρ = 10 × 1.96 × 10⁻⁷ / (1.6 × 10⁻⁸) ≈ 122.7 m
If d is doubled, A becomes 4 times, so R becomes 1/4: 10 Ω/4 = 2.5 Ω.
Answer: Length ≈ 122.7 m; doubling the diameter reduces the resistance to one-fourth (2.5 Ω).

subject: Physics
question_english: Why are alloys used in heating devices like electric irons and toasters, tungsten for bulb filaments, and copper and aluminium for transmission lines?
question_hinglish: Electric iron aur toaster jaise heating devices mein alloys, bulb filament mein tungsten, aur transmission lines mein copper aur aluminium kyun use hote hain?
answer_english:
Alloys: their resistivity is generally higher than that of their constituent metals, and they do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures, so they suit heating elements.
Tungsten: a strong metal with a very high melting point (3380°C), so the filament can get very hot and emit light without melting.
Copper and aluminium: they have very low resistivity, so they are good conductors and waste little energy as heat in transmission lines.
answer_hinglish:

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors connected in series.
question_hinglish: Series mein jude teen resistors ke equivalent resistance ka expression derive karo.
answer_english:
In series, the same current I flows through each resistor, and the total potential difference equals the sum of the potential differences across them: V = V₁ + V₂ + V₃.
Replace them by an equivalent resistor Rₛ with the same V and I: V = IRₛ.
By Ohm's law for each resistor: V₁ = IR₁, V₂ = IR₂, V₃ = IR₃.
So IRₛ = IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃, giving Rₛ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃.
The series resistance is greater than any individual resistance.

Har resistor pe Ohm's law: V₁ = IR₁, V₂ = IR₂, V₃ = IR₃.
Toh IRₛ = IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃, yaani Rₛ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃.
Series resistance kisi bhi akele resistance se zyada hota hai.
ncert_context: In a series combination of resistors the current is the same in every part of the circuit or the same current through each resistor. The total potential difference across a combination of resistors in series is equal to the sum of potential difference across the individual resistors. That is, V = V₁ + V₂ + V₃. Let I be the current through the circuit. It is possible to replace the three resistors joined in series by an equivalent single resistor of resistance Rₛ, such that the potential difference V across it, and the current I through the circuit remains the same. Applying the Ohm's law to the entire circuit, we have V = I Rₛ. On applying Ohm's law to the three resistors separately, V₁ = I R₁, V₂ = I R₂, V₃ = I R₃. Then I Rₛ = I R₁ + I R₂ + I R₃, or Rₛ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃. When several resistors are joined in series, the resistance of the combination equals the sum of their individual resistances, and is thus greater than any individual resistance.

subject: Physics
question_english: Derive the expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors connected in parallel.
question_hinglish: Parallel mein jude teen resistors ke equivalent resistance ka expression derive karo.
answer_english:
In parallel, the potential difference V across each resistor is the same, and the total current equals the sum of the branch currents: I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃.
For the equivalent resistance Rₚ: I = V/Rₚ.
For each resistor: I₁ = V/R₁, I₂ = V/R₂, I₃ = V/R₃.
So V/Rₚ = V/R₁ + V/R₂ + V/R₃, giving 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃.
The reciprocal of the equivalent resistance equals the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.

Equivalent resistance ka reciprocal alag-alag resistances ke reciprocals ke jod ke barabar hota hai.

question_english: An electric lamp of resistance 20 Ω and a conductor of 4 Ω are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find (a) the total resistance, (b) the current, and (c) the potential difference across the lamp and the conductor.
question_hinglish: 20 Ω resistance ka electric lamp aur 4 Ω ka conductor 6 V battery se series mein jude hain. Nikaalo (a) kul resistance, (b) current, aur (c) lamp aur conductor ke across potential difference.
answer_english:
(a) Rₛ = R₁ + R₂ = 20 Ω + 4 Ω = 24 Ω
(b) I = V/Rₛ = 6 V/24 Ω = 0.25 A
(c) Lamp: V₁ = IR₁ = 0.25 A × 20 Ω = 5 V
Conductor: V₂ = IR₂ = 0.25 A × 4 Ω = 1 V
Jaanch: 5 V + 1 V = 6 V, equal to the battery voltage.

question_english: Resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V battery. Find (a) the current through each resistor, (b) the total current, and (c) the total resistance.
question_hinglish: 5 Ω, 10 Ω aur 30 Ω ke resistors 12 V battery se parallel mein jude hain. Nikaalo (a) har resistor ka current, (b) kul current, aur (c) kul resistance.
answer_hinglish:
Parallel mein har resistor ke across V = 12 V hai.
(a) I₁ = 12/5 = 2.4 A; I₂ = 12/10 = 1.2 A; I₃ = 12/30 = 0.4 A
(b) I = 2.4 + 1.2 + 0.4 = 4 A

question_english: In a circuit, R₁ = 10 Ω and R₂ = 40 Ω are in parallel, and this is in series with a parallel group of R₃ = 30 Ω, R₄ = 20 Ω and R₅ = 60 Ω. A 12 V battery is connected. Find the total resistance and the total current.
question_hinglish: Ek circuit mein R₁ = 10 Ω aur R₂ = 40 Ω parallel mein hain, aur ye R₃ = 30 Ω, R₄ = 20 Ω aur R₅ = 60 Ω ke parallel group ke saath series mein hai. 12 V battery judi hai. Kul resistance aur kul current nikaalo.
ncert_context: Example 11.9 If R₁ = 10 Ω, R₂ = 40 Ω, R₃ = 30 Ω, R₄ = 20 Ω, R₅ = 60 Ω, and a 12 V battery is connected to the arrangement. Calculate (a) the total resistance in the circuit, and (b) the total current flowing in the circuit. Solution: Suppose we replace the parallel resistors R₁ and R₂ by an equivalent resistor of resistance R′. Similarly we replace the parallel resistors R₃, R₄ and R₅ by an equivalent single resistor of resistance R″. 1/R′ = 1/10 + 1/40 = 5/40; that is R′ = 8 Ω. 1/R″ = 1/30 + 1/20 + 1/60 = 6/60; that is, R″ = 10 Ω. Thus, the total resistance, R = R′ + R″ = 18 Ω. To calculate the current, we use Ohm's law, and get I = V/R = 12 V/18 Ω = 0.67 A.

question_english: How can three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω be connected to give a total resistance of (a) 4 Ω, (b) 1 Ω? Also, how would you connect three 6 Ω resistors to get (i) 9 Ω, (ii) 4 Ω?

(ii) 4 Ω: two 6 Ω in series (12 Ω), in parallel with the third: 12 × 6/18 = 4 Ω.
