subject: Physics
question_english: Why is a series arrangement not used for domestic circuits? What are the advantages of connecting devices in parallel?
question_hinglish: Ghar ke circuits mein series arrangement kyun nahi use hota? Devices ko parallel mein jodne ke kya fayde hain?
answer_english:
Series disadvantages: the current is the same throughout, so it is impracticable to connect a bulb and a heater in series, as they need very different currents. Also, if one component fails, the circuit breaks and none works (as with 'fairy lights', where each bulb must be tested to find the dead one).
Parallel advantages: each device gets the full voltage and the current divides according to each gadget's resistance, so devices with different resistances get the current they need. The total resistance decreases, and one device failing does not stop the others.
answer_hinglish:
Series ke nuksaan: poore circuit mein current same hota hai, isliye bulb aur heater ko series mein jodna bekaar hai, kyunki inhe bahut alag current chahiye. Saath hi ek component kharaab hone pe circuit toot jaata hai aur koi kaam nahi karta (jaise 'fairy lights' mein, jahan kharaab bulb dhoondhne ke liye har bulb check karna padta hai).
Parallel ke fayde: har device ko poora voltage milta hai aur current har gadget ke resistance ke hisaab se bant jaata hai, toh alag resistance waale devices ko zaroori current milta hai. Kul resistance ghatta hai, aur ek device kharaab hone se baaki nahi rukte.
ncert_context: We have seen that in a series circuit the current is constant throughout the electric circuit. Thus it is obviously impracticable to connect an electric bulb and an electric heater in series, because they need currents of widely different values to operate properly. Another major disadvantage of a series circuit is that when one component fails the circuit is broken and none of the components works. If you have used 'fairy lights' to decorate buildings on festivals, on marriage celebrations etc., you might have seen the electrician spending lot of time in trouble-locating and replacing the 'dead' bulb – each has to be tested to find which has fused or gone. On the other hand, a parallel circuit divides the current through the electrical gadgets. The total resistance in a parallel circuit is decreased. This is helpful particularly when each gadget has different resistance and requires different current to operate properly.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is the heating effect of electric current? Derive Joule's law of heating.
question_hinglish: Electric current ka heating effect kya hai? Joule's law of heating derive karo.
answer_english:
A source spends energy to maintain current. Part may do useful work (like rotating fan blades), the rest raises the gadget's temperature. In a purely resistive circuit, all the source energy is dissipated as heat. This is the heating effect of electric current.
Derivation: work done moving charge Q through potential difference V is VQ. Power input P = VQ/t = VI. Energy supplied in time t = VIt, which appears as heat: H = VIt. Using V = IR: H = I²Rt. This is Joule's law of heating.
Heat is directly proportional to (i) the square of the current, (ii) the resistance, and (iii) the time the current flows.
answer_hinglish:
Current banaaye rakhne ke liye source energy kharch karta hai. Kuch hissa useful kaam mein jaata hai (jaise fan ke blades ghumaana), baaki gadget ka temperature badhaata hai. Sirf resistors waale circuit mein saari energy garmi ban jaati hai. Ye electric current ka heating effect hai.
Derivation: charge Q ko potential difference V se le jaane ka work VQ hai. Power P = VQ/t = VI. Time t mein di gayi energy = VIt, jo garmi banti hai: H = VIt. V = IR lagaane pe: H = I²Rt. Ye Joule's law of heating hai.
Garmi (i) current ke square, (ii) resistance, aur (iii) current behne ke samay ke seedhe anupaati hoti hai.
ncert_context: A part of the source energy in maintaining the current may be consumed into useful work (like in rotating the blades of an electric fan). Rest of the source energy may be expended in heat to raise the temperature of gadget. If the electric circuit is purely resistive, the source energy continually gets dissipated entirely in the form of heat. This is known as the heating effect of electric current. Consider a current I flowing through a resistor of resistance R. Let the potential difference across it be V. Let t be the time during which a charge Q flows across. The work done in moving the charge Q through a potential difference V is VQ. Hence the power input to the circuit by the source is P = V Q/t = VI. The energy supplied in time t is VIt. This energy gets dissipated in the resistor as heat: H = VIt. Applying Ohm's law, we get H = I²Rt. This is known as Joule's law of heating. Heat produced is directly proportional to the square of current for a given resistance, directly proportional to resistance for a given current, and directly proportional to the time for which the current flows.

messages_english.content:
Context:
A part of the source energy in maintaining the current may be consumed into useful work (like in rotating the blades of an electric fan). Rest of the source energy may be expended in heat to raise the temperature of gadget. If the electric circuit is purely resistive, the source energy continually gets dissipated entirely in the form of heat. This is known as the heating effect of electric current. Consider a current I flowing through a resistor of resistance R. Let the potential difference across it be V. Let t be the time during which a charge Q flows across. The work done in moving the charge Q through a potential difference V is VQ. Hence the power input to the circuit by the source is P = V Q/t = VI. The energy supplied in time t is VIt. This energy gets dissipated in the resistor as heat: H = VIt. Applying Ohm's law, we get H = I²Rt. This is known as Joule's law of heating. Heat produced is directly proportional to the square of current for a given resistance, directly proportional to resistance for a given current, and directly proportional to the time for which the current flows.

question_english: Why does the cord of an electric heater not glow while the heating element does?
question_hinglish: Electric heater ki cord kyun nahi chamakti jabki heating element chamakta hai?
answer_english: The same current flows through the cord and the heating element, which are in series. By Joule's law, H = I²Rt, so for the same current the heat produced is proportional to resistance. The cord is made of copper with very low resistance, so it produces little heat. subject: Physics
question_english: What is an electric fuse and how does it protect a circuit? What fuse should be used for a 1 kW iron on 220 V?
question_hinglish: Electric fuse kya hai aur circuit ko kaise bachaata hai? 220 V pe 1 kW iron ke liye kaun sa fuse lagana chahiye?
answer_english:
A fuse protects circuits and appliances by stopping any unduly high current. It is placed in series with the device and is a piece of wire of a metal or alloy of appropriate melting point (e.g. aluminium, copper, iron, lead), usually in a porcelain cartridge with metal ends. If the current exceeds the specified value, the fuse wire heats up, melts and breaks the circuit. Domestic fuses are rated 1 A, 2 A, 3 A, 5 A, 10 A, etc.
For a 1 kW iron at 220 V: I = 1000/220 ≈ 4.54 A, so a 5 A fuse must be used.

Fuse zaroorat se zyada current ko rokkar circuits aur appliances ko bachaata hai. Ye device ke saath series mein lagta hai aur sahi melting point waali metal ya alloy (jaise aluminium, copper, iron, lead) ki wire hota hai, aksar metal siron waale porcelain cartridge mein. Current tay value se zyada ho toh fuse wire garam hokar pighal jaati hai aur circuit tod deti hai. Ghar ke fuse 1 A, 2 A, 3 A, 5 A, 10 A aadi rating ke hote hain.
220 V pe 1 kW iron: I = 1000/220 ≈ 4.54 A, isliye 5 A ka fuse lagana chahiye.

subject: Physics
question_english: Define electric power and give its formulas. What is 1 watt? What is the commercial unit of electrical energy?
question_hinglish: Electric power ki paribhasha aur formulas do. 1 watt kya hai? Electrical energy ki commercial unit kya hai?
answer_english:
Electric power is the rate at which electric energy is consumed or dissipated in a circuit: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
SI unit: watt (W). 1 W is the power consumed by a device carrying 1 A at a potential difference of 1 V: 1 W = 1 V × 1 A.
The watt is small, so the kilowatt (1 kW = 1000 W) is used. Energy = power × time, so its unit is watt hour (W h). The commercial unit is the kilowatt hour (kW h), called a 'unit': 1 kW h = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
answer_hinglish:
Electric power woh dar hai jisse circuit mein electric energy kharch hoti hai: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
SI unit: watt (W). 1 W us device ki power hai jo 1 V potential difference pe 1 A current leta hai: 1 W = 1 V × 1 A.
Watt chhoti unit hai, isliye kilowatt (1 kW = 1000 W) use hota hai. Energy = power × time, toh iski unit watt hour (W h) hai. Commercial unit kilowatt hour (kW h) hai, jise 'unit' kehte hain: 1 kW h = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
ncert_context: The rate of doing work is power. This is also the rate of consumption of energy. Equation (11.21) gives the rate at which electric energy is dissipated or consumed in an electric circuit. This is also termed as electric power. The power P is given by P = VI, or P = I²R = V²/R. The SI unit of electric power is watt (W). It is the power consumed by a device that carries 1 A of current when operated at a potential difference of 1 V. Thus, 1 W = 1 volt × 1 ampere = 1 V A. The unit 'watt' is very small. Therefore, in actual practice we use a much larger unit called 'kilowatt'. It is equal to 1000 watts. Since electrical energy is the product of power and time, the unit of electric energy is, therefore, watt hour (W h). The commercial unit of electric energy is kilowatt hour (kW h), commonly known as 'unit'. 1 kW h = 1000 watt × 3600 second = 3.6 × 10⁶ watt second = 3.6 × 10⁶ joule (J).

question_english: Compare the power used in the 2 Ω resistor in: (i) a 6 V battery in series with 1 Ω and 2 Ω resistors, and (ii) a 4 V battery in parallel with 12 Ω and 2 Ω resistors.

(ii) In parallel, V across 2 Ω = 4 V
P = V²/R = (4)²/2 = 8 W
Answer: The power in the 2 Ω resistor is the same, 8 W, in both circuits.

question_english: What did Hans Christian Oersted discover and why is it important?
question_hinglish: Hans Christian Oersted ne kya khoja aur ye kyun mahatvapoorn hai?

question_english: What is a magnetic field? What do the north and south poles of a compass needle mean?
question_hinglish: Magnetic field kya hai? Compass needle ke north aur south pole ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english:
The region surrounding a magnet in which the force of the magnet can be detected is called a magnetic field. It has both direction and magnitude.
A compass needle is a small bar magnet. The end pointing towards north is the north-seeking or north pole; the end pointing towards south is the south-seeking or south pole. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
answer_hinglish:
Magnet ke aas-paas ka woh area jahan magnet ka force mehsoos kiya ja sake, magnetic field kehlaata hai. Iski direction aur magnitude dono hoti hain.
Compass needle ek chhota bar magnet hai. North ki taraf waala sira north-seeking ya north pole, aur south ki taraf waala south-seeking ya south pole hai. Same poles ek doosre ko door dhakelte hain aur ulte poles kheenchte hain.

question_english: Why does a compass needle get deflected when brought near a bar magnet? Why do iron filings sprinkled around a bar magnet form a pattern?
question_hinglish: Bar magnet ke paas laane pe compass needle kyun ghoomti hai? Bar magnet ke aas-paas chhidke iron filings pattern kyun banaate hain?
answer_english:
A compass needle is itself a small magnet. The bar magnet exerts a force in the region around it (its magnetic field), and this force acts on the poles of the needle, deflecting it.
Iron filings around the magnet also experience this force, which makes them arrange themselves along the magnetic field lines, forming a pattern.
answer_hinglish:
Compass needle khud ek chhota magnet hai. Bar magnet apne aas-paas ke area (magnetic field) mein force lagaata hai, jo needle ke poles pe lagkar use ghuma deta hai.
Magnet ke aas-paas ke iron filings bhi ye force mehsoos karte hain, jisse ve magnetic field lines ke along lagkar pattern bana lete hain.

The magnet exerts its influence in the region surrounding it. Therefore the iron filings experience a force. The force thus exerted makes iron filings to arrange in a pattern. The region surrounding a magnet, in which the force of the magnet can be detected, is said to have a magnetic field. The lines along which the iron filings align themselves represent magnetic field lines.

subject: Physics
question_english: List the properties of magnetic field lines.
question_hinglish: Magnetic field lines ki properties batao.
answer_english:
1. Outside a magnet, field lines emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole; inside the magnet, they go from the south pole to the north pole. So they are closed curves.
2. The direction of the field at a point is the direction in which a north pole of a compass needle moves there.
3. The relative strength of the field is shown by how close the lines are: the field is stronger where the lines are crowded.
4. No two field lines cross each other.
answer_hinglish:
1. Magnet ke bahar field lines north pole se nikalti hain aur south pole pe milti hain; magnet ke andar south pole se north pole jaati hain. Isliye ye closed curves hain.
2. Kisi point pe field ki direction woh hai jidhar compass needle ka north pole wahan chalta hai.
3. Field ki relative strength lines ki nazdeeki se dikhti hai: jahan lines ghani hon wahan field zyada strong.
4. Koi do field lines ek doosre ko kaatti nahi.
ncert_context: Magnetic field is a quantity that has both direction and magnitude. The direction of the magnetic field is taken to be the direction in which a north pole of the compass needle moves inside it. Therefore it is taken by convention that the field lines emerge from north pole and merge at the south pole. Inside the magnet, the direction of field lines is from its south pole to its north pole. Thus the magnetic field lines are closed curves. The relative strength of the magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of the field lines. The field is stronger, that is, the force acting on the pole of another magnet placed is greater where the field lines are crowded. No two field-lines are found to cross each other.

question_english: Why don't two magnetic field lines intersect each other?
question_hinglish: Do magnetic field lines ek doosre ko kyun nahi kaatti?
answer_english: If two field lines crossed, then at the point of intersection the compass needle would have to point in two directions at once. This is not possible, since the magnetic field at a point has only one direction. So no two field lines cross.
answer_hinglish: Agar do field lines kaatti, toh kaatne waale point pe compass needle ko ek saath do directions mein point karna padta. Ye namumkin hai, kyunki ek point pe magnetic field ki sirf ek direction hoti hai. Isliye koi do field lines nahi kaatti.

subject: Physics
question_english: Describe the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor. How does it depend on the current and the distance from the wire?
question_hinglish: Seedhe current-carrying conductor ke aas-paas ki magnetic field batao. Ye current aur wire se doori pe kaise nirbhar karti hai?
answer_english:
Iron filings around a vertical current-carrying wire form concentric circles centred on the wire; these are the magnetic field lines. The direction is given by the north pole of a compass and reverses if the current is reversed.
If the current increases, the compass deflection at a point increases, so the field is stronger with more current.
If the compass is moved farther from the wire at the same current, the deflection decreases, so the field weakens with distance. The concentric circles become larger as we move away.
answer_hinglish:
Khadi current waali wire ke aas-paas iron filings wire pe centred concentric circles banaate hain; yahi magnetic field lines hain. Direction compass ke north pole se milti hai aur current ulta karne pe ulti ho jaati hai.
Current badhaane pe kisi point pe compass ka ghoomna badhta hai, yaani zyada current se field zyada strong.
Same current pe compass ko wire se door le jaane pe ghoomna ghatta hai, yaani doori ke saath field kamzor hoti hai. Door jaane pe concentric circles bade hote jaate hain.
ncert_context: You would find that the iron filings align themselves showing a pattern of concentric circles around the copper wire. What do these concentric circles represent? They represent the magnetic field lines. The direction of the north pole of the compass needle would give the direction of the field lines produced by the electric current through the straight wire. If the current is increased, the deflection also increases. It indicates that the magnitude of the magnetic field produced at a given point increases as the current through the wire increases. Now place the compass at a farther point from the conducting wire. We see that the deflection in the needle decreases. Thus the magnetic field produced by a given current in the conductor decreases as the distance from it increases. The concentric circles representing the magnetic field around a current-carrying straight wire become larger and larger as we move away from it.

subject: Physics
question_english: A straight wire placed over a compass carries current from north to south. Which way does the north pole of the needle move? What if the current is reversed?
question_hinglish: Compass ke upar rakhi seedhi wire mein current north se south behta hai. Needle ka north pole kidhar jaata hai? Current ulta karne pe kya hoga?
answer_english: With current from north to south, the north pole of the compass needle moves towards the east. When the current is reversed (south to north), the needle moves the opposite way, towards the west. This shows that reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field.
answer_hinglish: Current north se south ho toh compass needle ka north pole east ki taraf jaata hai. Current ulta (south se north) karne pe needle ulti taraf, west ki taraf jaati hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki current ulta karne se magnetic field ki direction bhi ulti ho jaati hai.
ncert_context: Take a long straight copper wire, two or three cells of 1.5 V each, and a plug key. Connect all of them in series. Place the straight wire parallel to and over a compass needle. Plug the key in the circuit. Observe the direction of deflection of the north pole of the needle. If the current flows from north to south, the north pole of the compass needle would move towards the east. Replace the cell connections in the circuit. This would result in the change of the direction of current through the copper wire, that is, from south to north. You will see that now the needle moves in opposite direction, that is, towards the west. It means that the direction of magnetic field produced by the electric current is also reversed.

subject: Physics
question_english: Current through a horizontal power line flows from east to west. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point directly below it and directly above it?
question_hinglish: Horizontal power line mein current east se west behta hai. Uske theek neeche aur theek upar ke point pe magnetic field ki direction kya hai?
answer_english: By the right-hand thumb rule (thumb pointing west), the field lines circle the wire clockwise when viewed from the east end, and anti-clockwise when viewed from the west end, in a plane perpendicular to the wire. So at a point directly below the wire the field points from north to south, and at a point directly above it the field points from south to north.
answer_hinglish: Right-hand thumb rule se (angootha west ki taraf), wire ke perpendicular plane mein field lines east sire se dekhne pe clockwise aur west sire se dekhne pe anti-clockwise ghoomti hain. Isliye wire ke theek neeche field north se south ki taraf, aur theek upar south se north ki taraf hoti hai.
ncert_context: Imagine that you are holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand such that the thumb points towards the direction of current. Then your fingers will wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field. This is known as the right-hand thumb rule. Example 12.1 A current through a horizontal power line flows in east to west direction. What is the direction of magnetic field at a point directly below it and at a point directly above it? Solution: The current is in the east-west direction. Applying the right-hand thumb rule, we get that the magnetic field (at any point below or above the wire) turns clockwise in a plane perpendicular to the wire, when viewed from the east end, and anti-clockwise, when viewed from the west end.

answer_english:
At every point of the loop, the field forms concentric circles that grow larger away from the wire. At the centre of the loop, the arcs of these big circles look like straight lines. By the right-hand rule, every section of the wire contributes field lines in the same direction inside the loop.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is a solenoid? Describe the magnetic field of a current-carrying solenoid.
question_hinglish: Solenoid kya hai? Current waale solenoid ki magnetic field batao.
answer_english:
A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder is called a solenoid.
Its field pattern is similar to that of a bar magnet: one end behaves as a magnetic north pole and the other as a south pole. Inside the solenoid, the field lines are parallel straight lines, which means the magnetic field is the same at all points inside, i.e. uniform.
answer_hinglish:
Insulated copper wire ke bahut saare gol turns ko cylinder ke shape mein paas-paas lapetne se bani coil solenoid kehlaati hai.
Iski field ka pattern bar magnet jaisa hota hai: ek sira magnetic north pole aur doosra south pole ki tarah behave karta hai. Solenoid ke andar field lines parallel seedhi lines hoti hain, yaani andar har point pe magnetic field same, matlab uniform hoti hai.
ncert_context: A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder is called a solenoid. Compare the pattern of the field with the magnetic field around a bar magnet. Do they look similar? Yes, they are similar. In fact, one end of the solenoid behaves as a magnetic north pole, while the other behaves as the south pole. The field lines inside the solenoid are in the form of parallel straight lines. This indicates that the magnetic field is the same at all points inside the solenoid. That is, the field is uniform inside the solenoid.

subject: Physics
question_english: Describe the activity showing that a current-carrying conductor experiences a force in a magnetic field. What does it show?
question_hinglish: Current waale conductor pe magnetic field mein force lagta hai, ye dikhaane waali activity batao. Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer_english:
A 5 cm aluminium rod AB is suspended horizontally between the poles of a strong horse-shoe magnet, with the field directed upwards. When current passes from B to A, the rod is displaced to the left; reversing the current displaces it to the right. Interchanging the magnet's poles also reverses the force.
This shows that a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force, and its direction depends on both the direction of the current and the direction of the field. Ampere had suggested that the magnet exerts an equal and opposite force on the conductor.
answer_hinglish:

subject: Physics
question_english: State Fleming's left-hand rule. When is the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field the largest?
question_hinglish: Fleming's left-hand rule batao. Magnetic field mein current waale conductor pe force sabse zyada kab hota hai?
answer_english:
Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of motion or force on the conductor.
The force is largest when the direction of current is at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field.
answer_hinglish:
Fleming's left-hand rule: left hand ka angootha, forefinger aur middle finger aise failaao ki teeno ek doosre ke perpendicular hon. Agar forefinger magnetic field ki direction aur middle finger current ki direction mein ho, toh angootha conductor pe lagne waale force ya motion ki direction batata hai.
Force sabse zyada tab hota hai jab current ki direction magnetic field ke right angle pe ho.
ncert_context: Experiments have shown that the displacement of the rod is largest (or the magnitude of the force is the highest) when the direction of current is at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field. In such a condition we can use a simple rule to find the direction of the force on the conductor. The force is perpendicular to both of them. The three directions can be illustrated through a simple rule, called Fleming's left-hand rule. According to this rule, stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of your left hand such that they are mutually perpendicular. If the first finger points in the direction of magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of current, then the thumb will point in the direction of motion or the force acting on the conductor.

subject: Physics
question_english:
An electron enters a magnetic field at right angles to it (in the textbook figure, the electron moves to the right and the field points upward in the page plane.) The direction of force on the electron will be
(a) to the right
(b) to the left
(c) out of the page
(d) into the page
question_hinglish:
Ek electron magnetic field mein uske right angle pe ghusta hai. (Textbook figure mein electron right ki taraf chal raha hai aur field page ke plane mein upar ki taraf hai.) Electron pe force ki direction hogi
(a) right ki taraf
(b) left ki taraf
(c) page se bahar
(d) page ke andar
answer_english: (d) into the page. By Fleming's left-hand rule, the force is perpendicular to both the field and the current. The direction of current is opposite to the motion of electrons, which gives a force directed into the page.
answer_hinglish: (d) page ke andar. Fleming's left-hand rule se force field aur current dono ke perpendicular hota hai. Current ki direction electrons ki chaal ke ulti maani jaati hai, jisse force page ke andar aata hai.

subject: Physics
question_english: How is magnetism useful in medicine? Which organs of the body produce significant magnetic fields?
question_hinglish: Medicine mein magnetism kaise kaam aata hai? Shareer ke kaun se organs khaas magnetic field banaate hain?
answer_english: An electric current always produces a magnetic field. Even weak ion currents along nerve cells produce magnetic fields; e.g. when we touch something, the nerve impulse to the muscles produces a temporary field, about one-billionth of the earth's magnetic field. The heart and the brain are the two main organs where the field produced is significant. The magnetic field inside the body is the basis of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), which produces images of body parts that help in medical diagnosis.
answer_hinglish: Electric current hamesha magnetic field banata hai. Nerve cells ke along chalne waale kamzor ion currents bhi magnetic field banaate hain; jaise kuch chhoone pe muscles tak jaane waala nerve impulse ek temporary field banata hai, jo earth ki magnetic field ka lagbhag ek-arabvaan hissa hai. Heart aur brain do mukhya organs hain jahan bani field khaas hoti hai. Shareer ke andar ki magnetic field Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) ka aadhaar hai, jo body parts ki images banakar diagnosis mein madad karti hai.

These fields are very weak and are about one-billionth of the earth's magnetic field. Two main organs in the human body where the magnetic field produced is significant, are the heart and the brain. The magnetic field inside the body forms the basis of obtaining the images of different body parts. This is done using a technique called Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Analysis of these images helps in medical diagnosis.

subject: Physics
question_english: Describe the three wires in a domestic electric supply and the function of each.
question_hinglish: Ghar ki electric supply ke teen wires aur har ek ka kaam batao.
answer_english:
Live wire: red insulation, also called positive.
Neutral wire: black insulation, also called negative. The potential difference between live and neutral is 220 V in India.
Earth wire: green insulation, connected to a metal plate deep in the earth near the house. It is a safety measure for appliances with a metallic body.
The supply comes through mains (overhead poles or underground cables), passes through a main fuse into the electricity meter, and through the main switch to the house's line wires. Homes receive AC at 220 V and 50 Hz.

Earth wire: hara insulation, ghar ke paas zameen mein gehri metal plate se juda. Metal body waale appliances ke liye safety ka upaay hai.
Supply mains (bijli ke khambhe ya underground cable) se aati hai, main fuse se hokar electricity meter mein, aur main switch se ghar ke line wires tak jaati hai. Gharon mein 220 V aur 50 Hz ki AC milti hai.

One of the wires in this supply, usually with red insulation cover, is called live wire (or positive). Another wire, with black insulation, is called neutral wire (or negative). In our country, the potential difference between the two is 220 V. At the meter-board in the house, these wires pass into an electricity meter through a main fuse. Through the main switch they are connected to the line wires in the house. The earth wire, which has insulation of green colour, is usually connected to a metal plate deep in the earth near the house. This is used as a safety measure, especially for those appliances that have a metallic body. In our houses we receive AC electric power of 220 V with a frequency of 50 Hz.

subject: Physics
question_english: What is the function of an earth wire? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?
question_hinglish: Earth wire ka kya kaam hai? Metal waale appliances ko earth karna kyun zaroori hai?
answer_english: The earth wire (green insulation) is connected to a metal plate deep in the earth. The metallic body of appliances like an electric press, toaster, table fan or refrigerator is connected to it. It provides a low-resistance conducting path for current. If current leaks to the metal body, the earth wire keeps the body at the potential of the earth, so the user does not get a severe electric shock.
answer_hinglish: Earth wire (hara insulation) zameen mein gehri metal plate se judi hoti hai. Electric press, toaster, table fan ya fridge jaise appliances ki metal body isse jodi jaati hai. Ye current ke liye kam resistance waala raasta deti hai. Agar current metal body mein leak ho, toh earth wire body ko earth ke potential pe rakhti hai, jisse user ko zor ka electric shock nahi lagta.
ncert_context: The earth wire, which has insulation of green colour, is usually connected to a metal plate deep in the earth near the house. This is used as a safety measure, especially for those appliances that have a metallic body, for example, electric press, toaster, table fan, refrigerator, etc. The metallic body is connected to the earth wire, which provides a low-resistance conducting path for the current. Thus, it ensures that any leakage of current to the metallic body of the appliance keeps its potential to that of the earth, and the user may not get a severe electric shock.

subject: Physics
question_english: Why are domestic appliances connected in parallel? Why are two separate circuits of 15 A and 5 A used?
question_hinglish: Ghar ke appliances parallel mein kyun jode jaate hain? 15 A aur 5 A ke do alag circuits kyun use hote hain?
answer_english:
In each circuit, appliances are connected across the live and neutral wires in parallel so that each gets an equal potential difference, and each has its own ON/OFF switch.
Two circuits are used: a 15 A circuit for high-power appliances such as geysers and air coolers, and a 5 A circuit for bulbs, fans, etc.
answer_hinglish:
Har circuit mein appliances live aur neutral wires ke across parallel mein jode jaate hain taaki har ek ko barabar potential difference mile, aur har ek ka apna ON/OFF switch hota hai.
Do circuits hote hain: geyser aur air cooler jaise zyada power waale appliances ke liye 15 A ka circuit, aur bulb, fan aadi ke liye 5 A ka circuit.
ncert_context: These wires supply electricity to separate circuits within the house. Often, two separate circuits are used, one of 15 A current rating for appliances with higher power ratings such as geysers, air coolers, etc. The other circuit is of 5 A current rating for bulbs, fans, etc. In each separate circuit, different appliances can be connected across the live and neutral wires. Each appliance has a separate switch to 'ON'/'OFF' the flow of current through it. In order that each appliance has equal potential difference, they are connected parallel to each other.

subject: Physics
question_english: When does a short circuit occur? What is overloading and how does a fuse protect against it?
question_hinglish: Short circuit kab hota hai? Overloading kya hai aur fuse isse kaise bachaata hai?
answer_english:
A short circuit occurs when the live wire and the neutral wire come into direct contact, e.g. when wire insulation is damaged or an appliance is faulty. The current in the circuit then increases abruptly.
Overloading can be caused by short-circuiting, an accidental hike in supply voltage, or connecting too many appliances to a single socket.
The fuse protects by stopping the unduly high current: Joule heating melts the fuse wire, which breaks the circuit and prevents damage to the circuit and appliances.

question_english: An electric oven of 2 kW power rating is operated in a domestic circuit (220 V) that has a current rating of 5 A. What result do you expect? Explain.
question_hinglish: 2 kW power rating ka electric oven 5 A current rating waale ghar ke circuit (220 V) pe chalaaya jaata hai. Kya hoga? Samjhao.

question_english: Name two safety measures used in electric circuits and appliances. What precaution should be taken to avoid overloading of domestic circuits?
question_hinglish: Electric circuits aur appliances mein use hone waale do safety upaay batao. Ghar ke circuits ki overloading se bachne ke liye kya saavdhaani rakhni chahiye?
answer_english:

1. Electric fuse: melts and breaks the circuit when the current is unduly high (short circuit or overloading).
2. Earth wire: connects the metallic body of appliances to the earth, so leaked current does not give the user a severe shock.

question_english: True or False: (a) The field at the centre of a long circular coil carrying current will be parallel straight lines. (b) A wire with green insulation is usually the live wire of an electric supply.
question_hinglish: Sahi ya galat: (a) Current waali lambi circular coil ke centre pe field parallel seedhi lines hogi. (b) Hare insulation waali wire aam taur pe electric supply ki live wire hoti hai.
answer_english:
(a) True. At the centre of a current-carrying circular coil, the arcs of the large concentric field circles appear as straight lines, and all sections of the wire contribute in the same direction.
(b) False. The green wire is the earth wire; the live wire usually has red insulation.
answer_hinglish:
(a) Sahi. Current waali circular coil ke centre pe bade concentric field circles ke arcs seedhi lines jaise dikhte hain, aur wire ka har hissa same direction mein field deta hai.
(b) Galat. Hari wire earth wire hai; live wire ka insulation aam taur pe laal hota hai.
ncert_context: By the time we reach at the centre of the circular loop, the arcs of these big circles would appear as straight lines. Every point on the wire carrying current would give rise to the magnetic field appearing as straight lines at the center of the loop. One of the wires in this supply, usually with red insulation cover, is called live wire (or positive). Another wire, with black insulation, is called neutral wire (or negative). The earth wire, which has insulation of green colour, is usually connected to a metal plate deep in the earth near the house.

question_english: Fill in the blanks: (a) Magnetic field lines are closed curves; inside a magnet they go from the ______ pole to the ______ pole. (b) A magnet formed by placing soft iron inside a current-carrying solenoid is called an ______. (c) In India, the potential difference between live and neutral wires is ______.
question_hinglish: Khaali jagah bharo: (a) Magnetic field lines closed curves hain; magnet ke andar ye ______ pole se ______ pole jaati hain. (b) Current waale solenoid mein soft iron rakhne se bane magnet ko ______ kehte hain. (c) India mein live aur neutral wires ke beech potential difference ______ hai.
answer_english:
(a) south; north
(b) electromagnet
(c) 220 V
answer_hinglish:
(a) south se; north tak
(b) electromagnet
(c) 220 V (volt)
ncert_context: Field lines emerge from north pole and merge at the south pole. Inside the magnet, the direction of field lines is from its south pole to its north pole. Thus the magnetic field lines are closed curves. A strong magnetic field produced inside a solenoid can be used to magnetise a piece of magnetic material, like soft iron, when placed inside the coil. The magnet so formed is called an electromagnet. One of the wires in this supply, usually with red insulation cover, is called live wire. Another wire, with black insulation, is called neutral wire. In our country, the potential difference between the two is 220 V.

Question:
Khaali jagah bharo: (a) Magnetic field lines closed curves hain; magnet ke andar ye ______ pole se ______ pole jaati hain. (b) Current waale solenoid mein soft iron rakhne se bane magnet ko ______ kehte hain. (c) India mein live aur neutral wires ke beech potential difference ______ hai.

Intent Type: fill_blank
Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.

(a) south se; north tak
(b) electromagnet
(c) 220 V (volt)
